{{Shrine |name = Takagawara Shrine |religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Takagawara-jinja 02.jpg|270px]] |location = {{ill|Ise, Mie|ja|伊勢市|12=draft}}, Miyago 1-chome 3-19, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|ja|三重県|12=draft}} |latitude_deg = 34 | latitude_min = 29 | latitude_sec = 34.5 |longitude_deg = 136 | longitude_min = 42 | longitude_sec = 22.2 |map = Japan Mie |deity = {{ill|Tsukuyomi|ja|月夜見尊御魂|12=draft}} |rank = {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社|12=draft}} (small)
{{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮|1=Toyouke Daijingu|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮|12=draft}} Subordinate Shrine |founded = Before {{ill|Enryaku|ja|延暦|12=draft}} 23 (804) |main_hall = {{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|ja|神明造|12=draft}} |other_names = |pilgrimage_sites = |annual_festival = |rituals = {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭|12=draft}} }} '''Takagawara Shrine''' (高河原神社, ''Takagawara Jinja''Shikinen Sengu Memorial Sengu-kan "[http://www.sengukan.jp/wp-content/themes/sengukan/shrine/area06.php Takagawara Shrine たかがわらじんじゃ>>]" (Accessed October 8, 2013).[[iTV]] "[http://www.yoitokose.jp/ise/encyclopedia/t0010.php Takagawara Shrine | Ise Grand Shrine Encyclopedia | Ise-Shima Travel Yoitokose]" (Accessed October 8, 2013)., also pronounced ''Takakawara Jinja''Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.39Gakken Publishing (2013): p.57) is a [[Shinto]] shrine located in Miyago, {{ill|Ise, Mie|ja|伊勢市|12=draft}}, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|ja|三重県|12=draft}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|subordinate shrine (sessha/massha)|ja|摂末社|12=draft}} of {{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮|1=Toyouke Daijingu|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮|12=draft}} (the Outer Shrine of {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮|12=draft}}) and classified as a {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社|12=draft}}. It ranks 10th among the 16 subordinate shrines of the Outer ShrineUjiyamada City Hall (1929): pp.11–13.. The shrine is located within the precincts of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|ja|月夜見宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|12=draft}}, which is a separate shrine of the Outer ShrineIse Bunka-sha (2008): p.38. == Overview (概要) == Located at '''{{ill|Mie Prefecture|ja|三重県|12=draft}} {{ill|Ise, Mie|ja|伊勢市|12=draft}}''' '''1006 Miyago 1-chome'''式内社研究会 編（1990）：294ページ ('''modern address:''' '''1-3-19 Miyago, Ise City'''). The shrine is situated '''behind and to the right (northeast) of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月夜見宮|12=draft}}'s main hall'''. The shrine '''grounds are surrounded by a moat on three sides''', which is believed to be '''a remnant of a tributary of the {{ill|Miyagawa River (Mie)|ja|宮川 (三重県)|12=draft}}'''. The '''enshrined deity''' is '''{{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto no Mitama|ja|月夜見尊御魂|12=draft}} (つきよみのみことのみたま)'''. The shrine is located in '''Takagawara (高河原),''' an area near the '''Miyagawa River''', and serves as '''a {{ill|guardian deity|ja|守護神|12=draft}} (守護神) for the land development of the surrounding region'''. Many '''ancient texts''' describe the enshrined deity as the '''Mitama (spirit) of {{ill|Tsukiyomi|ja|月読|12=draft}}'''. According to the ''{{ill|Ruiju Jingi Hongen|ja|類聚神祇本源|12=draft}}'', '''reconstructions''' were '''regularly conducted from '''{{ill|Tokuji (era)|ja|徳治|12=draft}} 1 ({{ill|1306|ja|1306年|12=draft}})''' onwards, under the supervision of a special '''Zōsai-shi (造替使, shrine reconstruction official).'''Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p. 296 The ''{{ill|Ninomiya Kansa Enkaku Kō|ja|二宮管社沿革考|12=draft}}'' records that: {{quote|"According to the '''Ōei Tōkō Nikki (応永頭工日記)''', on the '''fourth day of the first month in '''{{ill|Ōei (era)|ja|応永|12=draft}} 26 ({{ill|1419|ja|1419th year|12=draft}})''', a great fire burned down '''{{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月夜見宮|12=draft}}''', its small shrine, '''Kawahara-sha (高河原社)''', and '''Imibiya-den (忌火屋殿, the sacred fire hall)'''."}} Thus, the shrine was confirmed to have '''existed until it burned down on '''{{ill|January 4 (old calendar)|ja|1月4日 (旧暦)|12=draft}}''', corresponding to '''{{ill|January 29|ja|1月29日|12=draft}}, 1419 (Julian calendar).''' --- === '''Reconstruction in the Edo Period'''=== After this '''destruction, the shrine fell into neglect''', and by the '''Early Modern Period (近世), its location was lost'''. {{Shrine |name = Takagawara Shrine |religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Takagawara-jinja 02.jpg|270px]] |location = {{ill|Ise, Mie|ja|伊勢市|12=draft}}, Miyago 1-chome 3-19, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|ja|三重県|12=draft}} |latitude_deg = 34 | latitude_min = 29 | latitude_sec = 34.5 |longitude_deg = 136 | longitude_min = 42 | longitude_sec = 22.2 |map = Japan Mie |deity = {{ill|Tsukuyomi|ja|月夜見尊御魂|12=draft}} |rank = {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社|12=draft}} (small)
{{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮|1=Toyouke Daijingu|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮|12=draft}} Subordinate Shrine |founded = Before {{ill|Enryaku|ja|延暦|12=draft}} 23 (804) |main_hall = {{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|ja|神明造|12=draft}} |other_names = |pilgrimage_sites = |annual_festival = |rituals = {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭|12=draft}} }} '''Takagawara Shrine''' (高河原神社, ''Takagawara Jinja''Shikinen Sengu Memorial Sengu-kan "[http://www.sengukan.jp/wp-content/themes/sengukan/shrine/area06.php Takagawara Shrine たかがわらじんじゃ>>]" (Accessed October 8, 2013).[[iTV]] "[http://www.yoitokose.jp/ise/encyclopedia/t0010.php Takagawara Shrine | Ise Grand Shrine Encyclopedia | Ise-Shima Travel Yoitokose]" (Accessed October 8, 2013)., also pronounced ''Takakawara Jinja''Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.39Gakken Publishing (2013): p.57) is a [[Shinto]] shrine located in Miyago, {{ill|Ise, Mie|ja|伊勢市|12=draft}}, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|ja|三重県|12=draft}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|subordinate shrine (sessha/massha)|ja|摂末社|12=draft}} of {{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮|1=Toyouke Daijingu|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮|12=draft}} (the Outer Shrine of {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮|12=draft}}) and classified as a {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社|12=draft}}. It ranks 10th among the 16 subordinate shrines of the Outer ShrineUjiyamada City Hall (1929): pp.11–13.. The shrine is located within the precincts of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|ja|月夜見宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|12=draft}}, which is a separate shrine of the Outer ShrineIse Bunka-sha (2008): p.38. == Overview (概要) == Located at '''{{ill|Mie Prefecture|ja|三重県|12=draft}} {{ill|Ise, Mie|ja|伊勢市|12=draft}}''' '''1006 Miyago 1-chome'''式内社研究会 編（1990）：294ページ ('''modern address:''' '''1-3-19 Miyago, Ise City'''). The shrine is situated '''behind and to the right (northeast) of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月夜見宮|12=draft}}'s main hall'''. The shrine '''grounds are surrounded by a moat on three sides''', which is believed to be '''a remnant of a tributary of the {{ill|Miyagawa River (Mie)|ja|宮川 (三重県)|12=draft}}'''. The '''enshrined deity''' is '''{{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto no Mitama|ja|月夜見尊御魂|12=draft}} (つきよみのみことのみたま)'''. The shrine is located in '''Takagawara (高河原),''' an area near the '''Miyagawa River''', and serves as '''a {{ill|guardian deity|ja|守護神|12=draft}} (守護神) for the land development of the surrounding region'''. Many '''ancient texts''' describe the enshrined deity as the '''Mitama (spirit) of {{ill|Tsukiyomi|ja|月読|12=draft}}'''. However, the ''{{ill|Shinmei-chō Kōshō Saikō|ja|神名帳考證再考|12=draft}}'' (''神名帳考證再考'') claims that the deity is actually '''{{ill|Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto|ja|倉稲魂命|12=draft}} (倉稲魂命)''', the '''deity of grain and prosperity'''. nother text, ''{{ill|Ninomiya Kansa Enkaku Kō|ja|二宮管社沿革考|12=draft}}'' (''二宮管社沿革考''), asserts that the '''original name of the shrine in the ''{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|12=draft}}'' (延喜式神名帳)''' was '''"{{ill|Kawahara-ni-Masu-Kuninamino-Kami Jinja|ja|川原坐国生神社|12=draft}}"''', proving that its deity is '''{{ill|Kuninamino-Kami|ja|国生神|12=draft}} (国生神), the god of land formation.'''Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): pp. 295–296 The '''main hall''' follows '''{{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|ja|神明造|12=draft}} (神明造, the {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮|12=draft}} architectural style)''' and has a '''wooden board roof ({{ill|Itabuki|ja|板葺|12=draft}})''', enclosed by a '''{{ill|Tamagaki|ja|玉垣|12=draft}} (玉垣, sacred fence)'''. Unlike most '''{{ill|Sessha|ja|摂社|12=draft}}・{{ill|Massha|ja|末社|12=draft}}・{{ill|Shokan-sha|ja|所管社|12=draft}}''' (摂社・末社・所管社, auxiliary shrines) of {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮|12=draft}}, which '''do not have an offering box ({{ill|Saisenbako|ja|賽銭箱|12=draft}})'''Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p. 26, '''Takagawara Shrine uniquely has one.''' == History (歴史) == Based on the '''definition of a {{ill|Sessha|ja|摂社|12=draft}} (auxiliary shrine) within {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮|12=draft}}''', '''this shrine was established before the compilation of the ''{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|12=draft}}'' in '''{{ill|Enchō (era)|ja|延長|12=draft}} 5 ({{ill|927|ja|927th year|12=draft}}).'''Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p. 22 * The shrine is listed in that text as '''"{{ill|Kawahara-ni-Masu-Kuninamino-Kami Jinja|ja|川原坐国生神社|12=draft}}".''' * Additionally, it is mentioned as '''"{{ill|Takagawara-sha|ja|高河原社|12=draft}}"''' in the ''{{ill|Toyuke Daijingu Gishiki-chō|ja|止由気宮儀式帳|12=draft}}''. * Since that text dates back to '''{{ill|Enryaku (era)|ja|延暦|12=draft}} 23 ({{ill|804|ja|804th year|12=draft}}),''' this confirms that '''the shrine existed before that time.''' According to the ''{{ill|Ruiju Jingi Hongen|ja|類聚神祇本源|12=draft}}'', '''reconstructions''' were '''regularly conducted from '''{{ill|Tokuji (era)|ja|徳治|12=draft}} 1 ({{ill|1306|ja|1306年|12=draft}})''' onwards, under the supervision of a special '''Zōsai-shi (造替使, shrine reconstruction official).'''Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p. 296 The ''{{ill|Ninomiya Kansa Enkaku Kō|ja|二宮管社沿革考|12=draft}}'' records that: {{quote|"According to the '''Ōei Tōkō Nikki (応永頭工日記)''', on the '''fourth day of the first month in '''{{ill|Ōei (era)|ja|応永|12=draft}} 26 ({{ill|1419|ja|1419th year|12=draft}})''', a great fire burned down '''{{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月夜見宮|12=draft}}''', its small shrine, '''Kawahara-sha (高河原社)''', and '''Imibiya-den (忌火屋殿, the sacred fire hall)'''."}} Thus, the shrine was confirmed to have '''existed until it burned down on '''{{ill|January 4 (old calendar)|ja|1月4日 (旧暦)|12=draft}}''', corresponding to '''{{ill|January 29|ja|1月29日|12=draft}}, 1419 (Julian calendar).''' --- === '''Reconstruction in the Edo Period'''=== After this '''destruction, the shrine fell into neglect''', and by the '''Early Modern Period (近世), its location was lost'''. However, thanks to the efforts of '''{{ill|Kawabe Kiyonaga|ja|河邊精長|12=draft}} (also known as {{ill|Ōnakatomi Kiyonaga|ja|大中臣精長|12=draft}}),''' the '''Grand Chief Priest ({{ill|Ōgūji|ja|大宮司|12=draft}}),''' the shrine was '''reconstructed on its present site on '''{{ill|Kanbun (era)|ja|寛文|12=draft}} 3, '''{{ill|July 7 (old calendar)|ja|7月7日 (旧暦)|12=draft}}''' (corresponding to '''{{ill|August 9|ja|8月9日|12=draft}}, {{ill|1663|ja|1663rd year|12=draft}} in the Gregorian calendar).''' * ''{{ill|Shinmei Hisho|ja|神名秘書|12=draft}}'' states: '''"Located in Numaki-go, Yamada Village. East of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月読宮|12=draft}}."''' * ''{{ill|Ruiju Jingi Hongen|ja|類聚神祇本源|12=draft}}'' states: '''"East of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月読宮|12=draft}}, within the same {{ill|Tamagaki|ja|玉垣|12=draft}} fence."''' * ''{{ill|Ninomiya Kansa Enkaku Kō|ja|二宮管社沿革考|12=draft}}'' claims that '''the original shrine site was actually the present-day '''{{ill|Suhara Taisha|ja|須原大社|12=draft}} in '''Ichinoki, Ise City.'''Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p. 295 --- === '''Reconstruction in the Modern Period'''=== * '''In {{ill|1911|ja|1911th year|12=draft}} ({{ill|Meiji|ja|明治|12=draft}} 44),''' the shrine was '''rebuilt.'''Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): p. 12 * '''In {{ill|1938|ja|1938th year|12=draft}} ({{ill|Shōwa|ja|昭和|12=draft}} 13),''' it was '''rebuilt again'''. * '''In {{ill|1957|ja|1957th year|12=draft}} (Shōwa 32),''' a '''major renovation''' was completed, and '''a sacred transfer ritual ({{ill|Sengyo|ja|遷御|12=draft}}) was performed 20 years later.'''Sakurai (1991): p. 298 --- == Rites and Festivals (祭事) == * '''February''' – {{ill|Kinen-sai (祈年祭)|ja|祈年祭|12=draft}} (Harvest Prayer Festival) * '''June & December''' – {{ill|Tsukinami-sai (月次祭)|ja|月次祭|1=Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|12=draft}} (Monthly Festival) * '''October''' – {{ill|Kannamesai (神嘗祭)|ja|神嘗祭|12=draft}} (Offering of First Fruits Festival) * '''November''' – {{ill|Niiname-sai (新嘗祭)|ja|新嘗祭|12=draft}} (Thanksgiving Harvest Festival) These '''four major rituals''' are '''conducted on-site by a Negi (禰宜, senior priest) in巡回祭典 (巡回祭,巡行 ceremony format).''' The following '''six rites are performed remotely (遥祀, Yōshi):''' * '''January''' – {{ill|Saitan-sai (歳旦祭)|ja|歳旦祭|12=draft}} (New Year's Festival) * '''January''' – {{ill|Genshi-sai (元始祭)|ja|元始祭|12=draft}} (Imperial Foundation Festival) * '''February 11''' – {{ill|Kenkoku-kinen-sai (建国記念祭)|ja|建国記念祭|12=draft}} (National Foundation Day) * '''May & August''' – {{ill|Kaze-no-Hi-no-Matsuri (風日祈祭)|ja|風日祈祭|12=draft}} (Wind and Rain Prayers) * '''December 23''' – {{ill|Tenchō-sai (天長祭)|ja|天長祭|12=draft}} (Emperor's Birthday Festival) --- == Access (交通) == [[File:Tsukiyominomiyamae Bus Stop.jpg|thumb|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya-mae Bus Stop]] '''Public Transport:''' * '''10-minute walk (550m)''' from '''{{ill|Ise City Station|ja|伊勢市駅|12=draft}} (JR & Kintetsu)'''.Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p. 33 * '''4-minute walk (360m)''' from '''Shindō Bus Stop (三重交通)'''. However, thanks to the efforts of '''{{ill|Kawabe Kiyonaga|ja|河邊精長|12=draft}} (also known as {{ill|Ōnakatomi Kiyonaga|ja|大中臣精長|12=draft}}),''' the '''Grand Chief Priest ({{ill|Ōgūji|ja|大宮司|12=draft}}),''' the shrine was '''reconstructed on its present site on '''{{ill|Kanbun (era)|ja|寛文|12=draft}} 3, '''{{ill|July 7 (old calendar)|ja|7月7日 (旧暦)|12=draft}}''' (corresponding to '''{{ill|August 9|ja|8月9日|12=draft}}, {{ill|1663|ja|1663rd year|12=draft}} in the Gregorian calendar).''' * ''{{ill|Shinmei Hisho|ja|神名秘書|12=draft}}'' states: '''"Located in Numaki-go, Yamada Village. East of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月読宮|12=draft}}."''' * ''{{ill|Ruiju Jingi Hongen|ja|類聚神祇本源|12=draft}}'' states: '''"East of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月読宮|12=draft}}, within the same {{ill|Tamagaki|ja|玉垣|12=draft}} fence."''' * ''{{ill|Ninomiya Kansa Enkaku Kō|ja|二宮管社沿革考|12=draft}}'' claims that '''the original shrine site was actually the present-day '''{{ill|Suhara Taisha|ja|須原大社|12=draft}} in '''Ichinoki, Ise City.'''Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p. 295 --- === '''Reconstruction in the Modern Period'''=== * '''In {{ill|1911|ja|1911th year|12=draft}} ({{ill|Meiji|ja|明治|12=draft}} 44),''' the shrine was '''rebuilt.'''Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): p. 12 * '''In {{ill|1938|ja|1938th year|12=draft}} ({{ill|Shōwa|ja|昭和|12=draft}} 13),''' it was '''rebuilt again'''. * '''In {{ill|1957|ja|1957th year|12=draft}} (Shōwa 32),''' a '''major renovation''' was completed, and '''a sacred transfer ritual ({{ill|Sengyo|ja|遷御|12=draft}}) was performed 20 years later.'''Sakurai (1991): p. 298 --- == Rites and Festivals (祭事) == * '''February''' – {{ill|Kinen-sai (祈年祭)|ja|祈年祭|12=draft}} (Harvest Prayer Festival) * '''June & December''' – {{ill|Tsukinami-sai (月次祭)|ja|月次祭|1=Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|12=draft}} (Monthly Festival) * '''October''' – {{ill|Kannamesai (神嘗祭)|ja|神嘗祭|12=draft}} (Offering of First Fruits Festival) * '''November''' – {{ill|Niiname-sai (新嘗祭)|ja|新嘗祭|12=draft}} (Thanksgiving Harvest Festival) These '''four major rituals''' are '''conducted on-site by a Negi (禰宜, senior priest) in巡回祭典 (巡回祭,巡行 ceremony format).''' The following '''six rites are performed remotely (遥祀, Yōshi):''' * '''January''' – {{ill|Saitan-sai (歳旦祭)|ja|歳旦祭|12=draft}} (New Year's Festival) * '''January''' – {{ill|Genshi-sai (元始祭)|ja|元始祭|12=draft}} (Imperial Foundation Festival) * '''February 11''' – {{ill|Kenkoku-kinen-sai (建国記念祭)|ja|建国記念祭|12=draft}} (National Foundation Day) * '''May & August''' – {{ill|Kaze-no-Hi-no-Matsuri (風日祈祭)|ja|風日祈祭|12=draft}} (Wind and Rain Prayers) * '''December 23''' – {{ill|Tenchō-sai (天長祭)|ja|天長祭|12=draft}} (Emperor's Birthday Festival) --- == Access (交通) == [[File:Tsukiyominomiyamae Bus Stop.jpg|thumb|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya-mae Bus Stop]] '''Public Transport:''' * '''10-minute walk (550m)''' from '''{{ill|Ise City Station|ja|伊勢市駅|12=draft}} (JR & Kintetsu)'''.Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p. 33 * '''4-minute walk (360m)''' from '''Shindō Bus Stop (三重交通)'''. {{Shrine |name = Takagawara Shrine |religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Takagawara-jinja 02.jpg|270px]] |location = {{ill|Ise, Mie|ja|伊勢市|12=draft}}, Miyago 1-chome 3-19, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|ja|三重県|12=draft}} |latitude_deg = 34 | latitude_min = 29 | latitude_sec = 34.5 |longitude_deg = 136 | longitude_min = 42 | longitude_sec = 22.2 |map = Japan Mie |deity = {{ill|Tsukuyomi|ja|月夜見尊御魂|12=draft}} |rank = {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社|12=draft}} (small)
{{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮|1=Toyouke Daijingu|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮|12=draft}} Subordinate Shrine |founded = Before {{ill|Enryaku|ja|延暦|12=draft}} 23 (804) |main_hall = {{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|ja|神明造|12=draft}} |other_names = |pilgrimage_sites = |annual_festival = |rituals = {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭|12=draft}} }} '''Takagawara Shrine''' (高河原神社, ''Takagawara Jinja''Shikinen Sengu Memorial Sengu-kan "[http://www.sengukan.jp/wp-content/themes/sengukan/shrine/area06.php Takagawara Shrine たかがわらじんじゃ>>]" (Accessed October 8, 2013).[[iTV]] "[http://www.yoitokose.jp/ise/encyclopedia/t0010.php Takagawara Shrine | Ise Grand Shrine Encyclopedia | Ise-Shima Travel Yoitokose]" (Accessed October 8, 2013)., also pronounced ''Takakawara Jinja''Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.39Gakken Publishing (2013): p.57) is a [[Shinto]] shrine located in Miyago, {{ill|Ise, Mie|ja|伊勢市|12=draft}}, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|ja|三重県|12=draft}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|subordinate shrine (sessha/massha)|ja|摂末社|12=draft}} of {{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮|1=Toyouke Daijingu|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮|12=draft}} (the Outer Shrine of {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮|12=draft}}) and classified as a {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社|12=draft}}. It ranks 10th among the 16 subordinate shrines of the Outer ShrineUjiyamada City Hall (1929): pp.11–13.. The shrine is located within the precincts of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|ja|月夜見宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|12=draft}}, which is a separate shrine of the Outer ShrineIse Bunka-sha (2008): p.38. == Overview (概要) == Located at '''{{ill|Mie Prefecture|ja|三重県|12=draft}} {{ill|Ise, Mie|ja|伊勢市|12=draft}}''' '''1006 Miyago 1-chome'''式内社研究会 編（1990）：294ページ ('''modern address:''' '''1-3-19 Miyago, Ise City'''). The shrine is situated '''behind and to the right (northeast) of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月夜見宮|12=draft}}'s main hall'''. The shrine '''grounds are surrounded by a moat on three sides''', which is believed to be '''a remnant of a tributary of the {{ill|Miyagawa River (Mie)|ja|宮川 (三重県)|12=draft}}'''. The '''enshrined deity''' is '''{{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto no Mitama|ja|月夜見尊御魂|12=draft}} (つきよみのみことのみたま)'''. The shrine is located in '''Takagawara (高河原),''' an area near the '''Miyagawa River''', and serves as '''a {{ill|guardian deity|ja|守護神|12=draft}} (守護神) for the land development of the surrounding region'''. Many '''ancient texts''' describe the enshrined deity as the '''Mitama (spirit) of {{ill|Tsukiyomi|ja|月読|12=draft}}'''. However, the ''{{ill|Shinmei-chō Kōshō Saikō|ja|神名帳考證再考|12=draft}}'' (''神名帳考證再考'') claims that the deity is actually '''{{ill|Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto|ja|倉稲魂命|12=draft}} (倉稲魂命)''', the '''deity of grain and prosperity'''. nother text, ''{{ill|Ninomiya Kansa Enkaku Kō|ja|二宮管社沿革考|12=draft}}'' (''二宮管社沿革考''), asserts that the '''original name of the shrine in the ''{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|12=draft}}'' (延喜式神名帳)''' was '''"{{ill|Kawahara-ni-Masu-Kuninamino-Kami Jinja|ja|川原坐国生神社|12=draft}}"''', proving that its deity is '''{{ill|Kuninamino-Kami|ja|国生神|12=draft}} (国生神), the god of land formation.'''Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): pp. 295–296 The '''main hall''' follows '''{{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|ja|神明造|12=draft}} (神明造, the {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮|12=draft}} architectural style)''' and has a '''wooden board roof ({{ill|Itabuki|ja|板葺|12=draft}})''', enclosed by a '''{{ill|Tamagaki|ja|玉垣|12=draft}} (玉垣, sacred fence)'''. Unlike most '''{{ill|Sessha|ja|摂社|12=draft}}・{{ill|Massha|ja|末社|12=draft}}・{{ill|Shokan-sha|ja|所管社|12=draft}}''' (摂社・末社・所管社, auxiliary shrines) of {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮|12=draft}}, which '''do not have an offering box ({{ill|Saisenbako|ja|賽銭箱|12=draft}})'''Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p. 26, '''Takagawara Shrine uniquely has one.''' == History (歴史) == Based on the '''definition of a {{ill|Sessha|ja|摂社|12=draft}} (auxiliary shrine) within {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮|12=draft}}''', '''this shrine was established before the compilation of the ''{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|12=draft}}'' in '''{{ill|Enchō (era)|ja|延長|12=draft}} 5 ({{ill|927|ja|927th year|12=draft}}).'''Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p. 22 * The shrine is listed in that text as '''"{{ill|Kawahara-ni-Masu-Kuninamino-Kami Jinja|ja|川原坐国生神社|12=draft}}".''' * Additionally, it is mentioned as '''"{{ill|Takagawara-sha|ja|高河原社|12=draft}}"''' in the ''{{ill|Toyuke Daijingu Gishiki-chō|ja|止由気宮儀式帳|12=draft}}''. * Since that text dates back to '''{{ill|Enryaku (era)|ja|延暦|12=draft}} 23 ({{ill|804|ja|804th year|12=draft}}),''' this confirms that '''the shrine existed before that time.''' According to the ''{{ill|Ruiju Jingi Hongen|ja|類聚神祇本源|12=draft}}'', '''reconstructions''' were '''regularly conducted from '''{{ill|Tokuji (era)|ja|徳治|12=draft}} 1 ({{ill|1306|ja|1306年|12=draft}})''' onwards, under the supervision of a special '''Zōsai-shi (造替使, shrine reconstruction official).'''Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p. 296 The ''{{ill|Ninomiya Kansa Enkaku Kō|ja|二宮管社沿革考|12=draft}}'' records that: {{quote|"According to the '''Ōei Tōkō Nikki (応永頭工日記)''', on the '''fourth day of the first month in '''{{ill|Ōei (era)|ja|応永|12=draft}} 26 ({{ill|1419|ja|1419th year|12=draft}})''', a great fire burned down '''{{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月夜見宮|12=draft}}''', its small shrine, '''Kawahara-sha (高河原社)''', and '''Imibiya-den (忌火屋殿, the sacred fire hall)'''."}} Thus, the shrine was confirmed to have '''existed until it burned down on '''{{ill|January 4 (old calendar)|ja|1月4日 (旧暦)|12=draft}}''', corresponding to '''{{ill|January 29|ja|1月29日|12=draft}}, 1419 (Julian calendar).''' --- === '''Reconstruction in the Edo Period'''=== After this '''destruction, the shrine fell into neglect''', and by the '''Early Modern Period (近世), its location was lost'''. However, thanks to the efforts of '''{{ill|Kawabe Kiyonaga|ja|河邊精長|12=draft}} (also known as {{ill|Ōnakatomi Kiyonaga|ja|大中臣精長|12=draft}}),''' the '''Grand Chief Priest ({{ill|Ōgūji|ja|大宮司|12=draft}}),''' the shrine was '''reconstructed on its present site on '''{{ill|Kanbun (era)|ja|寛文|12=draft}} 3, '''{{ill|July 7 (old calendar)|ja|7月7日 (旧暦)|12=draft}}''' (corresponding to '''{{ill|August 9|ja|8月9日|12=draft}}, {{ill|1663|ja|1663rd year|12=draft}} in the Gregorian calendar).''' * ''{{ill|Shinmei Hisho|ja|神名秘書|12=draft}}'' states: '''"Located in Numaki-go, Yamada Village. East of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月読宮|12=draft}}."''' * ''{{ill|Ruiju Jingi Hongen|ja|類聚神祇本源|12=draft}}'' states: '''"East of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月読宮|12=draft}}, within the same {{ill|Tamagaki|ja|玉垣|12=draft}} fence."''' * ''{{ill|Ninomiya Kansa Enkaku Kō|ja|二宮管社沿革考|12=draft}}'' claims that '''the original shrine site was actually the present-day '''{{ill|Suhara Taisha|ja|須原大社|12=draft}} in '''Ichinoki, Ise City.'''Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p. 295 --- === '''Reconstruction in the Modern Period'''=== * '''In {{ill|1911|ja|1911th year|12=draft}} ({{ill|Meiji|ja|明治|12=draft}} 44),''' the shrine was '''rebuilt.'''Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): p. 12 * '''In {{ill|1938|ja|1938th year|12=draft}} ({{ill|Shōwa|ja|昭和|12=draft}} 13),''' it was '''rebuilt again'''. * '''In {{ill|1957|ja|1957th year|12=draft}} (Shōwa 32),''' a '''major renovation''' was completed, and '''a sacred transfer ritual ({{ill|Sengyo|ja|遷御|12=draft}}) was performed 20 years later.'''Sakurai (1991): p. 298 --- == Rites and Festivals (祭事) == * '''February''' – {{ill|Kinen-sai (祈年祭)|ja|祈年祭|12=draft}} (Harvest Prayer Festival) * '''June & December''' – {{ill|Tsukinami-sai (月次祭)|ja|月次祭|1=Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|12=draft}} (Monthly Festival) * '''October''' – {{ill|Kannamesai (神嘗祭)|ja|神嘗祭|12=draft}} (Offering of First Fruits Festival) * '''November''' – {{ill|Niiname-sai (新嘗祭)|ja|新嘗祭|12=draft}} (Thanksgiving Harvest Festival) These '''four major rituals''' are '''conducted on-site by a Negi (禰宜, senior priest) in巡回祭典 (巡回祭,巡行 ceremony format).''' The following '''six rites are performed remotely (遥祀, Yōshi):''' * '''January''' – {{ill|Saitan-sai (歳旦祭)|ja|歳旦祭|12=draft}} (New Year's Festival) * '''January''' – {{ill|Genshi-sai (元始祭)|ja|元始祭|12=draft}} (Imperial Foundation Festival) * '''February 11''' – {{ill|Kenkoku-kinen-sai (建国記念祭)|ja|建国記念祭|12=draft}} (National Foundation Day) * '''May & August''' – {{ill|Kaze-no-Hi-no-Matsuri (風日祈祭)|ja|風日祈祭|12=draft}} (Wind and Rain Prayers) * '''December 23''' – {{ill|Tenchō-sai (天長祭)|ja|天長祭|12=draft}} (Emperor's Birthday Festival) --- == Access (交通) == [[File:Tsukiyominomiyamae Bus Stop.jpg|thumb|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya-mae Bus Stop]] '''Public Transport:''' * '''10-minute walk (550m)''' from '''{{ill|Ise City Station|ja|伊勢市駅|12=draft}} (JR & Kintetsu)'''.Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p. 33 * '''4-minute walk (360m)''' from '''Shindō Bus Stop (三重交通)'''. {{Shrine |name = Takagawara Shrine |religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Takagawara-jinja 02.jpg|270px]] |location = {{ill|Ise, Mie|ja|伊勢市|12=draft}}, Miyago 1-chome 3-19, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|ja|三重県|12=draft}} |latitude_deg = 34 | latitude_min = 29 | latitude_sec = 34.5 |longitude_deg = 136 | longitude_min = 42 | longitude_sec = 22.2 |map = Japan Mie |deity = {{ill|Tsukuyomi|ja|月夜見尊御魂|12=draft}} |rank = {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=draft}} (small)
{{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮|1=Toyouke Daijingu|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮|12=draft}} Subordinate Shrine |founded = Before {{ill|Enryaku|ja|延暦|12=draft}} 23 (804) |main_hall = {{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|ja|神明造|12=draft}} |other_names = |pilgrimage_sites = |annual_festival = |rituals = {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭|12=draft}} }} Takagawara Shrine (高河原神社, ''Takagawara Jinja''Shikinen Sengu Memorial Sengu-kan "[http://www.sengukan.jp/wp-content/themes/sengukan/shrine/area06.php Takagawara Shrine たかがわらじんじゃ>>]" (Accessed October 8, 2013).[[iTV]] "[http://www.yoitokose.jp/ise/encyclopedia/t0010.php Takagawara Shrine | Ise Grand Shrine Encyclopedia | Ise-Shima Travel Yoitokose]" (Accessed October 8, 2013)., also pronounced ''Takakawara Jinja''Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.39Gakken Publishing (2013): p.57) is a [[Shinto]] shrine located in Miyago, {{ill|Ise, Mie|ja|伊勢市|12=draft}}, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|ja|三重県|12=draft}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|subordinate shrine (sessha/massha)|ja|摂末社|12=draft}} of {{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮|1=Toyouke Daijingu|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮|12=draft}} (the Outer Shrine of {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮|12=draft}}) and classified as a {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=draft}}. It ranks 10th among the 16 subordinate shrines of the Outer ShrineUjiyamada City Hall (1929): pp.11–13.. The shrine is located within the precincts of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|ja|月夜見宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|12=draft}}, which is a separate shrine of the Outer ShrineIse Bunka-sha (2008): p.38. == Overview (概要) == Located at {{ill|Mie Prefecture|ja|三重県|12=draft}} {{ill|Ise, Mie|ja|伊勢市|12=draft}} 1006 Miyago 1-chome式内社研究会 編（1990）：294ページ (modern address: 1-3-19 Miyago, Ise City). The shrine is situated behind and to the right (northeast) of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月夜見宮|12=draft}}'s main hall. The shrine grounds are surrounded by a moat on three sides, which is believed to be a remnant of a tributary of the {{ill|Miyagawa River (Mie)|ja|宮川 (三重県)|12=draft}}. The enshrined deity is {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto no Mitama|ja|月夜見尊御魂|12=draft}} (つきよみのみことのみたま). The shrine is located in Takagawara (高河原), an area near the Miyagawa River, and serves as a {{ill|guardian deity|ja|守護神|12=draft}} (守護神) for the land development of the surrounding region. Many ancient texts describe the enshrined deity as the Mitama (spirit) of {{ill|Tsukiyomi|ja|月読|12=draft}}. However, the ''{{ill|Shinmei-chō Kōshō Saikō|ja|神名帳考證再考|12=draft}}'' (''神名帳考證再考'') claims that the deity is actually {{ill|Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto|ja|倉稲魂命|12=draft}} (倉稲魂命), the deity of grain and prosperity. nother text, ''{{ill|Ninomiya Kansa Enkaku Kō|ja|二宮管社沿革考|12=draft}}'' (''二宮管社沿革考''), asserts that the original name of the shrine in the ''{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|12=draft}}'' (延喜式神名帳) was "{{ill|Kawahara-ni-Masu-Kuninamino-Kami Jinja|ja|川原坐国生神社|12=draft}}", proving that its deity is {{ill|Kuninamino-Kami|ja|国生神|12=draft}} (国生神), the god of land formation.Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): pp. 295–296 The main hall follows {{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|ja|神明造|12=draft}} (神明造, the {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮|12=draft}} architectural style) and has a wooden board roof ({{ill|Itabuki|ja|板葺|12=draft}}), enclosed by a {{ill|Tamagaki|ja|玉垣|12=draft}} (玉垣, sacred fence). Unlike most {{ill|Sessha|ja|摂社|12=draft}}・{{ill|Massha|ja|末社|12=draft}}・{{ill|Shokan-sha|ja|所管社|12=draft}} (摂社・末社・所管社, auxiliary shrines) of {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮|12=draft}}, which do not have an offering box ({{ill|Saisenbako|ja|賽銭箱|12=draft}})Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p. 26, Takagawara Shrine uniquely has one. == History (歴史) == Based on the definition of a {{ill|Sessha|ja|摂社|12=draft}} (auxiliary shrine) within {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮|12=draft}}, this shrine was established before the compilation of the ''{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|12=draft}}'' in {{ill|Enchō (era)|ja|延長|12=draft}} 5 ({{ill|927|ja|927th year|12=draft}}).Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p. 22 * The shrine is listed in that text as "{{ill|Kawahara-ni-Masu-Kuninamino-Kami Jinja|ja|川原坐国生神社|12=draft}}". * Additionally, it is mentioned as "{{ill|Takagawara-sha|ja|高河原社|12=draft}}" in the ''{{ill|Toyuke Daijingu Gishiki-chō|ja|止由気宮儀式帳|12=draft}}''. * Since that text dates back to {{ill|Enryaku (era)|ja|延暦|12=draft}} 23 ({{ill|804|ja|804th year|12=draft}}), this confirms that the shrine existed before that time. According to the ''{{ill|Ruiju Jingi Hongen|ja|類聚神祇本源|12=draft}}'', reconstructions were regularly conducted from {{ill|Tokuji (era)|ja|徳治|12=draft}} 1 ({{ill|1306|ja|1306年|12=draft}}) onwards, under the supervision of a special Zōsai-shi (造替使, shrine reconstruction official).Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p. 296 The ''{{ill|Ninomiya Kansa Enkaku Kō|ja|二宮管社沿革考|12=draft}}'' records that: {{quote|"According to the '''Ōei Tōkō Nikki (応永頭工日記)''', on the '''fourth day of the first month in '''{{ill|Ōei (era)|ja|応永|12=draft}} 26 ({{ill|1419|ja|1419th year|12=draft}})''', a great fire burned down '''{{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月夜見宮|12=draft}}''', its small shrine, '''Kawahara-sha (高河原社)''', and '''Imibiya-den (忌火屋殿, the sacred fire hall)'''."}} Thus, the shrine was confirmed to have existed until it burned down on {{ill|January 4 (old calendar)|ja|1月4日 (旧暦)|12=draft}}, corresponding to {{ill|January 29|ja|1月29日|12=draft}}, 1419 (Julian calendar). --- === Reconstruction in the Edo Period=== After this destruction, the shrine fell into neglect, and by the Early Modern Period (近世), its location was lost. However, thanks to the efforts of {{ill|Kawabe Kiyonaga|ja|河邊精長|12=draft}} (also known as {{ill|Ōnakatomi Kiyonaga|ja|大中臣精長|12=draft}}), the Grand Chief Priest ({{ill|Ōgūji|ja|大宮司|12=draft}}), the shrine was reconstructed on its present site on {{ill|Kanbun (era)|ja|寛文|12=draft}} 3, {{ill|July 7 (old calendar)|ja|7月7日 (旧暦)|12=draft}} (corresponding to {{ill|August 9|ja|8月9日|12=draft}}, {{ill|1663|ja|1663rd year|12=draft}} in the Gregorian calendar). * ''{{ill|Shinmei Hisho|ja|神名秘書|12=draft}}'' states: "Located in Numaki-go, Yamada Village. East of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月読宮|12=draft}}." * ''{{ill|Ruiju Jingi Hongen|ja|類聚神祇本源|12=draft}}'' states: "East of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月読宮|12=draft}}, within the same {{ill|Tamagaki|ja|玉垣|12=draft}} fence." * ''{{ill|Ninomiya Kansa Enkaku Kō|ja|二宮管社沿革考|12=draft}}'' claims that the original shrine site was actually the present-day {{ill|Suhara Taisha|ja|須原大社|12=draft}} in Ichinoki, Ise City.Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p. 295 --- === Reconstruction in the Modern Period=== * In {{ill|1911|ja|1911th year|12=draft}} ({{ill|Meiji|ja|明治|12=draft}} 44), the shrine was rebuilt.Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): p. 12 * In {{ill|1938|ja|1938th year|12=draft}} ({{ill|Shōwa|ja|昭和|12=draft}} 13), it was rebuilt again. * In {{ill|1957|ja|1957th year|12=draft}} (Shōwa 32), a major renovation was completed, and a sacred transfer ritual ({{ill|Sengyo|ja|遷御|12=draft}}) was performed 20 years later.Sakurai (1991): p. 298 --- == Rites and Festivals (祭事) == * February – {{ill|Kinen-sai (祈年祭)|ja|祈年祭|12=draft}} (Harvest Prayer Festival) * June & December – {{ill|Tsukinami-sai (月次祭)|ja|月次祭|1=Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|12=draft}} (Monthly Festival) * October – {{ill|Kannamesai (神嘗祭)|ja|神嘗祭|12=draft}} (Offering of First Fruits Festival) * November – {{ill|Niiname-sai (新嘗祭)|ja|新嘗祭|12=draft}} (Thanksgiving Harvest Festival) These four major rituals are conducted on-site by a Negi (禰宜, senior priest) in巡回祭典 (巡回祭,巡行 ceremony format). The following six rites are performed remotely (遥祀, Yōshi): * January – {{ill|Saitan-sai (歳旦祭)|ja|歳旦祭|12=draft}} (New Year's Festival) * January – {{ill|Genshi-sai (元始祭)|ja|元始祭|12=draft}} (Imperial Foundation Festival) * February 11 – {{ill|Kenkoku-kinen-sai (建国記念祭)|ja|建国記念祭|12=draft}} (National Foundation Day) * May & August – {{ill|Kaze-no-Hi-no-Matsuri (風日祈祭)|ja|風日祈祭|12=draft}} (Wind and Rain Prayers) * December 23 – {{ill|Tenchō-sai (天長祭)|ja|天長祭|12=draft}} (Emperor's Birthday Festival) --- == Access (交通) == [[File:Tsukiyominomiyamae Bus Stop.jpg|thumb|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya-mae Bus Stop]] Public Transport: * 10-minute walk (550m) from {{ill|Ise City Station|ja|伊勢市駅|12=draft}} (JR & Kintetsu).Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p. 33 * 4-minute walk (360m) from Shindō Bus Stop (三重交通). By Car: * Approx. 5 minutes (2.5km) from Ise Nishi IC (伊勢西IC, Ise Expressway). * Metered parking available near the entrance. --- == References == {{Reflist}} == 参考文献 == * 宇治山田市役所 編『宇治山田市史 上巻』宇治山田市役所、昭和4th year 1月20日、862p. * [[学研パブリッシング]]『伊勢神宮に行こう』Gakken Mook神社紀行セレクションvol.1、[[薗田稔]]監修、学研マーケティング、2013rd year 7月4日、82p. ISBN 978-4-05-610047-1 * [[櫻井勝之進]]『伊勢神宮の祖型と展開』[[国書刊行会]]、平成3rd year 11月30日、318p. ISBN 4-336-03296-3 * 式内社研究会 編『式内社調査報告 第六巻 東海道1』[[Kogakkan University]]出版部、平成2nd year 2月28日、690p. ISBN 4-87644-080-8 * 『お伊勢さん125社めぐり』別冊『伊勢人』、[[伊勢文化舎]]、平成20th year 12月23日、151p. ISBN 978-4-900759-37-4 == See Also == * {{ill|List of Shikinaisha in Ise Province|ja|伊勢国の式内社一覧|12=draft}} * {{ill|List of 125 Shrines of Ise|ja|神宮125社の一覧|lt=List of 125 Shrines of Ise|1=List of Shikinaisha in Ise Province|3=伊勢国の式内社一覧|12=draft}} == External Links == * [http://www.jingukaikan.jp/125mairi/m02/0203.html 高河原神社（たかがわらじんじゃ）] - 財団法人伊勢神宮崇敬会 {{125 Shrines of Ise}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Shrines in Mie Prefecture]] [[Category:Subordinate shrines of Toyouke Daijingu]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Japan]] [[Category:Ise Grand Shrine]] [[Category:completion tier 5]] [[Category:125 Shrines of Ise]] [[Category:Completion tier 5]] [[Category:11]] [[Category:高河原神社]] [[Category:伊勢国の式内社]] [[Category:摂末社]] [[Category:伊勢市の神社]] [[Category:refreshing imported pages]] [[Category:category refresh]] [[Category:New]] [[Category:qq]] }} [[ja:高河原神社]] [[sn:Takagawara Shrine]] [[sn:akagawara Shrine]]

According to the ''{{ill|Ruiju Jingi Hongen|ja|類聚神祇本源|12=draft}}'', reconstructions were regularly conducted from {{ill|Tokuji (era)|ja|徳治|12=draft}} 1 ({{ill|1306|ja|1306年|12=draft}}) onwards, under the supervision of a special Zōsai-shi (造替使, shrine reconstruction official).Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p. 296 The ''{{ill|Ninomiya Kansa Enkaku Kō|ja|二宮管社沿革考|12=draft}}'' records that: {{quote|"According to the '''Ōei Tōkō Nikki (応永頭工日記)''', on the '''fourth day of the first month in '''{{ill|Ōei (era)|ja|応永|12=draft}} 26 ({{ill|1419|ja|1419th year|12=draft}})''', a great fire burned down '''{{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月夜見宮|12=draft}}''', its small shrine, '''Kawahara-sha (高河原社)''', and '''Imibiya-den (忌火屋殿, the sacred fire hall)'''."}} Thus, the shrine was confirmed to have existed until it burned down on {{ill|January 4 (old calendar)|ja|1月4日 (旧暦)|12=draft}}, corresponding to {{ill|January 29|ja|1月29日|12=draft}}, 1419 (Julian calendar). --- === Reconstruction in the Edo Period=== After this destruction, the shrine fell into neglect, and by the Early Modern Period (近世), its location was lost. However, thanks to the efforts of {{ill|Kawabe Kiyonaga|ja|河邊精長|12=draft}} (also known as {{ill|Ōnakatomi Kiyonaga|ja|大中臣精長|12=draft}}), the Grand Chief Priest ({{ill|Ōgūji|ja|大宮司|12=draft}}), the shrine was reconstructed on its present site on {{ill|Kanbun (era)|ja|寛文|12=draft}} 3, {{ill|July 7 (old calendar)|ja|7月7日 (旧暦)|12=draft}} (corresponding to {{ill|August 9|ja|8月9日|12=draft}}, {{ill|1663|ja|1663rd year|12=draft}} in the Gregorian calendar). * ''{{ill|Shinmei Hisho|ja|神名秘書|12=draft}}'' states: "Located in Numaki-go, Yamada Village. East of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月読宮|12=draft}}." * ''{{ill|Ruiju Jingi Hongen|ja|類聚神祇本源|12=draft}}'' states: "East of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月読宮|12=draft}}, within the same {{ill|Tamagaki|ja|玉垣|12=draft}} fence." * ''{{ill|Ninomiya Kansa Enkaku Kō|ja|二宮管社沿革考|12=draft}}'' claims that the original shrine site was actually the present-day {{ill|Suhara Taisha|ja|須原大社|12=draft}} in Ichinoki, Ise City.Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p. 295 --- === Reconstruction in the Modern Period=== * In {{ill|1911|ja|1911th year|12=draft}} ({{ill|Meiji|ja|明治|12=draft}} 44), the shrine was rebuilt.Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): p. 12 * In {{ill|1938|ja|1938th year|12=draft}} ({{ill|Shōwa|ja|昭和|12=draft}} 13), it was rebuilt again. * In {{ill|1957|ja|1957th year|12=draft}} (Shōwa 32), a major renovation was completed, and a sacred transfer ritual ({{ill|Sengyo|ja|遷御|12=draft}}) was performed 20 years later.Sakurai (1991): p. 298 --- == Rites and Festivals (祭事) == * February – {{ill|Kinen-sai (祈年祭)|ja|祈年祭|12=draft}} (Harvest Prayer Festival) * June & December – {{ill|Tsukinami-sai (月次祭)|ja|月次祭|1=Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|12=draft}} (Monthly Festival) * October – {{ill|Kannamesai (神嘗祭)|ja|神嘗祭|12=draft}} (Offering of First Fruits Festival) * November – {{ill|Niiname-sai (新嘗祭)|ja|新嘗祭|12=draft}} (Thanksgiving Harvest Festival) These four major rituals are conducted on-site by a Negi (禰宜, senior priest) in巡回祭典 (巡回祭,巡行 ceremony format). The following six rites are performed remotely (遥祀, Yōshi): * January – {{ill|Saitan-sai (歳旦祭)|ja|歳旦祭|12=draft}} (New Year's Festival) * January – {{ill|Genshi-sai (元始祭)|ja|元始祭|12=draft}} (Imperial Foundation Festival) * February 11 – {{ill|Kenkoku-kinen-sai (建国記念祭)|ja|建国記念祭|12=draft}} (National Foundation Day) * May & August – {{ill|Kaze-no-Hi-no-Matsuri (風日祈祭)|ja|風日祈祭|12=draft}} (Wind and Rain Prayers) * December 23 – {{ill|Tenchō-sai (天長祭)|ja|天長祭|12=draft}} (Emperor's Birthday Festival) --- == Access (交通) == [[File:Tsukiyominomiyamae Bus Stop.jpg|thumb|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya-mae Bus Stop]] Public Transport: * 10-minute walk (550m) from {{ill|Ise City Station|ja|伊勢市駅|12=draft}} (JR & Kintetsu).Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p. 33 * 4-minute walk (360m) from Shindō Bus Stop (三重交通). {{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮|1=Toyouke Daijingu|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮|12=draft|12=draft}} Subordinate Shrine |founded = Before {{ill|Enryaku|ja|延暦|12=draft|12=draft}} 23 (804) |main_hall = {{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|ja|神明造|12=draft|12=draft}} |other_names = |pilgrimage_sites = |annual_festival = |rituals = {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭|12=draft|12=draft}} }} Takagawara Shrine (高河原神社, ''Takagawara Jinja''Shikinen Sengu Memorial Sengu-kan "[http://www.sengukan.jp/wp-content/themes/sengukan/shrine/area06.php Takagawara Shrine たかがわらじんじゃ>>]" (Accessed October 8, 2013).[[iTV]] "[http://www.yoitokose.jp/ise/encyclopedia/t0010.php Takagawara Shrine | Ise Grand Shrine Encyclopedia | Ise-Shima Travel Yoitokose]" (Accessed October 8, 2013)., also pronounced ''Takakawara Jinja''Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.39Gakken Publishing (2013): p.57) is a [[Shinto]] shrine located in Miyago, {{ill|Ise, Mie|ja|伊勢市|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|ja|三重県|12=draft|12=draft}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|subordinate shrine (sessha/massha)|ja|摂末社|12=draft|12=draft}} of {{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮|1=Toyouke Daijingu|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮|12=draft|12=draft}} (the Outer Shrine of {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮|12=draft|12=draft}}) and classified as a {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=draft|12=draft}}. It ranks 10th among the 16 subordinate shrines of the Outer ShrineUjiyamada City Hall (1929): pp.11–13.. The shrine is located within the precincts of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|ja|月夜見宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|12=draft|12=draft}}, which is a separate shrine of the Outer ShrineIse Bunka-sha (2008): p.38. == Overview (概要) == Located at {{ill|Mie Prefecture|ja|三重県|12=draft|12=draft}} {{ill|Ise, Mie|ja|伊勢市|12=draft|12=draft}} 1006 Miyago 1-chome式内社研究会 編（1990）：294ページ (modern address: 1-3-19 Miyago, Ise City). The shrine is situated behind and to the right (northeast) of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月夜見宮|12=draft|12=draft}}'s main hall. The shrine grounds are surrounded by a moat on three sides, which is believed to be a remnant of a tributary of the {{ill|Miyagawa River (Mie)|ja|宮川 (三重県)|12=draft|12=draft}}. The enshrined deity is {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto no Mitama|ja|月夜見尊御魂|12=draft|12=draft}} (つきよみのみことのみたま). The shrine is located in Takagawara (高河原), an area near the Miyagawa River, and serves as a {{ill|guardian deity|ja|守護神|12=draft|12=draft}} (守護神) for the land development of the surrounding region. Many ancient texts describe the enshrined deity as the Mitama (spirit) of {{ill|Tsukiyomi|ja|月読|12=draft|12=draft}}. {{Shrine |name = Takagawara Shrine |religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Takagawara-jinja 02.jpg|270px]] |location = {{ill|Ise, Mie|ja|伊勢市|12=draft|12=draft}}, Miyago 1-chome 3-19, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|ja|三重県|12=draft|12=draft}} |latitude_deg = 34 | latitude_min = 29 | latitude_sec = 34.5 |longitude_deg = 136 | longitude_min = 42 | longitude_sec = 22.2 |map = Japan Mie |deity = {{ill|Tsukuyomi|ja|月夜見尊御魂|12=draft|12=draft}} |Rank = {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=draft|12=draft}} (small)
{{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮|1=Toyouke Daijingu|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮|12=draft|12=draft}} Subordinate Shrine |founded = Before {{ill|Enryaku|ja|延暦|12=draft|12=draft}} 23 (804) |main_hall = {{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|ja|神明造|12=draft|12=draft}} |other_names = |pilgrimage_sites = |annual_festival = |rituals = {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭|12=draft|12=draft}} }} Takagawara Shrine (高河原神社, ''Takagawara Jinja''Shikinen Sengu Memorial Sengu-kan "[http://www.sengukan.jp/wp-content/themes/sengukan/shrine/area06.php Takagawara Shrine たかがわらじんじゃ>>]" (Accessed October 8, 2013).[[iTV]] "[http://www.yoitokose.jp/ise/encyclopedia/t0010.php Takagawara Shrine | Ise Grand Shrine Encyclopedia | Ise-Shima Travel Yoitokose]" (Accessed October 8, 2013)., also pronounced ''Takakawara Jinja''Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.39Gakken Publishing (2013): p.57) is a [[Shinto]] shrine located in Miyago, {{ill|Ise, Mie|ja|伊勢市|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|ja|三重県|12=draft|12=draft}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|subordinate shrine (sessha/massha)|ja|摂末社|12=draft|12=draft}} of {{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮|1=Toyouke Daijingu|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮|12=draft|12=draft}} (the Outer Shrine of {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮|12=draft|12=draft}}) and classified as a {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=draft|12=draft}}. It Ranks 10th among the 16 subordinate shrines of the Outer ShrineUjiyamada City Hall (1929): pp.11–13.. The shrine is located within the precincts of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|ja|月夜見宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|12=draft|12=draft}}, which is a separate shrine of the Outer ShrineIse Bunka-sha (2008): p.38. == Overview (概要) == Located at {{ill|Mie Prefecture|ja|三重県|12=draft|12=draft}} {{ill|Ise, Mie|ja|伊勢市|12=draft|12=draft}} 1006 Miyago 1-chome式内社研究会 編（1990）：294ページ (modern address: 1-3-19 Miyago, Ise City). The shrine is situated behind and to the right (northeast) of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月夜見宮|12=draft|12=draft}}'s main hall. The shrine grounds are surrounded by a moat on three sides, which is believed to be a remnant of a tributary of the {{ill|Miyagawa River (Mie)|ja|宮川 (三重県)|12=draft|12=draft}}. The enshrined deity is {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto no Mitama|ja|月夜見尊御魂|12=draft|12=draft}} (つきよみのみことのみたま). The shrine is located in Takagawara (高河原), an area near the Miyagawa River, and serves as a {{ill|guardian deity|ja|守護神|12=draft|12=draft}} (守護神) for the land development of the surrounding region. Many ancient texts describe the enshrined deity as the Mitama (spirit) of {{ill|Tsukiyomi|ja|月読|12=draft|12=draft}}. However, the ''{{ill|Shinmei-chō Kōshō Saikō|ja|神名帳考證再考|12=draft|12=draft}}'' (''神名帳考證再考'') claims that the deity is actually {{ill|Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto|ja|倉稲魂命|12=draft|12=draft}} (倉稲魂命), the deity of grain and prosperity. nother text, ''{{ill|Ninomiya Kansa Enkaku Kō|ja|二宮管社沿革考|12=draft|12=draft}}'' (''二宮管社沿革考''), asserts that the original name of the shrine in the ''{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|12=draft|12=draft}}'' (延喜式神名帳) was "{{ill|Kawahara-ni-Masu-Kuninamino-Kami Jinja|ja|川原坐国生神社|12=draft|12=draft}}", proving that its deity is {{ill|Kuninamino-Kami|ja|国生神|12=draft|12=draft}} (国生神), the god of land formation.Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): pp. 295–296 The main hall follows {{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|ja|神明造|12=draft|12=draft}} (神明造, the {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮|12=draft|12=draft}} architectural style) and has a wooden board roof ({{ill|Itabuki|ja|板葺|12=draft|12=draft}}), enclosed by a {{ill|Tamagaki|ja|玉垣|12=draft|12=draft}} (玉垣, sacred fence). Unlike most {{ill|Sessha|ja|摂社|12=draft|12=draft}}・{{ill|Massha|ja|末社|12=draft|12=draft}}・{{ill|Shokan-sha|ja|所管社|12=draft|12=draft}} (摂社・末社・所管社, auxiliary shrines) of {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮|12=draft|12=draft}}, which do not have an offering box ({{ill|Saisenbako|ja|賽銭箱|12=draft|12=draft}})Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p. 26, Takagawara Shrine uniquely has one. == History (歴史) == Based on the definition of a {{ill|Sessha|ja|摂社|12=draft|12=draft}} (auxiliary shrine) within {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮|12=draft|12=draft}}, this shrine was established before the compilation of the ''{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|12=draft|12=draft}}'' in {{ill|Enchō (era)|ja|延長|12=draft|12=draft}} 5 ({{ill|927|ja|927th year|12=draft|12=draft}}).Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p. 22 * The shrine is listed in that text as "{{ill|Kawahara-ni-Masu-Kuninamino-Kami Jinja|ja|川原坐国生神社|12=draft|12=draft}}". * Additionally, it is mentioned as "{{ill|Takagawara-sha|ja|高河原社|12=draft|12=draft}}" in the ''{{ill|Toyuke Daijingu Gishiki-chō|ja|止由気宮儀式帳|12=draft|12=draft}}''. * Since that text dates back to {{ill|Enryaku (era)|ja|延暦|12=draft|12=draft}} 23 ({{ill|804|ja|804th year|12=draft|12=draft}}), this confirms that the shrine existed before that time. According to the ''{{ill|Ruiju Jingi Hongen|ja|類聚神祇本源|12=draft|12=draft}}'', reconstructions were regularly conducted from {{ill|Tokuji (era)|ja|徳治|12=draft|12=draft}} 1 ({{ill|1306|ja|1306年|12=draft|12=draft}}) onwards, under the supervision of a special Zōsai-shi (造替使, shrine reconstruction official).Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p. 296 The ''{{ill|Ninomiya Kansa Enkaku Kō|ja|二宮管社沿革考|12=draft|12=draft}}'' records that: {{quote|"According to the '''Ōei Tōkō Nikki (応永頭工日記)''', on the '''fourth day of the first month in '''{{ill|Ōei (era)|ja|応永|12=draft|12=draft}} 26 ({{ill|1419|ja|1419th year|12=draft|12=draft}})''', a great fire burned down '''{{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月夜見宮|12=draft|12=draft}}''', its small shrine, '''Kawahara-sha (高河原社)''', and '''Imibiya-den (忌火屋殿, the sacred fire hall)'''."}} Thus, the shrine was confirmed to have existed until it burned down on {{ill|January 4 (old calendar)|ja|1月4日 (旧暦)|12=draft|12=draft}}, corresponding to {{ill|January 29|ja|1月29日|12=draft|12=draft}}, 1419 (Julian calendar). --- === Reconstruction in the Edo Period=== After this destruction, the shrine fell into neglect, and by the Early Modern Period (近世), its location was lost. However, thanks to the efforts of {{ill|Kawabe Kiyonaga|ja|河邊精長|12=draft|12=draft}} (also known as {{ill|Ōnakatomi Kiyonaga|ja|大中臣精長|12=draft|12=draft}}), the Grand Chief Priest ({{ill|Ōgūji|ja|大宮司|12=draft|12=draft}}), the shrine was reconstructed on its present site on {{ill|Kanbun (era)|ja|寛文|12=draft|12=draft}} 3, {{ill|July 7 (old calendar)|ja|7月7日 (旧暦)|12=draft|12=draft}} (corresponding to {{ill|August 9|ja|8月9日|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|1663|ja|1663rd year|12=draft|12=draft}} in the Gregorian calendar). * ''{{ill|Shinmei Hisho|ja|神名秘書|12=draft|12=draft}}'' states: "Located in Numaki-go, Yamada Village. East of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月読宮|12=draft|12=draft}}." * ''{{ill|Ruiju Jingi Hongen|ja|類聚神祇本源|12=draft|12=draft}}'' states: "East of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月読宮|12=draft|12=draft}}, within the same {{ill|Tamagaki|ja|玉垣|12=draft|12=draft}} fence." * ''{{ill|Ninomiya Kansa Enkaku Kō|ja|二宮管社沿革考|12=draft|12=draft}}'' claims that the original shrine site was actually the present-day {{ill|Suhara Taisha|ja|須原大社|12=draft|12=draft}} in Ichinoki, Ise City.Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p. 295 --- === Reconstruction in the Modern Period=== * In {{ill|1911|ja|1911th year|12=draft|12=draft}} ({{ill|Meiji|ja|明治|12=draft|12=draft}} 44), the shrine was rebuilt.Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): p. 12 * In {{ill|1938|ja|1938th year|12=draft|12=draft}} ({{ill|Shōwa|ja|昭和|12=draft|12=draft}} 13), it was rebuilt again. * In {{ill|1957|ja|1957th year|12=draft|12=draft}} (Shōwa 32), a major renovation was completed, and a sacred transfer ritual ({{ill|Sengyo|ja|遷御|12=draft|12=draft}}) was performed 20 years later.Sakurai (1991): p. 298 --- == Rites and Festivals (祭事) == * February – {{ill|Kinen-sai (祈年祭)|ja|祈年祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (Harvest Prayer Festival) * June & December – {{ill|Tsukinami-sai (月次祭)|ja|月次祭|1=Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|12=draft|12=draft}} (Monthly Festival) * October – {{ill|Kannamesai (神嘗祭)|ja|神嘗祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (Offering of First Fruits Festival) * November – {{ill|Niiname-sai (新嘗祭)|ja|新嘗祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (Thanksgiving Harvest Festival) These four major rituals are conducted on-site by a Negi (禰宜, senior priest) in巡回祭典 (巡回祭,巡行 ceremony format). The following six rites are performed remotely (遥祀, Yōshi): * January – {{ill|Saitan-sai (歳旦祭)|ja|歳旦祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (New Year's Festival) * January – {{ill|Genshi-sai (元始祭)|ja|元始祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (Imperial Foundation Festival) * February 11 – {{ill|Kenkoku-kinen-sai (建国記念祭)|ja|建国記念祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (National Foundation Day) * May & August – {{ill|Kaze-no-Hi-no-Matsuri (風日祈祭)|ja|風日祈祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (Wind and Rain Prayers) * December 23 – {{ill|Tenchō-sai (天長祭)|ja|天長祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (Emperor's Birthday Festival) --- == Access (交通) == [[File:Tsukiyominomiyamae Bus Stop.jpg|thumb|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya-mae Bus Stop]] Public Transport: * 10-minute walk (550m) from {{ill|Ise City Station|ja|伊勢市駅|12=draft|12=draft}} (JR & Kintetsu).Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p. 33 * 4-minute walk (360m) from Shindō Bus Stop (三重交通). However, thanks to the efforts of {{ill|Kawabe Kiyonaga|ja|河邊精長|12=draft|12=draft}} (also known as {{ill|Ōnakatomi Kiyonaga|ja|大中臣精長|12=draft|12=draft}}), the Grand Chief Priest ({{ill|Ōgūji|ja|大宮司|12=draft|12=draft}}), the shrine was reconstructed on its present site on {{ill|Kanbun (era)|ja|寛文|12=draft|12=draft}} 3, {{ill|July 7 (old calendar)|ja|7月7日 (旧暦)|12=draft|12=draft}} (corresponding to {{ill|August 9|ja|8月9日|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|1663|ja|1663rd year|12=draft|12=draft}} in the Gregorian calendar). * ''{{ill|Shinmei Hisho|ja|神名秘書|12=draft|12=draft}}'' states: "Located in Numaki-go, Yamada Village. East of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月読宮|12=draft|12=draft}}." * ''{{ill|Ruiju Jingi Hongen|ja|類聚神祇本源|12=draft|12=draft}}'' states: "East of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月読宮|12=draft|12=draft}}, within the same {{ill|Tamagaki|ja|玉垣|12=draft|12=draft}} fence." * ''{{ill|Ninomiya Kansa Enkaku Kō|ja|二宮管社沿革考|12=draft|12=draft}}'' claims that the original shrine site was actually the present-day {{ill|Suhara Taisha|ja|須原大社|12=draft|12=draft}} in Ichinoki, Ise City.Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p. 295 --- === Reconstruction in the Modern Period=== * In {{ill|1911|ja|1911th year|12=draft|12=draft}} ({{ill|Meiji|ja|明治|12=draft|12=draft}} 44), the shrine was rebuilt.Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): p. 12 * In {{ill|1938|ja|1938th year|12=draft|12=draft}} ({{ill|Shōwa|ja|昭和|12=draft|12=draft}} 13), it was rebuilt again. * In {{ill|1957|ja|1957th year|12=draft|12=draft}} (Shōwa 32), a major renovation was completed, and a sacred transfer ritual ({{ill|Sengyo|ja|遷御|12=draft|12=draft}}) was performed 20 years later.Sakurai (1991): p. 298 --- == Rites and Festivals (祭事) == * February – {{ill|Kinen-sai (祈年祭)|ja|祈年祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (Harvest Prayer Festival) * June & December – {{ill|Tsukinami-sai (月次祭)|ja|月次祭|1=Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|12=draft|12=draft}} (Monthly Festival) * October – {{ill|Kannamesai (神嘗祭)|ja|神嘗祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (Offering of First Fruits Festival) * November – {{ill|Niiname-sai (新嘗祭)|ja|新嘗祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (Thanksgiving Harvest Festival) These four major rituals are conducted on-site by a Negi (禰宜, senior priest) in巡回祭典 (巡回祭,巡行 ceremony format). It is a {{ill|subordinate shrine (sessha/massha)|ja|摂末社|12=draft|12=draft}} of {{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮|1=Toyouke Daijingu|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮|12=draft|12=draft}} (the Outer Shrine of {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮|12=draft|12=draft}}) and classified as a {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=draft|12=draft}}. It Ranks 10th among the 16 subordinate shrines of the Outer ShrineUjiyamada City Hall (1929): pp.11–13.. The shrine is located within the precincts of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|ja|月夜見宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|12=draft|12=draft}}, which is a separate shrine of the Outer ShrineIse Bunka-sha (2008): p.38. == Overview (概要) == Located at {{ill|Mie Prefecture|ja|三重県|12=draft|12=draft}} {{ill|Ise, Mie|ja|伊勢市|12=draft|12=draft}} 1006 Miyago 1-chome式内社研究会 編（1990）：294ページ (modern address: 1-3-19 Miyago, Ise City). The shrine is situated behind and to the right (northeast) of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月夜見宮|12=draft|12=draft}}'s main hall. The shrine grounds are surrounded by a moat on three sides, which is believed to be a remnant of a tributary of the {{ill|Miyagawa River (Mie)|ja|宮川 (三重県)|12=draft|12=draft}}. The enshrined deity is {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto no Mitama|ja|月夜見尊御魂|12=draft|12=draft}} (つきよみのみことのみたま). The shrine is located in Takagawara (高河原), an area near the Miyagawa River, and serves as a {{ill|guardian deity|ja|守護神|12=draft|12=draft}} (守護神) for the land development of the surrounding region. {{Shrine |name = Takagawara Shrine |religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Takagawara-jinja 02.jpg|270px]] |location = {{ill|Ise, Mie|ja|伊勢市|12=draft|12=draft}}, Miyago 1-chome 3-19, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|ja|三重県|12=draft|12=draft}} |latitude_deg = 34 | latitude_min = 29 | latitude_sec = 34.5 |longitude_deg = 136 | longitude_min = 42 | longitude_sec = 22.2 |map = Japan Mie |deity = {{ill|Tsukuyomi|ja|月夜見尊御魂|12=draft|12=draft}} |Rank = {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=draft|12=draft}} (small)
{{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮|1=Toyouke Daijingu|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮|12=draft|12=draft}} Subordinate Shrine |founded = Before {{ill|Enryaku|ja|延暦|12=draft|12=draft}} 23 (804) |main_hall = {{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|ja|神明造|12=draft|12=draft}} |other_names = |pilgrimage_sites = |annual_festival = |rituals = {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭|12=draft|12=draft}} }} Takagawara Shrine (高河原神社, ''Takagawara Jinja''Shikinen Sengu Memorial Sengu-kan "[http://www.sengukan.jp/wp-content/themes/sengukan/shrine/area06.php Takagawara Shrine たかがわらじんじゃ>>]" (Accessed October 8, 2013).[[iTV]] "[http://www.yoitokose.jp/ise/encyclopedia/t0010.php Takagawara Shrine | Ise Grand Shrine Encyclopedia | Ise-Shima Travel Yoitokose]" (Accessed October 8, 2013)., also pronounced ''Takakawara Jinja''Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.39Gakken Publishing (2013): p.57) is a [[Shinto]] shrine located in Miyago, {{ill|Ise, Mie|ja|伊勢市|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|ja|三重県|12=draft|12=draft}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|subordinate shrine (sessha/massha)|ja|摂末社|12=draft|12=draft}} of {{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮|1=Toyouke Daijingu|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮|12=draft|12=draft}} (the Outer Shrine of {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮|12=draft|12=draft}}) and classified as a {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=draft|12=draft}}. It Ranks 10th among the 16 subordinate shrines of the Outer ShrineUjiyamada City Hall (1929): pp.11–13.. The shrine is located within the precincts of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|ja|月夜見宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|12=draft|12=draft}}, which is a separate shrine of the Outer ShrineIse Bunka-sha (2008): p.38. == Overview (概要) == Located at {{ill|Mie Prefecture|ja|三重県|12=draft|12=draft}} {{ill|Ise, Mie|ja|伊勢市|12=draft|12=draft}} 1006 Miyago 1-chome式内社研究会 編（1990）：294ページ (modern address: 1-3-19 Miyago, Ise City). The shrine is situated behind and to the right (northeast) of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月夜見宮|12=draft|12=draft}}'s main hall. The shrine grounds are surrounded by a moat on three sides, which is believed to be a remnant of a tributary of the {{ill|Miyagawa River (Mie)|ja|宮川 (三重県)|12=draft|12=draft}}. The enshrined deity is {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto no Mitama|ja|月夜見尊御魂|12=draft|12=draft}} (つきよみのみことのみたま). The shrine is located in Takagawara (高河原), an area near the Miyagawa River, and serves as a {{ill|guardian deity|ja|守護神|12=draft|12=draft}} (守護神) for the land development of the surrounding region. Many ancient texts describe the enshrined deity as the Mitama (spirit) of {{ill|Tsukiyomi|ja|月読|12=draft|12=draft}}. However, the ''{{ill|Shinmei-chō Kōshō Saikō|ja|神名帳考證再考|12=draft|12=draft}}'' (''神名帳考證再考'') claims that the deity is actually {{ill|Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto|ja|倉稲魂命|12=draft|12=draft}} (倉稲魂命), the deity of grain and prosperity. nother text, ''{{ill|Ninomiya Kansa Enkaku Kō|ja|二宮管社沿革考|12=draft|12=draft}}'' (''二宮管社沿革考''), asserts that the original name of the shrine in the ''{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|12=draft|12=draft}}'' (延喜式神名帳) was "{{ill|Kawahara-ni-Masu-Kuninamino-Kami Jinja|ja|川原坐国生神社|12=draft|12=draft}}", proving that its deity is {{ill|Kuninamino-Kami|ja|国生神|12=draft|12=draft}} (国生神), the god of land formation.Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): pp. 295–296 The main hall follows {{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|ja|神明造|12=draft|12=draft}} (神明造, the {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮|12=draft|12=draft}} architectural style) and has a wooden board roof ({{ill|Itabuki|ja|板葺|12=draft|12=draft}}), enclosed by a {{ill|Tamagaki|ja|玉垣|12=draft|12=draft}} (玉垣, sacred fence). Unlike most {{ill|Sessha|ja|摂社|12=draft|12=draft}}・{{ill|Massha|ja|末社|12=draft|12=draft}}・{{ill|Shokan-sha|ja|所管社|12=draft|12=draft}} (摂社・末社・所管社, auxiliary shrines) of {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮|12=draft|12=draft}}, which do not have an offering box ({{ill|Saisenbako|ja|賽銭箱|12=draft|12=draft}})Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p. 26, Takagawara Shrine uniquely has one. == History (歴史) == Based on the definition of a {{ill|Sessha|ja|摂社|12=draft|12=draft}} (auxiliary shrine) within {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮|12=draft|12=draft}}, this shrine was established before the compilation of the ''{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|12=draft|12=draft}}'' in {{ill|Enchō (era)|ja|延長|12=draft|12=draft}} 5 ({{ill|927|ja|927th year|12=draft|12=draft}}).Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p. 22 * The shrine is listed in that text as "{{ill|Kawahara-ni-Masu-Kuninamino-Kami Jinja|ja|川原坐国生神社|12=draft|12=draft}}". * Additionally, it is mentioned as "{{ill|Takagawara-sha|ja|高河原社|12=draft|12=draft}}" in the ''{{ill|Toyuke Daijingu Gishiki-chō|ja|止由気宮儀式帳|12=draft|12=draft}}''. * Since that text dates back to {{ill|Enryaku (era)|ja|延暦|12=draft|12=draft}} 23 ({{ill|804|ja|804th year|12=draft|12=draft}}), this confirms that the shrine existed before that time. According to the ''{{ill|Ruiju Jingi Hongen|ja|類聚神祇本源|12=draft|12=draft}}'', reconstructions were regularly conducted from {{ill|Tokuji (era)|ja|徳治|12=draft|12=draft}} 1 ({{ill|1306|ja|1306年|12=draft|12=draft}}) onwards, under the supervision of a special Zōsai-shi (造替使, shrine reconstruction official).Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p. 296 The ''{{ill|Ninomiya Kansa Enkaku Kō|ja|二宮管社沿革考|12=draft|12=draft}}'' records that: {{quote|"According to the '''Ōei Tōkō Nikki (応永頭工日記)''', on the '''fourth day of the first month in '''{{ill|Ōei (era)|ja|応永|12=draft|12=draft}} 26 ({{ill|1419|ja|1419th year|12=draft|12=draft}})''', a great fire burned down '''{{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月夜見宮|12=draft|12=draft}}''', its small shrine, '''Kawahara-sha (高河原社)''', and '''Imibiya-den (忌火屋殿, the sacred fire hall)'''."}} Thus, the shrine was confirmed to have existed until it burned down on {{ill|January 4 (old calendar)|ja|1月4日 (旧暦)|12=draft|12=draft}}, corresponding to {{ill|January 29|ja|1月29日|12=draft|12=draft}}, 1419 (Julian calendar). --- === Reconstruction in the Edo Period=== After this destruction, the shrine fell into neglect, and by the Early Modern Period (近世), its location was lost. However, thanks to the efforts of {{ill|Kawabe Kiyonaga|ja|河邊精長|12=draft|12=draft}} (also known as {{ill|Ōnakatomi Kiyonaga|ja|大中臣精長|12=draft|12=draft}}), the Grand Chief Priest ({{ill|Ōgūji|ja|大宮司|12=draft|12=draft}}), the shrine was reconstructed on its present site on {{ill|Kanbun (era)|ja|寛文|12=draft|12=draft}} 3, {{ill|July 7 (old calendar)|ja|7月7日 (旧暦)|12=draft|12=draft}} (corresponding to {{ill|August 9|ja|8月9日|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|1663|ja|1663rd year|12=draft|12=draft}} in the Gregorian calendar). * ''{{ill|Shinmei Hisho|ja|神名秘書|12=draft|12=draft}}'' states: "Located in Numaki-go, Yamada Village. East of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月読宮|12=draft|12=draft}}." * ''{{ill|Ruiju Jingi Hongen|ja|類聚神祇本源|12=draft|12=draft}}'' states: "East of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月読宮|12=draft|12=draft}}, within the same {{ill|Tamagaki|ja|玉垣|12=draft|12=draft}} fence." * ''{{ill|Ninomiya Kansa Enkaku Kō|ja|二宮管社沿革考|12=draft|12=draft}}'' claims that the original shrine site was actually the present-day {{ill|Suhara Taisha|ja|須原大社|12=draft|12=draft}} in Ichinoki, Ise City.Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p. 295 --- === Reconstruction in the Modern Period=== * In {{ill|1911|ja|1911th year|12=draft|12=draft}} ({{ill|Meiji|ja|明治|12=draft|12=draft}} 44), the shrine was rebuilt.Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): p. 12 * In {{ill|1938|ja|1938th year|12=draft|12=draft}} ({{ill|Shōwa|ja|昭和|12=draft|12=draft}} 13), it was rebuilt again. * In {{ill|1957|ja|1957th year|12=draft|12=draft}} (Shōwa 32), a major renovation was completed, and a sacred transfer ritual ({{ill|Sengyo|ja|遷御|12=draft|12=draft}}) was performed 20 years later.Sakurai (1991): p. 298 --- == Rites and Festivals (祭事) == * February – {{ill|Kinen-sai (祈年祭)|ja|祈年祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (Harvest Prayer Festival) * June & December – {{ill|Tsukinami-sai (月次祭)|ja|月次祭|1=Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|12=draft|12=draft}} (Monthly Festival) * October – {{ill|Kannamesai (神嘗祭)|ja|神嘗祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (Offering of First Fruits Festival) * November – {{ill|Niiname-sai (新嘗祭)|ja|新嘗祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (Thanksgiving Harvest Festival) These four major rituals are conducted on-site by a Negi (禰宜, senior priest) in巡回祭典 (巡回祭,巡行 ceremony format). The following six rites are performed remotely (遥祀, Yōshi): * January – {{ill|Saitan-sai (歳旦祭)|ja|歳旦祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (New Year's Festival) * January – {{ill|Genshi-sai (元始祭)|ja|元始祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (Imperial Foundation Festival) * February 11 – {{ill|Kenkoku-kinen-sai (建国記念祭)|ja|建国記念祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (National Foundation Day) * May & August – {{ill|Kaze-no-Hi-no-Matsuri (風日祈祭)|ja|風日祈祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (Wind and Rain Prayers) * December 23 – {{ill|Tenchō-sai (天長祭)|ja|天長祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (Emperor's Birthday Festival) --- == Access (交通) == [[File:Tsukiyominomiyamae Bus Stop.jpg|thumb|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya-mae Bus Stop]] Public Transport: * 10-minute walk (550m) from {{ill|Ise City Station|ja|伊勢市駅|12=draft|12=draft}} (JR & Kintetsu).Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p. 33 * 4-minute walk (360m) from Shindō Bus Stop (三重交通). By Car: * Approx. 5 minutes (2.5km) from Ise Nishi IC (伊勢西IC, Ise Expressway). * Metered parking available near the entrance. --- == References == {{Reflist}} == 参考文献 == * 宇治山田市役所 編『宇治山田市史 上巻』宇治山田市役所、昭和4th year 1月20日、862p. * [[学研パブリッシング]]『伊勢神宮に行こう』Gakken Mook神社紀行セレクションvol.1、[[薗田稔]]監修、学研マーケティング、2013rd year 7月4日、82p. It is a {{ill|subordinate shrine (sessha/massha)|ja|摂末社|12=draft|12=draft}} of {{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮|1=Toyouke Daijingu|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮|12=draft|12=draft}} (the Outer Shrine of {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮|12=draft|12=draft}}) and classified as a {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=draft|12=draft}}. It Ranks 10th among the 16 subordinate shrines of the Outer ShrineUjiyamada City Hall (1929): pp.11–13.. The shrine is located within the precincts of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|ja|月夜見宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|12=draft|12=draft}}, which is a separate shrine of the Outer ShrineIse Bunka-sha (2008): p.38. == Overview (概要) == Located at {{ill|Mie Prefecture|ja|三重県|12=draft|12=draft}} {{ill|Ise, Mie|ja|伊勢市|12=draft|12=draft}} 1006 Miyago 1-chome式内社研究会 編（1990）：294ページ (modern address: 1-3-19 Miyago, Ise City). The shrine is located in Takagawara (高河原), an area near the Miyagawa River, and serves as a {{ill|guardian deity|ja|守護神|12=draft|12=draft}} (守護神) for the land development of the surrounding region. Many ancient texts describe the enshrined deity as the Mitama (spirit) of {{ill|Tsukiyomi|ja|月読|12=draft|12=draft}}. However, the ''{{ill|Shinmei-chō Kōshō Saikō|ja|神名帳考證再考|12=draft|12=draft}}'' (''神名帳考證再考'') claims that the deity is actually {{ill|Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto|ja|倉稲魂命|12=draft|12=draft}} (倉稲魂命), the deity of grain and prosperity. nother text, ''{{ill|Ninomiya Kansa Enkaku Kō|ja|二宮管社沿革考|12=draft|12=draft}}'' (''二宮管社沿革考''), asserts that the original name of the shrine in the ''{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|12=draft|12=draft}}'' (延喜式神名帳) was "{{ill|Kawahara-ni-Masu-Kuninamino-Kami Jinja|ja|川原坐国生神社|12=draft|12=draft}}", proving that its deity is {{ill|Kuninamino-Kami|ja|国生神|12=draft|12=draft}} (国生神), the god of land formation.Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): pp. 295–296 The main hall follows {{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|ja|神明造|12=draft|12=draft}} (神明造, the {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮|12=draft|12=draft}} architectural style) and has a wooden board roof ({{ill|Itabuki|ja|板葺|12=draft|12=draft}}), enclosed by a {{ill|Tamagaki|ja|玉垣|12=draft|12=draft}} (玉垣, sacred fence). Unlike most {{ill|Sessha|ja|摂社|12=draft|12=draft}}・{{ill|Massha|ja|末社|12=draft|12=draft}}・{{ill|Shokan-sha|ja|所管社|12=draft|12=draft}} (摂社・末社・所管社, auxiliary shrines) of {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮|12=draft|12=draft}}, which do not have an offering box ({{ill|Saisenbako|ja|賽銭箱|12=draft|12=draft}})Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p. 26, Takagawara Shrine uniquely has one. == History (歴史) == Based on the definition of a {{ill|Sessha|ja|摂社|12=draft|12=draft}} (auxiliary shrine) within {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮|12=draft|12=draft}}, this shrine was established before the compilation of the ''{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|12=draft|12=draft}}'' in {{ill|Enchō (era)|ja|延長|12=draft|12=draft}} 5 ({{ill|927|ja|927th year|12=draft|12=draft}}).Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p. 22 * The shrine is listed in that text as "{{ill|Kawahara-ni-Masu-Kuninamino-Kami Jinja|ja|川原坐国生神社|12=draft|12=draft}}". * Additionally, it is mentioned as "{{ill|Takagawara-sha|ja|高河原社|12=draft|12=draft}}" in the ''{{ill|Toyuke Daijingu Gishiki-chō|ja|止由気宮儀式帳|12=draft|12=draft}}''. * Since that text dates back to {{ill|Enryaku (era)|ja|延暦|12=draft|12=draft}} 23 ({{ill|804|ja|804th year|12=draft|12=draft}}), this confirms that the shrine existed before that time. According to the ''{{ill|Ruiju Jingi Hongen|ja|類聚神祇本源|12=draft|12=draft}}'', reconstructions were regularly conducted from {{ill|Tokuji (era)|ja|徳治|12=draft|12=draft}} 1 ({{ill|1306|ja|1306年|12=draft|12=draft}}) onwards, under the supervision of a special Zōsai-shi (造替使, shrine reconstruction official).Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p. 296 The ''{{ill|Ninomiya Kansa Enkaku Kō|ja|二宮管社沿革考|12=draft|12=draft}}'' records that: {{quote|"According to the '''Ōei Tōkō Nikki (応永頭工日記)''', on the '''fourth day of the first month in '''{{ill|Ōei (era)|ja|応永|12=draft|12=draft}} 26 ({{ill|1419|ja|1419th year|12=draft|12=draft}})''', a great fire burned down '''{{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月夜見宮|12=draft|12=draft}}''', its small shrine, '''Kawahara-sha (高河原社)''', and '''Imibiya-den (忌火屋殿, the sacred fire hall)'''."}} Thus, the shrine was confirmed to have existed until it burned down on {{ill|January 4 (old calendar)|ja|1月4日 (旧暦)|12=draft|12=draft}}, corresponding to {{ill|January 29|ja|1月29日|12=draft|12=draft}}, 1419 (Julian calendar). --- === Reconstruction in the Edo Period=== After this destruction, the shrine fell into neglect, and by the Early Modern Period (近世), its location was lost. However, thanks to the efforts of {{ill|Kawabe Kiyonaga|ja|河邊精長|12=draft|12=draft}} (also known as {{ill|Ōnakatomi Kiyonaga|ja|大中臣精長|12=draft|12=draft}}), the Grand Chief Priest ({{ill|Ōgūji|ja|大宮司|12=draft|12=draft}}), the shrine was reconstructed on its present site on {{ill|Kanbun (era)|ja|寛文|12=draft|12=draft}} 3, {{ill|July 7 (old calendar)|ja|7月7日 (旧暦)|12=draft|12=draft}} (corresponding to {{ill|August 9|ja|8月9日|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|1663|ja|1663rd year|12=draft|12=draft}} in the Gregorian calendar). * ''{{ill|Shinmei Hisho|ja|神名秘書|12=draft|12=draft}}'' states: "Located in Numaki-go, Yamada Village. East of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月読宮|12=draft|12=draft}}." * ''{{ill|Ruiju Jingi Hongen|ja|類聚神祇本源|12=draft|12=draft}}'' states: "East of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月読宮|12=draft|12=draft}}, within the same {{ill|Tamagaki|ja|玉垣|12=draft|12=draft}} fence." * ''{{ill|Ninomiya Kansa Enkaku Kō|ja|二宮管社沿革考|12=draft|12=draft}}'' claims that the original shrine site was actually the present-day {{ill|Suhara Taisha|ja|須原大社|12=draft|12=draft}} in Ichinoki, Ise City.Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p. 295 --- === Reconstruction in the Modern Period=== * In {{ill|1911|ja|1911th year|12=draft|12=draft}} ({{ill|Meiji|ja|明治|12=draft|12=draft}} 44), the shrine was rebuilt.Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): p. 12 * In {{ill|1938|ja|1938th year|12=draft|12=draft}} ({{ill|Shōwa|ja|昭和|12=draft|12=draft}} 13), it was rebuilt again. * In {{ill|1957|ja|1957th year|12=draft|12=draft}} (Shōwa 32), a major renovation was completed, and a sacred transfer ritual ({{ill|Sengyo|ja|遷御|12=draft|12=draft}}) was performed 20 years later.Sakurai (1991): p. 298 --- == Rites and Festivals (祭事) == * February – {{ill|Kinen-sai (祈年祭)|ja|祈年祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (Harvest Prayer Festival) * June & December – {{ill|Tsukinami-sai (月次祭)|ja|月次祭|1=Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|12=draft|12=draft}} (Monthly Festival) * October – {{ill|Kannamesai (神嘗祭)|ja|神嘗祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (Offering of First Fruits Festival) * November – {{ill|Niiname-sai (新嘗祭)|ja|新嘗祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (Thanksgiving Harvest Festival) These four major rituals are conducted on-site by a Negi (禰宜, senior priest) in巡回祭典 (巡回祭,巡行 ceremony format). The following six rites are performed remotely (遥祀, Yōshi): * January – {{ill|Saitan-sai (歳旦祭)|ja|歳旦祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (New Year's Festival) * January – {{ill|Genshi-sai (元始祭)|ja|元始祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (Imperial Foundation Festival) * February 11 – {{ill|Kenkoku-kinen-sai (建国記念祭)|ja|建国記念祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (National Foundation Day) * May & August – {{ill|Kaze-no-Hi-no-Matsuri (風日祈祭)|ja|風日祈祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (Wind and Rain Prayers) * December 23 – {{ill|Tenchō-sai (天長祭)|ja|天長祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (Emperor's Birthday Festival) --- == Access (交通) == [[File:Tsukiyominomiyamae Bus Stop.jpg|thumb|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya-mae Bus Stop]] Public Transport: * 10-minute walk (550m) from {{ill|Ise City Station|ja|伊勢市駅|12=draft|12=draft}} (JR & Kintetsu).Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p. 33 * 4-minute walk (360m) from Shindō Bus Stop (三重交通). By Car: * Approx. 5 minutes (2.5km) from Ise Nishi IC (伊勢西IC, Ise Expressway). * Metered parking available near the entrance. --- == References == {{Reflist}} == 参考文献 == * 宇治山田市役所 編『宇治山田市史 上巻』宇治山田市役所、昭和4th year 1月20日、862p. * [[学研パブリッシング]]『伊勢神宮に行こう』Gakken Mook神社紀行セレクションvol.1、[[薗田稔]]監修、学研マーケティング、2013rd year 7月4日、82p.
