{{Shrine |name = Takagawara Shrine |religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Takagawara-jinja 02.jpg|270px]] |location = {{ill|Ise, Mie|ja|伊勢市|12=draft|12=draft}}, Miyago 1-chome 3-19, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|ja|三重県|12=draft|12=draft}} |latitude_deg = 34 | latitude_min = 29 | latitude_sec = 34.5 |longitude_deg = 136 | longitude_min = 42 | longitude_sec = 22.2 |map = Japan Mie |deity = {{ill|Tsukuyomi|ja|月夜見尊御魂|12=draft|12=draft}} |Rank = {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=draft|12=draft}} (small)
{{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮|1=Toyouke Daijingu|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮|12=draft|12=draft}} Subordinate Shrine |founded = Before {{ill|Enryaku|ja|延暦|12=draft|12=draft}} 23 (804) |main_hall = {{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|ja|神明造|12=draft|12=draft}} |other_names = |pilgrimage_sites = |annual_festival = |rituals = {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭|12=draft|12=draft}} }} Takagawara Shrine (高河原神社, ''Takagawara Jinja''Shikinen Sengu Memorial Sengu-kan "[http://www.sengukan.jp/wp-content/themes/sengukan/shrine/area06.php Takagawara Shrine たかがわらじんじゃ>>]" (Accessed October 8, 2013).[[iTV]] "[http://www.yoitokose.jp/ise/encyclopedia/t0010.php Takagawara Shrine | Ise Grand Shrine Encyclopedia | Ise-Shima Travel Yoitokose]" (Accessed October 8, 2013)., also pronounced ''Takakawara Jinja''Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.39Gakken Publishing (2013): p.57) is a [[Shinto]] shrine located in Miyago, {{ill|Ise, Mie|ja|伊勢市|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|ja|三重県|12=draft|12=draft}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|subordinate shrine (sessha/massha)|ja|摂末社|12=draft|12=draft}} of {{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮|1=Toyouke Daijingu|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮|12=draft|12=draft}} (the Outer Shrine of {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮|12=draft|12=draft}}) and classified as a {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=draft|12=draft}}. It Ranks 10th among the 16 subordinate shrines of the Outer ShrineUjiyamada City Hall (1929): pp.11–13.. The shrine is located within the precincts of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|ja|月夜見宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|12=draft|12=draft}}, which is a separate shrine of the Outer ShrineIse Bunka-sha (2008): p.38. == Overview (概要) == Located at {{ill|Mie Prefecture|ja|三重県|12=draft|12=draft}} {{ill|Ise, Mie|ja|伊勢市|12=draft|12=draft}} 1006 Miyago 1-chome式内社研究会 編（1990）：294ページ (modern address: 1-3-19 Miyago, Ise City). The shrine is situated behind and to the right (northeast) of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月夜見宮|12=draft|12=draft}}'s main hall. The shrine grounds are surrounded by a moat on three sides, which is believed to be a remnant of a tributary of the {{ill|Miyagawa River (Mie)|ja|宮川 (三重県)|12=draft|12=draft}}. The enshrined deity is {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto no Mitama|ja|月夜見尊御魂|12=draft|12=draft}} (つきよみのみことのみたま). The shrine is located in Takagawara (高河原), an area near the Miyagawa River, and serves as a {{ill|guardian deity|ja|守護神|12=draft|12=draft}} (守護神) for the land development of the surrounding region. Many ancient texts describe the enshrined deity as the Mitama (spirit) of {{ill|Tsukiyomi|ja|月読|12=draft|12=draft}}. However, the ''{{ill|Shinmei-chō Kōshō Saikō|ja|神名帳考證再考|12=draft|12=draft}}'' (''神名帳考證再考'') claims that the deity is actually {{ill|Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto|ja|倉稲魂命|12=draft|12=draft}} (倉稲魂命), the deity of grain and prosperity. nother text, ''{{ill|Ninomiya Kansa Enkaku Kō|ja|二宮管社沿革考|12=draft|12=draft}}'' (''二宮管社沿革考''), asserts that the original name of the shrine in the ''{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|12=draft|12=draft}}'' (延喜式神名帳) was "{{ill|Kawahara-ni-Masu-Kuninamino-Kami Jinja|ja|川原坐国生神社|12=draft|12=draft}}", proving that its deity is {{ill|Kuninamino-Kami|ja|国生神|12=draft|12=draft}} (国生神), the god of land formation.Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): pp. 295–296 The main hall follows {{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|ja|神明造|12=draft|12=draft}} (神明造, the {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮|12=draft|12=draft}} architectural style) and has a wooden board roof ({{ill|Itabuki|ja|板葺|12=draft|12=draft}}), enclosed by a {{ill|Tamagaki|ja|玉垣|12=draft|12=draft}} (玉垣, sacred fence). Unlike most {{ill|Sessha|ja|摂社|12=draft|12=draft}}・{{ill|Massha|ja|末社|12=draft|12=draft}}・{{ill|Shokan-sha|ja|所管社|12=draft|12=draft}} (摂社・末社・所管社, auxiliary shrines) of {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮|12=draft|12=draft}}, which do not have an offering box ({{ill|Saisenbako|ja|賽銭箱|12=draft|12=draft}})Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p. 26, Takagawara Shrine uniquely has one. == History (歴史) == Based on the definition of a {{ill|Sessha|ja|摂社|12=draft|12=draft}} (auxiliary shrine) within {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮|12=draft|12=draft}}, this shrine was established before the compilation of the ''{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|12=draft|12=draft}}'' in {{ill|Enchō (era)|ja|延長|12=draft|12=draft}} 5 ({{ill|927|ja|927th year|12=draft|12=draft}}).Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p. 22 * The shrine is listed in that text as "{{ill|Kawahara-ni-Masu-Kuninamino-Kami Jinja|ja|川原坐国生神社|12=draft|12=draft}}". * Additionally, it is mentioned as "{{ill|Takagawara-sha|ja|高河原社|12=draft|12=draft}}" in the ''{{ill|Toyuke Daijingu Gishiki-chō|ja|止由気宮儀式帳|12=draft|12=draft}}''. * Since that text dates back to {{ill|Enryaku (era)|ja|延暦|12=draft|12=draft}} 23 ({{ill|804|ja|804th year|12=draft|12=draft}}), this confirms that the shrine existed before that time. According to the ''{{ill|Ruiju Jingi Hongen|ja|類聚神祇本源|12=draft|12=draft}}'', reconstructions were regularly conducted from {{ill|Tokuji (era)|ja|徳治|12=draft|12=draft}} 1 ({{ill|1306|ja|1306年|12=draft|12=draft}}) onwards, under the supervision of a special Zōsai-shi (造替使, shrine reconstruction official).Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p. 296 The ''{{ill|Ninomiya Kansa Enkaku Kō|ja|二宮管社沿革考|12=draft|12=draft}}'' records that: {{quote|"According to the '''Ōei Tōkō Nikki (応永頭工日記)''', on the '''fourth day of the first month in '''{{ill|Ōei (era)|ja|応永|12=draft|12=draft}} 26 ({{ill|1419|ja|1419th year|12=draft|12=draft}})''', a great fire burned down '''{{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月夜見宮|12=draft|12=draft}}''', its small shrine, '''Kawahara-sha (高河原社)''', and '''Imibiya-den (忌火屋殿, the sacred fire hall)'''."}} Thus, the shrine was confirmed to have existed until it burned down on {{ill|January 4 (old calendar)|ja|1月4日 (旧暦)|12=draft|12=draft}}, corresponding to {{ill|January 29|ja|1月29日|12=draft|12=draft}}, 1419 (Julian calendar). --- === Reconstruction in the Edo Period=== After this destruction, the shrine fell into neglect, and by the Early Modern Period (近世), its location was lost. However, thanks to the efforts of {{ill|Kawabe Kiyonaga|ja|河邊精長|12=draft|12=draft}} (also known as {{ill|Ōnakatomi Kiyonaga|ja|大中臣精長|12=draft|12=draft}}), the Grand Chief Priest ({{ill|Ōgūji|ja|大宮司|12=draft|12=draft}}), the shrine was reconstructed on its present site on {{ill|Kanbun (era)|ja|寛文|12=draft|12=draft}} 3, {{ill|July 7 (old calendar)|ja|7月7日 (旧暦)|12=draft|12=draft}} (corresponding to {{ill|August 9|ja|8月9日|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|1663|ja|1663rd year|12=draft|12=draft}} in the Gregorian calendar). * ''{{ill|Shinmei Hisho|ja|神名秘書|12=draft|12=draft}}'' states: "Located in Numaki-go, Yamada Village. East of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月読宮|12=draft|12=draft}}." * ''{{ill|Ruiju Jingi Hongen|ja|類聚神祇本源|12=draft|12=draft}}'' states: "East of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月読宮|12=draft|12=draft}}, within the same {{ill|Tamagaki|ja|玉垣|12=draft|12=draft}} fence." * ''{{ill|Ninomiya Kansa Enkaku Kō|ja|二宮管社沿革考|12=draft|12=draft}}'' claims that the original shrine site was actually the present-day {{ill|Suhara Taisha|ja|須原大社|12=draft|12=draft}} in Ichinoki, Ise City.Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p. 295 --- === Reconstruction in the Modern Period=== * In {{ill|1911|ja|1911th year|12=draft|12=draft}} ({{ill|Meiji|ja|明治|1=Meiji era|12=draft|12=draft}} 44), the shrine was rebuilt.Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): p. 12 * In {{ill|1938|ja|1938th year|12=draft|12=draft}} ({{ill|Shōwa|ja|昭和|12=draft|12=draft}} 13), it was rebuilt again. * In {{ill|1957|ja|1957th year|12=draft|12=draft}} (Shōwa 32), a major renovation was completed, and a sacred transfer ritual ({{ill|Sengyo|ja|遷御|12=draft|12=draft}}) was performed 20 years later.Sakurai (1991): p. 298 --- == Rites and Festivals (祭事) == * February – {{ill|Kinen-sai (祈年祭)|ja|祈年祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (Harvest Prayer Festival) * June & December – {{ill|Tsukinami-sai (月次祭)|ja|月次祭|1=Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|12=draft|12=draft}} (Monthly Festival) * October – {{ill|Kannamesai (神嘗祭)|ja|神嘗祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (Offering of First Fruits Festival) * November – {{ill|Niiname-sai (新嘗祭)|ja|新嘗祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (Thanksgiving Harvest Festival) These four major rituals are conducted on-site by a Negi (禰宜, senior priest) in巡回祭典 (巡回祭,巡行 ceremony format). The following six rites are performed remotely (遥祀, Yōshi): * January – {{ill|Saitan-sai (歳旦祭)|ja|歳旦祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (New Year's Festival) * January – {{ill|Genshi-sai (元始祭)|ja|元始祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (Imperial Foundation Festival) * February 11 – {{ill|Kenkoku-kinen-sai (建国記念祭)|ja|建国記念祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (National Foundation Day) * May & August – {{ill|Kaze-no-Hi-no-Matsuri (風日祈祭)|ja|風日祈祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (Wind and Rain Prayers) * December 23 – {{ill|Tenchō-sai (天長祭)|ja|天長祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (Emperor's Birthday Festival) --- == Access (交通) == [[File:Tsukiyominomiyamae Bus Stop.jpg|thumb|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya-mae Bus Stop]] Public Transport: * 10-minute walk (550m) from {{ill|Ise City Station|ja|伊勢市駅|12=draft|12=draft}} (JR & Kintetsu).Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p. 33 * 4-minute walk (360m) from Shindō Bus Stop (三重交通). {{Shrine |name = Takagawara Shrine |religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Takagawara-jinja 02.jpg|270px]] |location = {{ill|Ise, Mie|ja|伊勢市|12=draft|12=draft}}, Miyago 1-chome 3-19, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|ja|三重県|12=draft|12=draft}} |latitude_deg = 34 | latitude_min = 29 | latitude_sec = 34.5 |longitude_deg = 136 | longitude_min = 42 | longitude_sec = 22.2 |map = Japan Mie |deity = {{ill|Tsukuyomi|ja|月夜見尊御魂|12=draft|12=draft}} |Rank = {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=draft|12=draft}} (small)
{{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮|1=Toyouke Daijingu|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮|12=draft|12=draft}} Subordinate Shrine |founded = Before {{ill|Enryaku|ja|延暦|12=draft|12=draft}} 23 (804) |main_hall = {{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|ja|神明造|12=draft|12=draft}} |other_names = |pilgrimage_sites = |annual_festival = |rituals = {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭|12=draft|12=draft}} }} Takagawara Shrine (高河原神社, ''Takagawara Jinja''Shikinen Sengu Memorial Sengu-kan "[http://www.sengukan.jp/wp-content/themes/sengukan/shrine/area06.php Takagawara Shrine たかがわらじんじゃ>>]" (Accessed October 8, 2013).[[iTV]] "[http://www.yoitokose.jp/ise/encyclopedia/t0010.php Takagawara Shrine | Ise Grand Shrine Encyclopedia | Ise-Shima Travel Yoitokose]" (Accessed October 8, 2013)., also pronounced ''Takakawara Jinja''Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.39Gakken Publishing (2013): p.57) is a [[Shinto]] shrine located in Miyago, {{ill|Ise, Mie|ja|伊勢市|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|ja|三重県|12=draft|12=draft}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|subordinate shrine (sessha/massha)|ja|摂末社|12=draft|12=draft}} of {{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮|1=Toyouke Daijingu|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮|12=draft|12=draft}} (the Outer Shrine of {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮|12=draft|12=draft}}) and classified as a {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=draft|12=draft}}. It Ranks 10th among the 16 subordinate shrines of the Outer ShrineUjiyamada City Hall (1929): pp.11–13.. The shrine is located within the precincts of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|ja|月夜見宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|12=draft|12=draft}}, which is a separate shrine of the Outer ShrineIse Bunka-sha (2008): p.38. == Overview (概要) == Located at {{ill|Mie Prefecture|ja|三重県|12=draft|12=draft}} {{ill|Ise, Mie|ja|伊勢市|12=draft|12=draft}} 1006 Miyago 1-chome式内社研究会 編（1990）：294ページ (modern address: 1-3-19 Miyago, Ise City). The shrine is situated behind and to the right (northeast) of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月夜見宮|12=draft|12=draft}}'s main hall. The shrine grounds are surrounded by a moat on three sides, which is believed to be a remnant of a tributary of the {{ill|Miyagawa River (Mie)|ja|宮川 (三重県)|12=draft|12=draft}}. The enshrined deity is {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto no Mitama|ja|月夜見尊御魂|12=draft|12=draft}} (つきよみのみことのみたま). The shrine is located in Takagawara (高河原), an area near the Miyagawa River, and serves as a {{ill|guardian deity|ja|守護神|12=draft|12=draft}} (守護神) for the land development of the surrounding region. Many ancient texts describe the enshrined deity as the Mitama (spirit) of {{ill|Tsukiyomi|ja|月読|12=draft|12=draft}}. However, the ''{{ill|Shinmei-chō Kōshō Saikō|ja|神名帳考證再考|12=draft|12=draft}}'' (''神名帳考證再考'') claims that the deity is actually {{ill|Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto|ja|倉稲魂命|12=draft|12=draft}} (倉稲魂命), the deity of grain and prosperity. nother text, ''{{ill|Ninomiya Kansa Enkaku Kō|ja|二宮管社沿革考|12=draft|12=draft}}'' (''二宮管社沿革考''), asserts that the original name of the shrine in the ''{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|12=draft|12=draft}}'' (延喜式神名帳) was "{{ill|Kawahara-ni-Masu-Kuninamino-Kami Jinja|ja|川原坐国生神社|12=draft|12=draft}}", proving that its deity is {{ill|Kuninamino-Kami|ja|国生神|12=draft|12=draft}} (国生神), the god of land formation.Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): pp. 295–296 The main hall follows {{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|ja|神明造|12=draft|12=draft}} (神明造, the {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮|12=draft|12=draft}} architectural style) and has a wooden board roof ({{ill|Itabuki|ja|板葺|12=draft|12=draft}}), enclosed by a {{ill|Tamagaki|ja|玉垣|12=draft|12=draft}} (玉垣, sacred fence). Unlike most {{ill|Sessha|ja|摂社|12=draft|12=draft}}・{{ill|Massha|ja|末社|12=draft|12=draft}}・{{ill|Shokan-sha|ja|所管社|12=draft|12=draft}} (摂社・末社・所管社, auxiliary shrines) of {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮|12=draft|12=draft}}, which do not have an offering box ({{ill|Saisenbako|ja|賽銭箱|12=draft|12=draft}})Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p. 26, Takagawara Shrine uniquely has one. == History (歴史) == Based on the definition of a {{ill|Sessha|ja|摂社|12=draft|12=draft}} (auxiliary shrine) within {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮|12=draft|12=draft}}, this shrine was established before the compilation of the ''{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|12=draft|12=draft}}'' in {{ill|Enchō (era)|ja|延長|12=draft|12=draft}} 5 ({{ill|927|ja|927th year|12=draft|12=draft}}).Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p. 22 * The shrine is listed in that text as "{{ill|Kawahara-ni-Masu-Kuninamino-Kami Jinja|ja|川原坐国生神社|12=draft|12=draft}}". * Additionally, it is mentioned as "{{ill|Takagawara-sha|ja|高河原社|12=draft|12=draft}}" in the ''{{ill|Toyuke Daijingu Gishiki-chō|ja|止由気宮儀式帳|12=draft|12=draft}}''. * Since that text dates back to {{ill|Enryaku (era)|ja|延暦|12=draft|12=draft}} 23 ({{ill|804|ja|804th year|12=draft|12=draft}}), this confirms that the shrine existed before that time. According to the ''{{ill|Ruiju Jingi Hongen|ja|類聚神祇本源|12=draft|12=draft}}'', reconstructions were regularly conducted from {{ill|Tokuji (era)|ja|徳治|12=draft|12=draft}} 1 ({{ill|1306|ja|1306年|12=draft|12=draft}}) onwards, under the supervision of a special Zōsai-shi (造替使, shrine reconstruction official).Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p. 296 The ''{{ill|Ninomiya Kansa Enkaku Kō|ja|二宮管社沿革考|12=draft|12=draft}}'' records that: {{quote|"According to the '''Ōei Tōkō Nikki (応永頭工日記)''', on the '''fourth day of the first month in '''{{ill|Ōei (era)|ja|応永|12=draft|12=draft}} 26 ({{ill|1419|ja|1419th year|12=draft|12=draft}})''', a great fire burned down '''{{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月夜見宮|12=draft|12=draft}}''', its small shrine, '''Kawahara-sha (高河原社)''', and '''Imibiya-den (忌火屋殿, the sacred fire hall)'''."}} Thus, the shrine was confirmed to have existed until it burned down on {{ill|January 4 (old calendar)|ja|1月4日 (旧暦)|12=draft|12=draft}}, corresponding to {{ill|January 29|ja|1月29日|12=draft|12=draft}}, 1419 (Julian calendar). --- === Reconstruction in the Edo Period=== After this destruction, the shrine fell into neglect, and by the Early Modern Period (近世), its location was lost. However, thanks to the efforts of {{ill|Kawabe Kiyonaga|ja|河邊精長|12=draft|12=draft}} (also known as {{ill|Ōnakatomi Kiyonaga|ja|大中臣精長|12=draft|12=draft}}), the Grand Chief Priest ({{ill|Ōgūji|ja|大宮司|12=draft|12=draft}}), the shrine was reconstructed on its present site on {{ill|Kanbun (era)|ja|寛文|12=draft|12=draft}} 3, {{ill|July 7 (old calendar)|ja|7月7日 (旧暦)|12=draft|12=draft}} (corresponding to {{ill|August 9|ja|8月9日|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|1663|ja|1663rd year|12=draft|12=draft}} in the Gregorian calendar). * ''{{ill|Shinmei Hisho|ja|神名秘書|12=draft|12=draft}}'' states: "Located in Numaki-go, Yamada Village. East of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月読宮|12=draft|12=draft}}." * ''{{ill|Ruiju Jingi Hongen|ja|類聚神祇本源|12=draft|12=draft}}'' states: "East of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月読宮|12=draft|12=draft}}, within the same {{ill|Tamagaki|ja|玉垣|12=draft|12=draft}} fence." * ''{{ill|Ninomiya Kansa Enkaku Kō|ja|二宮管社沿革考|12=draft|12=draft}}'' claims that the original shrine site was actually the present-day {{ill|Suhara Taisha|ja|須原大社|12=draft|12=draft}} in Ichinoki, Ise City.Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p. 295 --- === Reconstruction in the Modern Period=== * In {{ill|1911|ja|1911th year|12=draft|12=draft}} ({{ill|Meiji|ja|明治|1=Meiji era|12=draft|12=draft}} 44), the shrine was rebuilt.Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): p. 12 * In {{ill|1938|ja|1938th year|12=draft|12=draft}} ({{ill|Shōwa|ja|昭和|12=draft|12=draft}} 13), it was rebuilt again. * In {{ill|1957|ja|1957th year|12=draft|12=draft}} (Shōwa 32), a major renovation was completed, and a sacred transfer ritual ({{ill|Sengyo|ja|遷御|12=draft|12=draft}}) was performed 20 years later.Sakurai (1991): p. 298 --- == Rites and Festivals (祭事) == * February – {{ill|Kinen-sai (祈年祭)|ja|祈年祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (Harvest Prayer Festival) * June & December – {{ill|Tsukinami-sai (月次祭)|ja|月次祭|1=Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|12=draft|12=draft}} (Monthly Festival) * October – {{ill|Kannamesai (神嘗祭)|ja|神嘗祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (Offering of First Fruits Festival) * November – {{ill|Niiname-sai (新嘗祭)|ja|新嘗祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (Thanksgiving Harvest Festival) These four major rituals are conducted on-site by a Negi (禰宜, senior priest) in巡回祭典 (巡回祭,巡行 ceremony format). The following six rites are performed remotely (遥祀, Yōshi): * January – {{ill|Saitan-sai (歳旦祭)|ja|歳旦祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (New Year's Festival) * January – {{ill|Genshi-sai (元始祭)|ja|元始祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (Imperial Foundation Festival) * February 11 – {{ill|Kenkoku-kinen-sai (建国記念祭)|ja|建国記念祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (National Foundation Day) * May & August – {{ill|Kaze-no-Hi-no-Matsuri (風日祈祭)|ja|風日祈祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (Wind and Rain Prayers) * December 23 – {{ill|Tenchō-sai (天長祭)|ja|天長祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (Emperor's Birthday Festival) --- == Access (交通) == [[File:Tsukiyominomiyamae Bus Stop.jpg|thumb|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya-mae Bus Stop]] Public Transport: * 10-minute walk (550m) from {{ill|Ise City Station|ja|伊勢市駅|12=draft|12=draft}} (JR & Kintetsu).Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p. 33 * 4-minute walk (360m) from Shindō Bus Stop (三重交通). By Car: * Approx. 5 minutes (2.5km) from Ise Nishi IC (伊勢西IC, Ise Expressway). * Metered parking available near the entrance. --- == References == {{Reflist}} == 参考文献 == * 宇治山田市役所 編『宇治山田市史 上巻』宇治山田市役所、昭和4th year 1月20日、862p. * [[学研パブリッシング]]『伊勢神宮に行こう』Gakken Mook神社紀行セレクションvol.1、[[薗田稔]]監修、学研マーケティング、2013rd year 7月4日、82p. ISBN 978-4-05-610047-1 * [[櫻井勝之進]]『伊勢神宮の祖型と展開』[[国書刊行会]]、平成3rd year 11月30日、318p. ISBN 4-336-03296-3 * 式内社研究会 編『式内社調査報告 第六巻 東海道1』[[Kogakkan University]]出版部、平成2nd year 2月28日、690p. ISBN 4-87644-080-8 * 『お伊勢さん125社めぐり』別冊『伊勢人』、[[伊勢文化舎]]、平成20th year 12月23日、151p. ISBN 978-4-900759-37-4 == See Also == * {{ill|List of Shikinaisha in Ise Province|ja|伊勢国の式内社一覧|12=draft|12=draft}} * {{ill|List of 125 Shrines of Ise|ja|神宮125社の一覧|lt=List of 125 Shrines of Ise|1=List of Shikinaisha in Ise Province|3=伊勢国の式内社一覧|12=draft|12=draft}} == External Links == * [http://www.jingukaikan.jp/125mairi/m02/0203.html 高河原神社（たかがわらじんじゃ）] - 財団法人伊勢神宮崇敬会 {{125 Shrines of Ise}} {{draft categories| }} {{draft categories| [[Category:Shrines in Mie Prefecture]] [[Category:Subordinate shrines of Toyouke Daijingu]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Japan]] [[Category:Ise Grand Shrine]] [[Category:Completion tier 5]] [[Category:125 Shrines of Ise]] [[Category:11]] [[Category:高河原神社]] [[Category:伊勢国の式内社]] [[Category:摂末社]] [[Category:伊勢市の神社]] [[Category:category refresh]] [[Category:New]] [[Category:qq]] }} [[ja:高河原神社]] [[sn:Takagawara Shrine]] [[sn:akagawara Shrine]]

Many ancient texts describe the enshrined deity as the Mitama (spirit) of {{ill|Tsukiyomi|ja|月読|12=draft|12=draft}}. However, the ''{{ill|Shinmei-chō Kōshō Saikō|ja|神名帳考證再考|12=draft|12=draft}}'' (''神名帳考證再考'') claims that the deity is actually {{ill|Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto|ja|倉稲魂命|12=draft|12=draft}} (倉稲魂命), the deity of grain and prosperity. nother text, ''{{ill|Ninomiya Kansa Enkaku Kō|ja|二宮管社沿革考|12=draft|12=draft}}'' (''二宮管社沿革考''), asserts that the original name of the shrine in the ''{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|12=draft|12=draft}}'' (延喜式神名帳) was "{{ill|Kawahara-ni-Masu-Kuninamino-Kami Jinja|ja|川原坐国生神社|12=draft|12=draft}}", proving that its deity is {{ill|Kuninamino-Kami|ja|国生神|12=draft|12=draft}} (国生神), the god of land formation.Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): pp. 295–296 The main hall follows {{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|ja|神明造|12=draft|12=draft}} (神明造, the {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮|12=draft|12=draft}} architectural style) and has a wooden board roof ({{ill|Itabuki|ja|板葺|12=draft|12=draft}}), enclosed by a {{ill|Tamagaki|ja|玉垣|12=draft|12=draft}} (玉垣, sacred fence). Unlike most {{ill|Sessha|ja|摂社|12=draft|12=draft}}・{{ill|Massha|ja|末社|12=draft|12=draft}}・{{ill|Shokan-sha|ja|所管社|12=draft|12=draft}} (摂社・末社・所管社, auxiliary shrines) of {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮|12=draft|12=draft}}, which do not have an offering box ({{ill|Saisenbako|ja|賽銭箱|12=draft|12=draft}})Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p. 26, Takagawara Shrine uniquely has one. == History (歴史) == Based on the definition of a {{ill|Sessha|ja|摂社|12=draft|12=draft}} (auxiliary shrine) within {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮|12=draft|12=draft}}, this shrine was established before the compilation of the ''{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|12=draft|12=draft}}'' in {{ill|Enchō (era)|ja|延長|12=draft|12=draft}} 5 ({{ill|927|ja|927th year|12=draft|12=draft}}).Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p. 22 * The shrine is listed in that text as "{{ill|Kawahara-ni-Masu-Kuninamino-Kami Jinja|ja|川原坐国生神社|12=draft|12=draft}}". * Additionally, it is mentioned as "{{ill|Takagawara-sha|ja|高河原社|12=draft|12=draft}}" in the ''{{ill|Toyuke Daijingu Gishiki-chō|ja|止由気宮儀式帳|12=draft|12=draft}}''. * Since that text dates back to {{ill|Enryaku (era)|ja|延暦|12=draft|12=draft}} 23 ({{ill|804|ja|804th year|12=draft|12=draft}}), this confirms that the shrine existed before that time. According to the ''{{ill|Ruiju Jingi Hongen|ja|類聚神祇本源|12=draft|12=draft}}'', reconstructions were regularly conducted from {{ill|Tokuji (era)|ja|徳治|12=draft|12=draft}} 1 ({{ill|1306|ja|1306年|12=draft|12=draft}}) onwards, under the supervision of a special Zōsai-shi (造替使, shrine reconstruction official).Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p. 296 The ''{{ill|Ninomiya Kansa Enkaku Kō|ja|二宮管社沿革考|12=draft|12=draft}}'' records that: {{quote|"According to the '''Ōei Tōkō Nikki (応永頭工日記)''', on the '''fourth day of the first month in '''{{ill|Ōei (era)|ja|応永|12=draft|12=draft}} 26 ({{ill|1419|ja|1419th year|12=draft|12=draft}})''', a great fire burned down '''{{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月夜見宮|12=draft|12=draft}}''', its small shrine, '''Kawahara-sha (高河原社)''', and '''Imibiya-den (忌火屋殿, the sacred fire hall)'''."}} Thus, the shrine was confirmed to have existed until it burned down on {{ill|January 4 (old calendar)|ja|1月4日 (旧暦)|12=draft|12=draft}}, corresponding to {{ill|January 29|ja|1月29日|12=draft|12=draft}}, 1419 (Julian calendar). --- === Reconstruction in the Edo Period=== After this destruction, the shrine fell into neglect, and by the Early Modern Period (近世), its location was lost. However, thanks to the efforts of {{ill|Kawabe Kiyonaga|ja|河邊精長|12=draft|12=draft}} (also known as {{ill|Ōnakatomi Kiyonaga|ja|大中臣精長|12=draft|12=draft}}), the Grand Chief Priest ({{ill|Ōgūji|ja|大宮司|12=draft|12=draft}}), the shrine was reconstructed on its present site on {{ill|Kanbun (era)|ja|寛文|12=draft|12=draft}} 3, {{ill|July 7 (old calendar)|ja|7月7日 (旧暦)|12=draft|12=draft}} (corresponding to {{ill|August 9|ja|8月9日|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|1663|ja|1663rd year|12=draft|12=draft}} in the Gregorian calendar). * ''{{ill|Shinmei Hisho|ja|神名秘書|12=draft|12=draft}}'' states: "Located in Numaki-go, Yamada Village. East of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月読宮|12=draft|12=draft}}." * ''{{ill|Ruiju Jingi Hongen|ja|類聚神祇本源|12=draft|12=draft}}'' states: "East of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月読宮|12=draft|12=draft}}, within the same {{ill|Tamagaki|ja|玉垣|12=draft|12=draft}} fence." * ''{{ill|Ninomiya Kansa Enkaku Kō|ja|二宮管社沿革考|12=draft|12=draft}}'' claims that the original shrine site was actually the present-day {{ill|Suhara Taisha|ja|須原大社|12=draft|12=draft}} in Ichinoki, Ise City.Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p. 295 --- === Reconstruction in the Modern Period=== * In {{ill|1911|ja|1911th year|12=draft|12=draft}} ({{ill|Meiji|ja|明治|1=Meiji era|12=draft|12=draft}} 44), the shrine was rebuilt.Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): p. 12 * In {{ill|1938|ja|1938th year|12=draft|12=draft}} ({{ill|Shōwa|ja|昭和|12=draft|12=draft}} 13), it was rebuilt again. * In {{ill|1957|ja|1957th year|12=draft|12=draft}} (Shōwa 32), a major renovation was completed, and a sacred transfer ritual ({{ill|Sengyo|ja|遷御|12=draft|12=draft}}) was performed 20 years later.Sakurai (1991): p. 298 --- == Rites and Festivals (祭事) == * February – {{ill|Kinen-sai (祈年祭)|ja|祈年祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (Harvest Prayer Festival) * June & December – {{ill|Tsukinami-sai (月次祭)|ja|月次祭|1=Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|12=draft|12=draft}} (Monthly Festival) * October – {{ill|Kannamesai (神嘗祭)|ja|神嘗祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (Offering of First Fruits Festival) * November – {{ill|Niiname-sai (新嘗祭)|ja|新嘗祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (Thanksgiving Harvest Festival) These four major rituals are conducted on-site by a Negi (禰宜, senior priest) in巡回祭典 (巡回祭,巡行 ceremony format). The following six rites are performed remotely (遥祀, Yōshi): * January – {{ill|Saitan-sai (歳旦祭)|ja|歳旦祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (New Year's Festival) * January – {{ill|Genshi-sai (元始祭)|ja|元始祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (Imperial Foundation Festival) * February 11 – {{ill|Kenkoku-kinen-sai (建国記念祭)|ja|建国記念祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (National Foundation Day) * May & August – {{ill|Kaze-no-Hi-no-Matsuri (風日祈祭)|ja|風日祈祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (Wind and Rain Prayers) * December 23 – {{ill|Tenchō-sai (天長祭)|ja|天長祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (Emperor's Birthday Festival) --- == Access (交通) == [[File:Tsukiyominomiyamae Bus Stop.jpg|thumb|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya-mae Bus Stop]] Public Transport: * 10-minute walk (550m) from {{ill|Ise City Station|ja|伊勢市駅|12=draft|12=draft}} (JR & Kintetsu).Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p. 33 * 4-minute walk (360m) from Shindō Bus Stop (三重交通). By Car: * Approx. 5 minutes (2.5km) from Ise Nishi IC (伊勢西IC, Ise Expressway). * Metered parking available near the entrance. --- == References == {{Reflist}} == 参考文献 == * 宇治山田市役所 編『宇治山田市史 上巻』宇治山田市役所、昭和4th year 1月20日、862p. * [[学研パブリッシング]]『伊勢神宮に行こう』Gakken Mook神社紀行セレクションvol.1、[[薗田稔]]監修、学研マーケティング、2013rd year 7月4日、82p. ISBN 978-4-05-610047-1 * [[櫻井勝之進]]『伊勢神宮の祖型と展開』[[国書刊行会]]、平成3rd year 11月30日、318p. ISBN 4-336-03296-3 * 式内社研究会 編『式内社調査報告 第六巻 東海道1』[[Kogakkan University]]出版部、平成2nd year 2月28日、690p. ISBN 4-87644-080-8 * 『お伊勢さん125社めぐり』別冊『伊勢人』、[[伊勢文化舎]]、平成20th year 12月23日、151p. ISBN 978-4-900759-37-4 == See Also == * {{ill|List of Shikinaisha in Ise Province|ja|伊勢国の式内社一覧|12=draft|12=draft}} * {{ill|List of 125 Shrines of Ise|ja|神宮125社の一覧|lt=List of 125 Shrines of Ise|1=List of Shikinaisha in Ise Province|3=伊勢国の式内社一覧|12=draft|12=draft}} == External Links == * [http://www.jingukaikan.jp/125mairi/m02/0203.html 高河原神社（たかがわらじんじゃ）] - 財団法人伊勢神宮崇敬会 {{125 Shrines of Ise}} {{draft categories| }} {{draft categories| [[Category:Shrines in Mie Prefecture]] [[Category:Subordinate shrines of Toyouke Daijingu]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Japan]] [[Category:Ise Grand Shrine]] [[Category:Completion tier 5]] [[Category:125 Shrines of Ise]] [[Category:11]] [[Category:高河原神社]] [[Category:伊勢国の式内社]] [[Category:摂末社]] [[Category:伊勢市の神社]] [[Category:category refresh]] [[Category:New]] [[Category:qq]] }} [[ja:高河原神社]] [[sn:Takagawara Shrine]] [[sn:akagawara Shrine]]

{{Shrine |name = Takagawara Shrine |religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Takagawara-jinja 02.jpg|270px]] |location = {{ill|Ise, Mie|ja|伊勢市|12=draft|12=draft}}, Miyago 1-chome 3-19, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|ja|三重県|12=draft|12=draft}} |latitude_deg = 34 | latitude_min = 29 | latitude_sec = 34.5 |longitude_deg = 136 | longitude_min = 42 | longitude_sec = 22.2 |map = Japan Mie |deity = {{ill|Tsukuyomi|ja|月夜見尊御魂|12=draft|12=draft}} |Rank = {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=draft|12=draft}} (small)
{{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮|1=Toyouke Daijingu|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮|12=draft|12=draft}} Subordinate Shrine |founded = Before {{ill|Enryaku|ja|延暦|12=draft|12=draft}} 23 (804) |main_hall = {{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|ja|神明造|12=draft|12=draft}} |other_names = |pilgrimage_sites = |annual_festival = |rituals = {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭|12=draft|12=draft}} }} Takagawara Shrine (高河原神社, ''Takagawara Jinja''Shikinen Sengu Memorial Sengu-kan "[http://www.sengukan.jp/wp-content/themes/sengukan/shrine/area06.php Takagawara Shrine たかがわらじんじゃ>>]" (Accessed October 8, 2013).[[iTV]] "[http://www.yoitokose.jp/ise/encyclopedia/t0010.php Takagawara Shrine | Ise Grand Shrine Encyclopedia | Ise-Shima Travel Yoitokose]" (Accessed October 8, 2013)., also pronounced ''Takakawara Jinja''Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.39Gakken Publishing (2013): p.57) is a [[Shinto]] shrine located in Miyago, {{ill|Ise, Mie|ja|伊勢市|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|ja|三重県|12=draft|12=draft}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|subordinate shrine (sessha/massha)|ja|摂末社|12=draft|12=draft}} of {{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮|1=Toyouke Daijingu|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮|12=draft|12=draft}} (the Outer Shrine of {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮|12=draft|12=draft}}) and classified as a {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=draft|12=draft}}. It Ranks 10th among the 16 subordinate shrines of the Outer ShrineUjiyamada City Hall (1929): pp.11–13.. The shrine is located within the precincts of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|ja|月夜見宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|12=draft|12=draft}}, which is a separate shrine of the Outer ShrineIse Bunka-sha (2008): p.38. == Overview (概要) == Located at {{ill|Mie Prefecture|ja|三重県|12=draft|12=draft}} {{ill|Ise, Mie|ja|伊勢市|12=draft|12=draft}} 1006 Miyago 1-chome式内社研究会 編（1990）：294ページ (modern address: 1-3-19 Miyago, Ise City). The shrine is situated behind and to the right (northeast) of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月夜見宮|12=draft|12=draft}}'s main hall. The shrine grounds are surrounded by a moat on three sides, which is believed to be a remnant of a tributary of the {{ill|Miyagawa River (Mie)|ja|宮川 (三重県)|12=draft|12=draft}}. The enshrined deity is {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto no Mitama|ja|月夜見尊御魂|12=draft|12=draft}} (つきよみのみことのみたま). The shrine is located in Takagawara (高河原), an area near the Miyagawa River, and serves as a {{ill|guardian deity|ja|守護神|12=draft|12=draft}} (守護神) for the land development of the surrounding region. Many ancient texts describe the enshrined deity as the Mitama (spirit) of {{ill|Tsukiyomi|ja|月読|12=draft|12=draft}}. According to the ''{{ill|Ruiju Jingi Hongen|ja|類聚神祇本源|12=draft|12=draft}}'', reconstructions were regularly conducted from {{ill|Tokuji (era)|ja|徳治|12=draft|12=draft}} 1 ({{ill|1306|ja|1306年|12=draft|12=draft}}) onwards, under the supervision of a special Zōsai-shi (造替使, shrine reconstruction official).Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p. 296 The ''{{ill|Ninomiya Kansa Enkaku Kō|ja|二宮管社沿革考|12=draft|12=draft}}'' records that: {{quote|"According to the '''Ōei Tōkō Nikki (応永頭工日記)''', on the '''fourth day of the first month in '''{{ill|Ōei (era)|ja|応永|12=draft|12=draft}} 26 ({{ill|1419|ja|1419th year|12=draft|12=draft}})''', a great fire burned down '''{{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月夜見宮|12=draft|12=draft}}''', its small shrine, '''Kawahara-sha (高河原社)''', and '''Imibiya-den (忌火屋殿, the sacred fire hall)'''."}} Thus, the shrine was confirmed to have existed until it burned down on {{ill|January 4 (old calendar)|ja|1月4日 (旧暦)|12=draft|12=draft}}, corresponding to {{ill|January 29|ja|1月29日|12=draft|12=draft}}, 1419 (Julian calendar). --- === Reconstruction in the Edo Period=== After this destruction, the shrine fell into neglect, and by the Early Modern Period (近世), its location was lost. However, thanks to the efforts of {{ill|Kawabe Kiyonaga|ja|河邊精長|12=draft|12=draft}} (also known as {{ill|Ōnakatomi Kiyonaga|ja|大中臣精長|12=draft|12=draft}}), the Grand Chief Priest ({{ill|Ōgūji|ja|大宮司|12=draft|12=draft}}), the shrine was reconstructed on its present site on {{ill|Kanbun (era)|ja|寛文|12=draft|12=draft}} 3, {{ill|July 7 (old calendar)|ja|7月7日 (旧暦)|12=draft|12=draft}} (corresponding to {{ill|August 9|ja|8月9日|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|1663|ja|1663rd year|12=draft|12=draft}} in the Gregorian calendar). * ''{{ill|Shinmei Hisho|ja|神名秘書|12=draft|12=draft}}'' states: "Located in Numaki-go, Yamada Village. East of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月読宮|12=draft|12=draft}}." * ''{{ill|Ruiju Jingi Hongen|ja|類聚神祇本源|12=draft|12=draft}}'' states: "East of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月読宮|12=draft|12=draft}}, within the same {{ill|Tamagaki|ja|玉垣|12=draft|12=draft}} fence." * ''{{ill|Ninomiya Kansa Enkaku Kō|ja|二宮管社沿革考|12=draft|12=draft}}'' claims that the original shrine site was actually the present-day {{ill|Suhara Taisha|ja|須原大社|12=draft|12=draft}} in Ichinoki, Ise City.Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p. 295 --- === Reconstruction in the Modern Period=== * In {{ill|1911|ja|1911th year|12=draft|12=draft}} ({{ill|Meiji|ja|明治|1=Meiji era|12=draft|12=draft}} 44), the shrine was rebuilt.Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): p. 12 * In {{ill|1938|ja|1938th year|12=draft|12=draft}} ({{ill|Shōwa|ja|昭和|12=draft|12=draft}} 13), it was rebuilt again. * In {{ill|1957|ja|1957th year|12=draft|12=draft}} (Shōwa 32), a major renovation was completed, and a sacred transfer ritual ({{ill|Sengyo|ja|遷御|12=draft|12=draft}}) was performed 20 years later.Sakurai (1991): p. 298 --- == Rites and Festivals (祭事) == * February – {{ill|Kinen-sai (祈年祭)|ja|祈年祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (Harvest Prayer Festival) * June & December – {{ill|Tsukinami-sai (月次祭)|ja|月次祭|1=Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|12=draft|12=draft}} (Monthly Festival) * October – {{ill|Kannamesai (神嘗祭)|ja|神嘗祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (Offering of First Fruits Festival) * November – {{ill|Niiname-sai (新嘗祭)|ja|新嘗祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (Thanksgiving Harvest Festival) These four major rituals are conducted on-site by a Negi (禰宜, senior priest) in巡回祭典 (巡回祭,巡行 ceremony format). The following six rites are performed remotely (遥祀, Yōshi): * January – {{ill|Saitan-sai (歳旦祭)|ja|歳旦祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (New Year's Festival) * January – {{ill|Genshi-sai (元始祭)|ja|元始祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (Imperial Foundation Festival) * February 11 – {{ill|Kenkoku-kinen-sai (建国記念祭)|ja|建国記念祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (National Foundation Day) * May & August – {{ill|Kaze-no-Hi-no-Matsuri (風日祈祭)|ja|風日祈祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (Wind and Rain Prayers) * December 23 – {{ill|Tenchō-sai (天長祭)|ja|天長祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (Emperor's Birthday Festival) --- == Access (交通) == [[File:Tsukiyominomiyamae Bus Stop.jpg|thumb|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya-mae Bus Stop]] Public Transport: * 10-minute walk (550m) from {{ill|Ise City Station|ja|伊勢市駅|12=draft|12=draft}} (JR & Kintetsu).Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p. 33 * 4-minute walk (360m) from Shindō Bus Stop (三重交通). By Car: * Approx. 5 minutes (2.5km) from Ise Nishi IC (伊勢西IC, Ise Expressway). * Metered parking available near the entrance. --- == References == {{Reflist}} == 参考文献 == * 宇治山田市役所 編『宇治山田市史 上巻』宇治山田市役所、昭和4th year 1月20日、862p. * [[学研パブリッシング]]『伊勢神宮に行こう』Gakken Mook神社紀行セレクションvol.1、[[薗田稔]]監修、学研マーケティング、2013rd year 7月4日、82p. {{Shrine |name = Takagawara Shrine |religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Takagawara-jinja 02.jpg|270px]] |location = {{ill|Ise, Mie|ja|伊勢市|12=draft|12=draft}}, Miyago 1-chome 3-19, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|ja|三重県|12=draft|12=draft}} |latitude_deg = 34 | latitude_min = 29 | latitude_sec = 34.5 |longitude_deg = 136 | longitude_min = 42 | longitude_sec = 22.2 |map = Japan Mie |deity = {{ill|Tsukuyomi|ja|月夜見尊御魂|12=draft|12=draft}} |Rank = {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=draft|12=draft}} (small)
{{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮|1=Toyouke Daijingu|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮|12=draft|12=draft}} Subordinate Shrine |founded = Before {{ill|Enryaku|ja|延暦|12=draft|12=draft}} 23 (804) |main_hall = {{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|ja|神明造|12=draft|12=draft}} |other_names = |pilgrimage_sites = |annual_festival = |rituals = {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭|12=draft|12=draft}} }} Takagawara Shrine (高河原神社, ''Takagawara Jinja''Shikinen Sengu Memorial Sengu-kan "[http://www.sengukan.jp/wp-content/themes/sengukan/shrine/area06.php Takagawara Shrine たかがわらじんじゃ>>]" (Accessed October 8, 2013).[[iTV]] "[http://www.yoitokose.jp/ise/encyclopedia/t0010.php Takagawara Shrine | Ise Grand Shrine Encyclopedia | Ise-Shima Travel Yoitokose]" (Accessed October 8, 2013)., also pronounced ''Takakawara Jinja''Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.39Gakken Publishing (2013): p.57) is a [[Shinto]] shrine located in Miyago, {{ill|Ise, Mie|ja|伊勢市|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|ja|三重県|12=draft|12=draft}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|subordinate shrine (sessha/massha)|ja|摂末社|12=draft|12=draft}} of {{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮|1=Toyouke Daijingu|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮|12=draft|12=draft}} (the Outer Shrine of {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮|12=draft|12=draft}}) and classified as a {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=draft|12=draft}}. It Ranks 10th among the 16 subordinate shrines of the Outer ShrineUjiyamada City Hall (1929): pp.11–13.. The shrine is located within the precincts of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|ja|月夜見宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|12=draft|12=draft}}, which is a separate shrine of the Outer ShrineIse Bunka-sha (2008): p.38. == Overview (概要) == Located at {{ill|Mie Prefecture|ja|三重県|12=draft|12=draft}} {{ill|Ise, Mie|ja|伊勢市|12=draft|12=draft}} 1006 Miyago 1-chome式内社研究会 編（1990）：294ページ (modern address: 1-3-19 Miyago, Ise City). The shrine is situated behind and to the right (northeast) of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月夜見宮|12=draft|12=draft}}'s main hall. The shrine grounds are surrounded by a moat on three sides, which is believed to be a remnant of a tributary of the {{ill|Miyagawa River (Mie)|ja|宮川 (三重県)|12=draft|12=draft}}. The enshrined deity is {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto no Mitama|ja|月夜見尊御魂|12=draft|12=draft}} (つきよみのみことのみたま). The shrine is located in Takagawara (高河原), an area near the Miyagawa River, and serves as a {{ill|guardian deity|ja|守護神|12=draft|12=draft}} (守護神) for the land development of the surrounding region. Many ancient texts describe the enshrined deity as the Mitama (spirit) of {{ill|Tsukiyomi|ja|月読|12=draft|12=draft}}. However, the ''{{ill|Shinmei-chō Kōshō Saikō|ja|神名帳考證再考|12=draft|12=draft}}'' (''神名帳考證再考'') claims that the deity is actually {{ill|Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto|ja|倉稲魂命|12=draft|12=draft}} (倉稲魂命), the deity of grain and prosperity. nother text, ''{{ill|Ninomiya Kansa Enkaku Kō|ja|二宮管社沿革考|12=draft|12=draft}}'' (''二宮管社沿革考''), asserts that the original name of the shrine in the ''{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|12=draft|12=draft}}'' (延喜式神名帳) was "{{ill|Kawahara-ni-Masu-Kuninamino-Kami Jinja|ja|川原坐国生神社|12=draft|12=draft}}", proving that its deity is {{ill|Kuninamino-Kami|ja|国生神|12=draft|12=draft}} (国生神), the god of land formation.Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): pp. 295–296 The main hall follows {{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|ja|神明造|12=draft|12=draft}} (神明造, the {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮|12=draft|12=draft}} architectural style) and has a wooden board roof ({{ill|Itabuki|ja|板葺|12=draft|12=draft}}), enclosed by a {{ill|Tamagaki|ja|玉垣|12=draft|12=draft}} (玉垣, sacred fence). Unlike most {{ill|Sessha|ja|摂社|12=draft|12=draft}}・{{ill|Massha|ja|末社|12=draft|12=draft}}・{{ill|Shokan-sha|ja|所管社|12=draft|12=draft}} (摂社・末社・所管社, auxiliary shrines) of {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮|12=draft|12=draft}}, which do not have an offering box ({{ill|Saisenbako|ja|賽銭箱|12=draft|12=draft}})Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p. 26, Takagawara Shrine uniquely has one. == History (歴史) == Based on the definition of a {{ill|Sessha|ja|摂社|12=draft|12=draft}} (auxiliary shrine) within {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮|12=draft|12=draft}}, this shrine was established before the compilation of the ''{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|12=draft|12=draft}}'' in {{ill|Enchō (era)|ja|延長|12=draft|12=draft}} 5 ({{ill|927|ja|927th year|12=draft|12=draft}}).Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p. 22 * The shrine is listed in that text as "{{ill|Kawahara-ni-Masu-Kuninamino-Kami Jinja|ja|川原坐国生神社|12=draft|12=draft}}". * Additionally, it is mentioned as "{{ill|Takagawara-sha|ja|高河原社|12=draft|12=draft}}" in the ''{{ill|Toyuke Daijingu Gishiki-chō|ja|止由気宮儀式帳|12=draft|12=draft}}''. * Since that text dates back to {{ill|Enryaku (era)|ja|延暦|12=draft|12=draft}} 23 ({{ill|804|ja|804th year|12=draft|12=draft}}), this confirms that the shrine existed before that time. According to the ''{{ill|Ruiju Jingi Hongen|ja|類聚神祇本源|12=draft|12=draft}}'', reconstructions were regularly conducted from {{ill|Tokuji (era)|ja|徳治|12=draft|12=draft}} 1 ({{ill|1306|ja|1306年|12=draft|12=draft}}) onwards, under the supervision of a special Zōsai-shi (造替使, shrine reconstruction official).Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p. 296 The ''{{ill|Ninomiya Kansa Enkaku Kō|ja|二宮管社沿革考|12=draft|12=draft}}'' records that: {{quote|"According to the '''Ōei Tōkō Nikki (応永頭工日記)''', on the '''fourth day of the first month in '''{{ill|Ōei (era)|ja|応永|12=draft|12=draft}} 26 ({{ill|1419|ja|1419th year|12=draft|12=draft}})''', a great fire burned down '''{{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月夜見宮|12=draft|12=draft}}''', its small shrine, '''Kawahara-sha (高河原社)''', and '''Imibiya-den (忌火屋殿, the sacred fire hall)'''."}} Thus, the shrine was confirmed to have existed until it burned down on {{ill|January 4 (old calendar)|ja|1月4日 (旧暦)|12=draft|12=draft}}, corresponding to {{ill|January 29|ja|1月29日|12=draft|12=draft}}, 1419 (Julian calendar). --- === Reconstruction in the Edo Period=== After this destruction, the shrine fell into neglect, and by the Early Modern Period (近世), its location was lost. However, thanks to the efforts of {{ill|Kawabe Kiyonaga|ja|河邊精長|12=draft|12=draft}} (also known as {{ill|Ōnakatomi Kiyonaga|ja|大中臣精長|12=draft|12=draft}}), the Grand Chief Priest ({{ill|Ōgūji|ja|大宮司|12=draft|12=draft}}), the shrine was reconstructed on its present site on {{ill|Kanbun (era)|ja|寛文|12=draft|12=draft}} 3, {{ill|July 7 (old calendar)|ja|7月7日 (旧暦)|12=draft|12=draft}} (corresponding to {{ill|August 9|ja|8月9日|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|1663|ja|1663rd year|12=draft|12=draft}} in the Gregorian calendar). * ''{{ill|Shinmei Hisho|ja|神名秘書|12=draft|12=draft}}'' states: "Located in Numaki-go, Yamada Village. East of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月読宮|12=draft|12=draft}}." * ''{{ill|Ruiju Jingi Hongen|ja|類聚神祇本源|12=draft|12=draft}}'' states: "East of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月読宮|12=draft|12=draft}}, within the same {{ill|Tamagaki|ja|玉垣|12=draft|12=draft}} fence." * ''{{ill|Ninomiya Kansa Enkaku Kō|ja|二宮管社沿革考|12=draft|12=draft}}'' claims that the original shrine site was actually the present-day {{ill|Suhara Taisha|ja|須原大社|12=draft|12=draft}} in Ichinoki, Ise City.Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p. 295 --- === Reconstruction in the Modern Period=== * In {{ill|1911|ja|1911th year|12=draft|12=draft}} ({{ill|Meiji|ja|明治|1=Meiji era|12=draft|12=draft}} 44), the shrine was rebuilt.Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): p. 12 * In {{ill|1938|ja|1938th year|12=draft|12=draft}} ({{ill|Shōwa|ja|昭和|12=draft|12=draft}} 13), it was rebuilt again. * In {{ill|1957|ja|1957th year|12=draft|12=draft}} (Shōwa 32), a major renovation was completed, and a sacred transfer ritual ({{ill|Sengyo|ja|遷御|12=draft|12=draft}}) was performed 20 years later.Sakurai (1991): p. 298 --- == Rites and Festivals (祭事) == * February – {{ill|Kinen-sai (祈年祭)|ja|祈年祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (Harvest Prayer Festival) * June & December – {{ill|Tsukinami-sai (月次祭)|ja|月次祭|1=Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|12=draft|12=draft}} (Monthly Festival) * October – {{ill|Kannamesai (神嘗祭)|ja|神嘗祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (Offering of First Fruits Festival) * November – {{ill|Niiname-sai (新嘗祭)|ja|新嘗祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (Thanksgiving Harvest Festival) These four major rituals are conducted on-site by a Negi (禰宜, senior priest) in巡回祭典 (巡回祭,巡行 ceremony format). {{Shrine |name = Takagawara Shrine |religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Takagawara-jinja 02.jpg|270px]] |location = {{ill|Ise, Mie|ja|伊勢市|12=draft|12=draft}}, Miyago 1-chome 3-19, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|ja|三重県|12=draft|12=draft}} |latitude_deg = 34 | latitude_min = 29 | latitude_sec = 34.5 |longitude_deg = 136 | longitude_min = 42 | longitude_sec = 22.2 |map = Japan Mie |deity = {{ill|Tsukuyomi|ja|月夜見尊御魂|12=draft|12=draft}} |Rank = {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=draft|12=draft}} (small)
{{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮|1=Toyouke Daijingu|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮|12=draft|12=draft}} Subordinate Shrine |founded = Before {{ill|Enryaku|ja|延暦|12=draft|12=draft}} 23 (804) |main_hall = {{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|ja|神明造|12=draft|12=draft}} |other_names = |pilgrimage_sites = |annual_festival = |rituals = {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭|12=draft|12=draft}} }} Takagawara Shrine (高河原神社, ''Takagawara Jinja''Shikinen Sengu Memorial Sengu-kan "[http://www.sengukan.jp/wp-content/themes/sengukan/shrine/area06.php Takagawara Shrine たかがわらじんじゃ>>]" (Accessed October 8, 2013).[[iTV]] "[http://www.yoitokose.jp/ise/encyclopedia/t0010.php Takagawara Shrine | Ise Grand Shrine Encyclopedia | Ise-Shima Travel Yoitokose]" (Accessed October 8, 2013)., also pronounced ''Takakawara Jinja''Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.39Gakken Publishing (2013): p.57) is a [[Shinto]] shrine located in Miyago, {{ill|Ise, Mie|ja|伊勢市|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|ja|三重県|12=draft|12=draft}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|subordinate shrine (sessha/massha)|ja|摂末社|12=draft|12=draft}} of {{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮|1=Toyouke Daijingu|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮|12=draft|12=draft}} (the Outer Shrine of {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮|12=draft|12=draft}}) and classified as a {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=draft|12=draft}}. It Ranks 10th among the 16 subordinate shrines of the Outer ShrineUjiyamada City Hall (1929): pp.11–13.. The shrine is located within the precincts of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|ja|月夜見宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|12=draft|12=draft}}, which is a separate shrine of the Outer ShrineIse Bunka-sha (2008): p.38. == Overview (概要) == Located at {{ill|Mie Prefecture|ja|三重県|12=draft|12=draft}} {{ill|Ise, Mie|ja|伊勢市|12=draft|12=draft}} 1006 Miyago 1-chome式内社研究会 編（1990）：294ページ (modern address: 1-3-19 Miyago, Ise City). The shrine is situated behind and to the right (northeast) of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月夜見宮|12=draft|12=draft}}'s main hall. The shrine grounds are surrounded by a moat on three sides, which is believed to be a remnant of a tributary of the {{ill|Miyagawa River (Mie)|ja|宮川 (三重県)|12=draft|12=draft}}. The enshrined deity is {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto no Mitama|ja|月夜見尊御魂|12=draft|12=draft}} (つきよみのみことのみたま). The shrine is located in Takagawara (高河原), an area near the Miyagawa River, and serves as a {{ill|guardian deity|ja|守護神|12=draft|12=draft}} (守護神) for the land development of the surrounding region. Many ancient texts describe the enshrined deity as the Mitama (spirit) of {{ill|Tsukiyomi|ja|月読|12=draft|12=draft}}. However, the ''{{ill|Shinmei-chō Kōshō Saikō|ja|神名帳考證再考|12=draft|12=draft}}'' (''神名帳考證再考'') claims that the deity is actually {{ill|Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto|ja|倉稲魂命|12=draft|12=draft}} (倉稲魂命), the deity of grain and prosperity. nother text, ''{{ill|Ninomiya Kansa Enkaku Kō|ja|二宮管社沿革考|12=draft|12=draft}}'' (''二宮管社沿革考''), asserts that the original name of the shrine in the ''{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|12=draft|12=draft}}'' (延喜式神名帳) was "{{ill|Kawahara-ni-Masu-Kuninamino-Kami Jinja|ja|川原坐国生神社|12=draft|12=draft}}", proving that its deity is {{ill|Kuninamino-Kami|ja|国生神|12=draft|12=draft}} (国生神), the god of land formation.Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): pp. 295–296 The main hall follows {{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|ja|神明造|12=draft|12=draft}} (神明造, the {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮|12=draft|12=draft}} architectural style) and has a wooden board roof ({{ill|Itabuki|ja|板葺|12=draft|12=draft}}), enclosed by a {{ill|Tamagaki|ja|玉垣|12=draft|12=draft}} (玉垣, sacred fence). Unlike most {{ill|Sessha|ja|摂社|12=draft|12=draft}}・{{ill|Massha|ja|末社|12=draft|12=draft}}・{{ill|Shokan-sha|ja|所管社|12=draft|12=draft}} (摂社・末社・所管社, auxiliary shrines) of {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮|12=draft|12=draft}}, which do not have an offering box ({{ill|Saisenbako|ja|賽銭箱|12=draft|12=draft}})Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p. 26, Takagawara Shrine uniquely has one. == History (歴史) == Based on the definition of a {{ill|Sessha|ja|摂社|12=draft|12=draft}} (auxiliary shrine) within {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮|12=draft|12=draft}}, this shrine was established before the compilation of the ''{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|12=draft|12=draft}}'' in {{ill|Enchō (era)|ja|延長|12=draft|12=draft}} 5 ({{ill|927|ja|927th year|12=draft|12=draft}}).Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p. 22 * The shrine is listed in that text as "{{ill|Kawahara-ni-Masu-Kuninamino-Kami Jinja|ja|川原坐国生神社|12=draft|12=draft}}". * Additionally, it is mentioned as "{{ill|Takagawara-sha|ja|高河原社|12=draft|12=draft}}" in the ''{{ill|Toyuke Daijingu Gishiki-chō|ja|止由気宮儀式帳|12=draft|12=draft}}''. * Since that text dates back to {{ill|Enryaku (era)|ja|延暦|12=draft|12=draft}} 23 ({{ill|804|ja|804th year|12=draft|12=draft}}), this confirms that the shrine existed before that time. According to the ''{{ill|Ruiju Jingi Hongen|ja|類聚神祇本源|12=draft|12=draft}}'', reconstructions were regularly conducted from {{ill|Tokuji (era)|ja|徳治|12=draft|12=draft}} 1 ({{ill|1306|ja|1306年|12=draft|12=draft}}) onwards, under the supervision of a special Zōsai-shi (造替使, shrine reconstruction official).Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p. 296 The ''{{ill|Ninomiya Kansa Enkaku Kō|ja|二宮管社沿革考|12=draft|12=draft}}'' records that: {{quote|"According to the '''Ōei Tōkō Nikki (応永頭工日記)''', on the '''fourth day of the first month in '''{{ill|Ōei (era)|ja|応永|12=draft|12=draft}} 26 ({{ill|1419|ja|1419th year|12=draft|12=draft}})''', a great fire burned down '''{{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月夜見宮|12=draft|12=draft}}''', its small shrine, '''Kawahara-sha (高河原社)''', and '''Imibiya-den (忌火屋殿, the sacred fire hall)'''."}} Thus, the shrine was confirmed to have existed until it burned down on {{ill|January 4 (old calendar)|ja|1月4日 (旧暦)|12=draft|12=draft}}, corresponding to {{ill|January 29|ja|1月29日|12=draft|12=draft}}, 1419 (Julian calendar). --- === Reconstruction in the Edo Period=== After this destruction, the shrine fell into neglect, and by the Early Modern Period (近世), its location was lost. However, thanks to the efforts of {{ill|Kawabe Kiyonaga|ja|河邊精長|12=draft|12=draft}} (also known as {{ill|Ōnakatomi Kiyonaga|ja|大中臣精長|12=draft|12=draft}}), the Grand Chief Priest ({{ill|Ōgūji|ja|大宮司|12=draft|12=draft}}), the shrine was reconstructed on its present site on {{ill|Kanbun (era)|ja|寛文|12=draft|12=draft}} 3, {{ill|July 7 (old calendar)|ja|7月7日 (旧暦)|12=draft|12=draft}} (corresponding to {{ill|August 9|ja|8月9日|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|1663|ja|1663rd year|12=draft|12=draft}} in the Gregorian calendar). * ''{{ill|Shinmei Hisho|ja|神名秘書|12=draft|12=draft}}'' states: "Located in Numaki-go, Yamada Village. East of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月読宮|12=draft|12=draft}}." * ''{{ill|Ruiju Jingi Hongen|ja|類聚神祇本源|12=draft|12=draft}}'' states: "East of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月読宮|12=draft|12=draft}}, within the same {{ill|Tamagaki|ja|玉垣|12=draft|12=draft}} fence." * ''{{ill|Ninomiya Kansa Enkaku Kō|ja|二宮管社沿革考|12=draft|12=draft}}'' claims that the original shrine site was actually the present-day {{ill|Suhara Taisha|ja|須原大社|12=draft|12=draft}} in Ichinoki, Ise City.Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p. 295 --- === Reconstruction in the Modern Period=== * In {{ill|1911|ja|1911th year|12=draft|12=draft}} ({{ill|Meiji|ja|明治|1=Meiji era|12=draft|12=draft}} 44), the shrine was rebuilt.Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): p. 12 * In {{ill|1938|ja|1938th year|12=draft|12=draft}} ({{ill|Shōwa|ja|昭和|12=draft|12=draft}} 13), it was rebuilt again. * In {{ill|1957|ja|1957th year|12=draft|12=draft}} (Shōwa 32), a major renovation was completed, and a sacred transfer ritual ({{ill|Sengyo|ja|遷御|12=draft|12=draft}}) was performed 20 years later.Sakurai (1991): p. 298 --- == Rites and Festivals (祭事) == * February – {{ill|Kinen-sai (祈年祭)|ja|祈年祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (Harvest Prayer Festival) * June & December – {{ill|Tsukinami-sai (月次祭)|ja|月次祭|1=Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|12=draft|12=draft}} (Monthly Festival) * October – {{ill|Kannamesai (神嘗祭)|ja|神嘗祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (Offering of First Fruits Festival) * November – {{ill|Niiname-sai (新嘗祭)|ja|新嘗祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (Thanksgiving Harvest Festival) These four major rituals are conducted on-site by a Negi (禰宜, senior priest) in巡回祭典 (巡回祭,巡行 ceremony format). The following six rites are performed remotely (遥祀, Yōshi): * January – {{ill|Saitan-sai (歳旦祭)|ja|歳旦祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (New Year's Festival) * January – {{ill|Genshi-sai (元始祭)|ja|元始祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (Imperial Foundation Festival) * February 11 – {{ill|Kenkoku-kinen-sai (建国記念祭)|ja|建国記念祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (National Foundation Day) * May & August – {{ill|Kaze-no-Hi-no-Matsuri (風日祈祭)|ja|風日祈祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (Wind and Rain Prayers) * December 23 – {{ill|Tenchō-sai (天長祭)|ja|天長祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (Emperor's Birthday Festival) --- == Access (交通) == [[File:Tsukiyominomiyamae Bus Stop.jpg|thumb|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya-mae Bus Stop]] Public Transport: * 10-minute walk (550m) from {{ill|Ise City Station|ja|伊勢市駅|12=draft|12=draft}} (JR & Kintetsu).Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p. 33 * 4-minute walk (360m) from Shindō Bus Stop (三重交通). By Car: * Approx. 5 minutes (2.5km) from Ise Nishi IC (伊勢西IC, Ise Expressway). * Metered parking available near the entrance. --- == References == {{Reflist}} == 参考文献 == * 宇治山田市役所 編『宇治山田市史 上巻』宇治山田市役所、昭和4th year 1月20日、862p. * [[学研パブリッシング]]『伊勢神宮に行こう』Gakken Mook神社紀行セレクションvol.1、[[薗田稔]]監修、学研マーケティング、2013rd year 7月4日、82p. ISBN 978-4-05-610047-1 * [[櫻井勝之進]]『伊勢神宮の祖型と展開』[[国書刊行会]]、平成3rd year 11月30日、318p. ISBN 4-336-03296-3 * 式内社研究会 編『式内社調査報告 第六巻 東海道1』[[Kogakkan University]]出版部、平成2nd year 2月28日、690p. ISBN 4-87644-080-8 * 『お伊勢さん125社めぐり』別冊『伊勢人』、[[伊勢文化舎]]、平成20th year 12月23日、151p. ISBN 978-4-900759-37-4 == See Also == * {{ill|List of Shikinaisha in Ise Province|ja|伊勢国の式内社一覧|12=draft|12=draft}} * {{ill|List of 125 Shrines of Ise|ja|神宮125社の一覧|lt=List of 125 Shrines of Ise|1=List of Shikinaisha in Ise Province|3=伊勢国の式内社一覧|12=draft|12=draft}} == External Links == * [http://www.jingukaikan.jp/125mairi/m02/0203.html 高河原神社（たかがわらじんじゃ）] - 財団法人伊勢神宮崇敬会 {{125 Shrines of Ise}} {{draft categories| }} {{draft categories| [[Category:Shrines in Mie Prefecture]] [[Category:Subordinate shrines of Toyouke Daijingu]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Japan]] [[Category:Ise Grand Shrine]] [[Category:Completion tier 5]] [[Category:125 Shrines of Ise]] [[Category:11]] [[Category:高河原神社]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Ise Province]] [[Category:Setsumatsusha]] [[Category:伊勢市の神社]] [[Category:category refresh]] [[Category:New]] [[Category:qq]] }} [[ja:高河原神社]] [[sn:Takagawara Shrine]] [[sn:akagawara Shrine]]

Unlike most {{ill|Sessha|ja|摂社|12=draft|12=draft}}・{{ill|Massha|ja|末社|12=draft|12=draft}}・{{ill|Shokan-sha|ja|所管社|12=draft|12=draft}} (摂社・末社・所管社, auxiliary shrines) of {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮|12=draft|12=draft}}, which do not have an offering box ({{ill|Saisenbako|ja|賽銭箱|12=draft|12=draft}})Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p. 26, Takagawara Shrine uniquely has one. == History (歴史) == Based on the definition of a {{ill|Sessha|ja|摂社|12=draft|12=draft}} (auxiliary shrine) within {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮|12=draft|12=draft}}, this shrine was established before the compilation of the ''{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|12=draft|12=draft}}'' in {{ill|Enchō (era)|ja|延長|12=draft|12=draft}} 5 ({{ill|927|ja|927th year|12=draft|12=draft}}).Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p. 22 * The shrine is listed in that text as "{{ill|Kawahara-ni-Masu-Kuninamino-Kami Jinja|ja|川原坐国生神社|12=draft|12=draft}}". * Additionally, it is mentioned as "{{ill|Takagawara-sha|ja|高河原社|12=draft|12=draft}}" in the ''{{ill|Toyuke Daijingu Gishiki-chō|ja|止由気宮儀式帳|12=draft|12=draft}}''. * Since that text dates back to {{ill|Enryaku (era)|ja|延暦|12=draft|12=draft}} 23 ({{ill|804|ja|804th year|12=draft|12=draft}}), this confirms that the shrine existed before that time. According to the ''{{ill|Ruiju Jingi Hongen|ja|類聚神祇本源|12=draft|12=draft}}'', reconstructions were regularly conducted from {{ill|Tokuji (era)|ja|徳治|12=draft|12=draft}} 1 ({{ill|1306|ja|1306年|12=draft|12=draft}}) onwards, under the supervision of a special Zōsai-shi (造替使, shrine reconstruction official).Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p. 296 The ''{{ill|Ninomiya Kansa Enkaku Kō|ja|二宮管社沿革考|12=draft|12=draft}}'' records that: {{quote|"According to the '''Ōei Tōkō Nikki (応永頭工日記)''', on the '''fourth day of the first month in '''{{ill|Ōei (era)|ja|応永|12=draft|12=draft}} 26 ({{ill|1419|ja|1419th year|12=draft|12=draft}})''', a great fire burned down '''{{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月夜見宮|12=draft|12=draft}}''', its small shrine, '''Kawahara-sha (高河原社)''', and '''Imibiya-den (忌火屋殿, the sacred fire hall)'''."}} Thus, the shrine was confirmed to have existed until it burned down on {{ill|January 4 (old calendar)|ja|1月4日 (旧暦)|12=draft|12=draft}}, corresponding to {{ill|January 29|ja|1月29日|12=draft|12=draft}}, 1419 (Julian calendar). --- === Reconstruction in the Edo Period=== After this destruction, the shrine fell into neglect, and by the Early Modern Period (近世), its location was lost. However, thanks to the efforts of {{ill|Kawabe Kiyonaga|ja|河邊精長|12=draft|12=draft}} (also known as {{ill|Ōnakatomi Kiyonaga|ja|大中臣精長|12=draft|12=draft}}), the Grand Chief Priest ({{ill|Ōgūji|ja|大宮司|12=draft|12=draft}}), the shrine was reconstructed on its present site on {{ill|Kanbun (era)|ja|寛文|12=draft|12=draft}} 3, {{ill|July 7 (old calendar)|ja|7月7日 (旧暦)|12=draft|12=draft}} (corresponding to {{ill|August 9|ja|8月9日|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|1663|ja|1663rd year|12=draft|12=draft}} in the Gregorian calendar). * ''{{ill|Shinmei Hisho|ja|神名秘書|12=draft|12=draft}}'' states: "Located in Numaki-go, Yamada Village. East of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月読宮|12=draft|12=draft}}." * ''{{ill|Ruiju Jingi Hongen|ja|類聚神祇本源|12=draft|12=draft}}'' states: "East of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月読宮|12=draft|12=draft}}, within the same {{ill|Tamagaki|ja|玉垣|12=draft|12=draft}} fence." * ''{{ill|Ninomiya Kansa Enkaku Kō|ja|二宮管社沿革考|12=draft|12=draft}}'' claims that the original shrine site was actually the present-day {{ill|Suhara Taisha|ja|須原大社|12=draft|12=draft}} in Ichinoki, Ise City.Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p. 295 --- === Reconstruction in the Modern Period=== * In {{ill|1911|ja|1911th year|12=draft|12=draft}} ({{ill|Meiji|ja|明治|1=Meiji era|12=draft|12=draft}} 44), the shrine was rebuilt.Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): p. 12 * In {{ill|1938|ja|1938th year|12=draft|12=draft}} ({{ill|Shōwa|ja|昭和|12=draft|12=draft}} 13), it was rebuilt again. * In {{ill|1957|ja|1957th year|12=draft|12=draft}} (Shōwa 32), a major renovation was completed, and a sacred transfer ritual ({{ill|Sengyo|ja|遷御|12=draft|12=draft}}) was performed 20 years later.Sakurai (1991): p. 298 --- == Rites and Festivals (祭事) == * February – {{ill|Kinen-sai (祈年祭)|ja|祈年祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (Harvest Prayer Festival) * June & December – {{ill|Tsukinami-sai (月次祭)|ja|月次祭|1=Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|12=draft|12=draft}} (Monthly Festival) * October – {{ill|Kannamesai (神嘗祭)|ja|神嘗祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (Offering of First Fruits Festival) * November – {{ill|Niiname-sai (新嘗祭)|ja|新嘗祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (Thanksgiving Harvest Festival) These four major rituals are conducted on-site by a Negi (禰宜, senior priest) in巡回祭典 (巡回祭,巡行 ceremony format). The following six rites are performed remotely (遥祀, Yōshi): * January – {{ill|Saitan-sai (歳旦祭)|ja|歳旦祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (New Year's Festival) * January – {{ill|Genshi-sai (元始祭)|ja|元始祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (Imperial Foundation Festival) * February 11 – {{ill|Kenkoku-kinen-sai (建国記念祭)|ja|建国記念祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (National Foundation Day) * May & August – {{ill|Kaze-no-Hi-no-Matsuri (風日祈祭)|ja|風日祈祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (Wind and Rain Prayers) * December 23 – {{ill|Tenchō-sai (天長祭)|ja|天長祭|12=draft|12=draft}} (Emperor's Birthday Festival) --- == Access (交通) == [[File:Tsukiyominomiyamae Bus Stop.jpg|thumb|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya-mae Bus Stop]] Public Transport: * 10-minute walk (550m) from {{ill|Ise City Station|ja|伊勢市駅|12=draft|12=draft}} (JR & Kintetsu).Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p. 33 * 4-minute walk (360m) from Shindō Bus Stop (三重交通). It is a {{ill|subordinate shrine (sessha/massha)|ja|摂末社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} of {{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮|1=Toyouke Daijingu|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (the Outer Shrine of {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) and classified as a {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. It Ranks 10th among the 16 subordinate shrines of the Outer ShrineUjiyamada City Hall (1929): pp.11–13.. The shrine is located within the precincts of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|ja|月夜見宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, which is a separate shrine of the Outer ShrineIse Bunka-sha (2008): p.38. == Overview (概要) == Located at {{ill|Mie Prefecture|ja|三重県|qq=draft|qq=draft}} {{ill|Ise, Mie|ja|伊勢市|qq=draft|qq=draft}} 1006 Miyago 1-chome式内社研究会 編（1990）：294ページ (modern address: 1-3-19 Miyago, Ise City). The shrine is situated behind and to the right (northeast) of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月夜見宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'s main hall. The shrine grounds are surrounded by a moat on three sides, which is believed to be a remnant of a tributary of the {{ill|Miyagawa River (Mie)|ja|宮川 (三重県)|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. The enshrined deity is {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto no Mitama|ja|月夜見尊御魂|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (つきよみのみことのみたま). The shrine is located in Takagawara (高河原), an area near the Miyagawa River, and serves as a {{ill|guardian deity|ja|守護神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (守護神) for the land development of the surrounding region. According to the ''{{ill|Ruiju Jingi Hongen|ja|類聚神祇本源|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'', reconstructions were regularly conducted from {{ill|Tokuji (era)|ja|徳治|qq=draft|qq=draft}} 1 ({{ill|1306|ja|1306年|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) onwards, under the supervision of a special Zōsai-shi (造替使, shrine reconstruction official).Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p. 296 The ''{{ill|Ninomiya Kansa Enkaku Kō|ja|二宮管社沿革考|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'' records that: {{quote|"According to the '''Ōei Tōkō Nikki (応永頭工日記)''', on the '''fourth day of the first month in '''{{ill|Ōei (era)|ja|応永|qq=draft|qq=draft}} 26 ({{ill|1419|ja|1419th year|qq=draft|qq=draft}})''', a great fire burned down '''{{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月夜見宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''', its small shrine, '''Kawahara-sha (高河原社)''', and '''Imibiya-den (忌火屋殿, the sacred fire hall)'''."}} Thus, the shrine was confirmed to have existed until it burned down on {{ill|January 4 (old calendar)|ja|1月4日 (旧暦)|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, corresponding to {{ill|January 29|ja|1月29日|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, 1419 (Julian calendar). --- === Reconstruction in the Edo Period=== After this destruction, the shrine fell into neglect, and by the Early Modern Period (近世), its location was lost. However, thanks to the efforts of {{ill|Kawabe Kiyonaga|ja|河邊精長|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (also known as {{ill|Ōnakatomi Kiyonaga|ja|大中臣精長|qq=draft|qq=draft}}), the Grand Chief Priest ({{ill|Ōgūji|ja|大宮司|qq=draft|qq=draft}}), the shrine was reconstructed on its present site on {{ill|Kanbun (era)|ja|寛文|qq=draft|qq=draft}} 3, {{ill|July 7 (old calendar)|ja|7月7日 (旧暦)|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (corresponding to {{ill|August 9|ja|8月9日|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|1663|ja|1663rd year|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in the Gregorian calendar). * ''{{ill|Shinmei Hisho|ja|神名秘書|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'' states: "Located in Numaki-go, Yamada Village. East of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月読宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}." * ''{{ill|Ruiju Jingi Hongen|ja|類聚神祇本源|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'' states: "East of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月読宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, within the same {{ill|Tamagaki|ja|玉垣|qq=draft|qq=draft}} fence." * ''{{ill|Ninomiya Kansa Enkaku Kō|ja|二宮管社沿革考|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'' claims that the original shrine site was actually the present-day {{ill|Suhara Taisha|ja|須原大社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in Ichinoki, Ise City.Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p. 295 --- === Reconstruction in the Modern Period=== * In {{ill|1911|ja|1911th year|qq=draft|qq=draft}} ({{ill|Meiji|ja|明治|1=Meiji era|qq=draft|qq=draft}} 44), the shrine was rebuilt.Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): p. 12 * In {{ill|1938|ja|1938th year|qq=draft|qq=draft}} ({{ill|Shōwa|ja|昭和|qq=draft|qq=draft}} 13), it was rebuilt again. * In {{ill|1957|ja|1957th year|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Shōwa 32), a major renovation was completed, and a sacred transfer ritual ({{ill|Sengyo|ja|遷御|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) was performed 20 years later.Sakurai (1991): p. 298 --- == Rites and Festivals (祭事) == * February – {{ill|Kinen-sai (祈年祭)|ja|祈年祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Harvest Prayer Festival) * June & December – {{ill|Tsukinami-sai (月次祭)|ja|月次祭|1=Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Monthly Festival) * October – {{ill|Kannamesai (神嘗祭)|ja|神嘗祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Offering of First Fruits Festival) * November – {{ill|Niiname-sai (新嘗祭)|ja|新嘗祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Thanksgiving Harvest Festival) These four major rituals are conducted on-site by a Negi (禰宜, senior priest) in巡回祭典 (巡回祭,巡行 ceremony format). The following six rites are performed remotely (遥祀, Yōshi): * January – {{ill|Saitan-sai (歳旦祭)|ja|歳旦祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (New Year's Festival) * January – {{ill|Genshi-sai (元始祭)|ja|元始祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Imperial Foundation Festival) * February 11 – {{ill|Kenkoku-kinen-sai (建国記念祭)|ja|建国記念祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (National Foundation Day) * May & August – {{ill|Kaze-no-Hi-no-Matsuri (風日祈祭)|ja|風日祈祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Wind and Rain Prayers) * December 23 – {{ill|Tenchō-sai (天長祭)|ja|天長祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Emperor's Birthday Festival) --- == Access (交通) == [[File:Tsukiyominomiyamae Bus Stop.jpg|thumb|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya-mae Bus Stop]] Public Transport: * 10-minute walk (550m) from {{ill|Ise City Station|ja|伊勢市駅|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (JR & Kintetsu).Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p. 33 * 4-minute walk (360m) from Shindō Bus Stop (三重交通). By Car: * Approx. 5 minutes (2.5km) from Ise Nishi IC (伊勢西IC, Ise Expressway). * Metered parking available near the entrance. --- == References == {{Reflist}} == 参考文献 == * 宇治山田市役所 編『宇治山田市史 上巻』宇治山田市役所、昭和4th year 1月20日、862p. * [[学研パブリッシング]]『伊勢神宮に行こう』Gakken Mook神社紀行セレクションvol.1、[[薗田稔]]監修、学研マーケティング、2013rd year 7月4日、82p. ISBN 978-4-05-610047-1 * [[櫻井勝之進]]『伊勢神宮の祖型と展開』[[国書刊行会]]、平成3rd year 11月30日、318p. ISBN 4-336-03296-3 * 式内社研究会 編『式内社調査報告 第六巻 東海道1』[[Kogakkan University]]出版部、平成2nd year 2月28日、690p. ISBN 4-87644-080-8 * 『お伊勢さん125社めぐり』別冊『伊勢人』、[[伊勢文化舎]]、平成20th year 12月23日、151p. revision.text:
{{神社 |名称 = 高河原神社 |画像 = [[File:Takagawara-jinja 02.jpg|270px]] |所在地 = [[三重県]][[伊勢市]]宮後一丁目3-19 |緯度度 = 34 | 緯度分 = 29 | 緯度秒 = 34.5 |経度度 = 136 |経度分 = 42 | 経度秒 = 22.2 |地図 = Japan Mie |祭神 = [[ツクヨミ|月夜見尊御魂]] |社格 = [[式内社]]（小）
[[豊受大神宮]]摂社 |創建 = [[延暦]]23年（[[804年]]）以前 |本殿 = [[神明造]] |別名 = |札所等 = |例祭 = |神事 = [[神嘗祭]] }} '''高河原神社'''（たかがわらじんじゃ式年遷宮記念せんぐう館"[http://www.sengukan.jp/wp-content/themes/sengukan/shrine/area06.php 高河原神社 <<たかがわらじんじゃ>>]"（2013年10月8日閲覧。）[[アイティービー|iTV]]"[http://www.yoitokose.jp/ise/encyclopedia/t0010.php 高河原神社|伊勢神宮百科辞典|伊勢志摩の旅よいとこせ]"（2013年10月8日閲覧。） 、たかかわらじんじゃ伊勢文化舎（2008）：39ページ学研パブリッシング（2013）：57ページ）は、[[三重県]][[伊勢市]]宮後にある[[神社]]。[[伊勢神宮]][[豊受大神宮]]（外宮）の[[摂末社|摂社]]。[[式内社]]。外宮の摂社16社のうち第10位である宇治山田市役所 編（1929）：11 - 13ページ。外宮の別宮である[[月夜見宮]]の境内にある伊勢文化舎（2008）：38ページ。 == 概要 == [[三重県]][[伊勢市]]宮後一丁目1006番地式内社研究会 編（1990）：294ページ（[[住居表示]]では宮後一丁目3番19号）に鎮座する。月夜見宮社殿の右手後方（北東）に位置する。境内地は三方を堀で囲まれているが、この堀は[[宮川 (三重県)|宮川]]の支流の名残とされる。 [[祭神]]は[[ツクヨミ|月夜見尊御魂]]（つきよみのみことのみたま）。鎮座地周辺は宮川の高河原であり、周辺[[地域]]の土地開拓の[[守護神]]である。多くの古書で祭神を月夜見（月読）の[[御魂]]であるとするが、『神名帳考證再考』は[[ウカノミタマ|倉稲魂命]]（うかのみたまのみこと）であると主張し、『二宮管社沿革考』は式内社としての社名「川原坐国生神社」から祭神が国生神であることは明らかだと述べている式内社研究会 編（1990）：295 - 296ページ。 [[社殿]]は[[神明造]]の[[板葺]]で、[[玉垣]]に囲まれている。伊勢神宮の摂社・末社・所管社には通例、[[賽銭]]箱は置かれていない伊勢文化舎（2008）：26ページが、高河原神社には賽銭箱が置かれている。 == 歴史 == 伊勢神宮の摂社の定義より『[[延喜式神名帳]]』成立、すなわち[[延長 (元号)|延長]]5年（[[927年]]）以前に創建された伊勢文化舎（2008）：22ページ。同書には「川原坐国生神社」として記載される。また、『止由気宮儀式帳』にも「高河原社」として記載があることから[[延暦]]23年（[[804年]]）以前から存在したことになる。『類聚神祇本源』の私記によれば、[[徳治]]元年（[[1306年]]）以降、造替使よって造り替えが行われるようになった式内社研究会 編（1990）：296ページ。『二宮管社沿革考』に「[[応永]]頭工日記云、応永廿六年正月四日ノ炎上ノ事、月夜見宮・同小殿・'''河原社'''・忌火屋殿御焼、ト云ヘリ。」とあり、応永廿六年[[1月4日 (旧暦)|正月四日]]（[[ユリウス暦]]：[[1419年]][[1月29日]]）に焼失するまで、高河原神社が存在したことは分かっている。 その後[[祭祀]]が行われなくなり、[[近世]]には社地不明となるが、[[大宮司]]・[[河辺精長|河邊精長]]（大中臣精長）の尽力により[[寛文]]3年[[7月7日 (旧暦)|7月7日]]（[[グレゴリオ暦]]：[[1663年]][[8月9日]]）に現社地で再興された（『摂社再興記』による）。鎮座地は『神名秘書』では「在沼木郷山田村。月読宮東。」とし、『類聚神祇本源』では「月読宮東、同玉垣内。」としている。『二宮管社沿革考』では、旧社地を伊勢市一之木の須原大社であるとしている式内社研究会 編（1990）：295ページ。 [[1911年]]（[[明治]]44年）3月に建て替えが行われている宇治山田市役所 編（1929）：12ページ。その後、[[1938年]]（[[昭和]]13年）に建て替えた後に[[1957年]]（昭和32年）に大修繕を行ったので、20年目に遷御を行った櫻井（1991）：298ページ。 == 祭祀 == [[祈年祭]]（2月）、[[月次祭]]（6月・12月）、[[神嘗祭]]（10月）、[[新嘗祭]]（11月）は、[[禰宜]]（ねぎ）が巡回祭典の形で境内にて祭祀を執行し、[[歳旦祭]]（1月）、[[元始祭]]（1月）、建国記念祭（[[2月11日]]）、風日祈祭（5月・8月）、[[天長祭]]（[[12月23日]]）は遥祀を行う。 == 交通 == [[ファイル:Tsukiyominomiyamae Bus Stop.jpg|thumb|最寄りの月夜見宮前バス停]] ;公共交通 * [[東海旅客鉄道|JR]][[参宮線]]・[[近畿日本鉄道|近鉄]][[近鉄山田線|山田線]][[伊勢市駅]]南口（JR側）から徒歩約10分（約550[[メートル|m]]）伊勢文化舎（2008）：33ページ。外宮北御門からは、神路通りで一直線に結ばれている。沿道には[[伊勢市立厚生小学校]]がある。 * [[三重交通]][[路線バス|バス]]新道[[バス停留所|バス停]]より徒歩約4分（約360m）。[[伊勢市コミュニティバス]]「おかげバス」月夜見宮前バス停よりすぐ。 ;自家用車 * [[伊勢自動車道]][[伊勢西インターチェンジ|伊勢西IC]]より[[三重県道32号伊勢磯部線]]（御木本道路）を北へ約5分（約2.5[[キロメートル|km]]）。境内入口前の道路に[[パーキングメーター]]付きの[[駐車場]]がある。 == 脚注 == {{Reflist}} == 参考文献 == * 宇治山田市役所 編『宇治山田市史 上巻』宇治山田市役所、昭和4年1月20日、862p. * [[学研パブリッシング]]『伊勢神宮に行こう』Gakken Mook神社紀行セレクションvol.1、[[薗田稔]]監修、学研マーケティング、2013年7月4日、82p. ISBN 978-4-05-610047-1 * [[櫻井勝之進]]『伊勢神宮の祖型と展開』[[国書刊行会]]、平成3年11月30日、318p. ISBN 4-336-03296-3 * 式内社研究会 編『式内社調査報告 第六巻 東海道1』[[皇學館大学]]出版部、平成2年2月28日、690p. ISBN 4-87644-080-8 * 『お伊勢さん125社めぐり』別冊『伊勢人』、[[伊勢文化舎]]、平成20年12月23日、151p. ISBN 978-4-900759-37-4 == 関連項目 == * [[伊勢国の式内社一覧]] * [[神宮125社の一覧]] == 外部リンク == * [http://www.jingukaikan.jp/125mairi/m02/0203.html 高河原神社（たかがわらじんじゃ）] - 財団法人伊勢神宮崇敬会 {{神宮125社}} {{神道 横}} {{デフォルトソート:たかかわらしんしや}} [[Category:神宮125社]] [[Category:伊勢国の式内社]] [[Category:摂末社]] [[Category:伊勢市の神社]]

13ページ。外宮の別宮である[[月夜見宮]]の境内にある伊勢文化舎（2008）：38ページ。 == 概要 == [[三重県]][[伊勢市]]宮後一丁目1006番地式内社研究会 編（1990）：294ページ（[[住居表示]]では宮後一丁目3番19号）に鎮座する。月夜見宮社殿の右手後方（北東）に位置する。境内地は三方を堀で囲まれているが、この堀は[[宮川 (三重県)|宮川]]の支流の名残とされる。 [[祭神]]は[[ツクヨミ|月夜見尊御魂]]（つきよみのみことのみたま）。鎮座地周辺は宮川の高河原であり、周辺[[地域]]の土地開拓の[[守護神]]である。多くの古書で祭神を月夜見（月読）の[[御魂]]であるとするが、『神名帳考證再考』は[[ウカノミタマ|倉稲魂命]]（うかのみたまのみこと）であると主張し、『二宮管社沿革考』は式内社としての社名「川原坐国生神社」から祭神が国生神であることは明らかだと述べている式内社研究会 編（1990）：295 - 296ページ。 [[社殿]]は[[神明造]]の[[板葺]]で、[[玉垣]]に囲まれている。伊勢神宮の摂社・末社・所管社には通例、[[賽銭]]箱は置かれていない伊勢文化舎（2008）：26ページが、高河原神社には賽銭箱が置かれている。 == 歴史 == 伊勢神宮の摂社の定義より『[[延喜式神名帳]]』成立、すなわち[[延長 (元号)|延長]]5年（[[927年]]）以前に創建された伊勢文化舎（2008）：22ページ。同書には「川原坐国生神社」として記載される。また、『止由気宮儀式帳』にも「高河原社」として記載があることから[[延暦]]23年（[[804年]]）以前から存在したことになる。『類聚神祇本源』の私記によれば、[[徳治]]元年（[[1306年]]）以降、造替使よって造り替えが行われるようになった式内社研究会 編（1990）：296ページ。『二宮管社沿革考』に「[[応永]]頭工日記云、応永廿六年正月四日ノ炎上ノ事、月夜見宮・同小殿・'''河原社'''・忌火屋殿御焼、ト云ヘリ。」とあり、応永廿六年[[1月4日 (旧暦)|正月四日]]（[[ユリウス暦]]：[[1419年]][[1月29日]]）に焼失するまで、高河原神社が存在したことは分かっている。 その後[[祭祀]]が行われなくなり、[[近世]]には社地不明となるが、[[大宮司]]・[[河辺精長|河邊精長]]（大中臣精長）の尽力により[[寛文]]3年[[7月7日 (旧暦)|7月7日]]（[[グレゴリオ暦]]：[[1663年]][[8月9日]]）に現社地で再興された（『摂社再興記』による）。鎮座地は『神名秘書』では「在沼木郷山田村。月読宮東。」とし、『類聚神祇本源』では「月読宮東、同玉垣内。」としている。『二宮管社沿革考』では、旧社地を伊勢市一之木の須原大社であるとしている式内社研究会 編（1990）：295ページ。 [[1911年]]（[[明治]]44年）3月に建て替えが行われている宇治山田市役所 編（1929）：12ページ。その後、[[1938年]]（[[昭和]]13年）に建て替えた後に[[1957年]]（昭和32年）に大修繕を行ったので、20年目に遷御を行った櫻井（1991）：298ページ。 == 祭祀 == [[祈年祭]]（2月）、[[月次祭]]（6月・12月）、[[神嘗祭]]（10月）、[[新嘗祭]]（11月）は、[[禰宜]]（ねぎ）が巡回祭典の形で境内にて祭祀を執行し、[[歳旦祭]]（1月）、[[元始祭]]（1月）、建国記念祭（[[2月11日]]）、風日祈祭（5月・8月）、[[天長祭]]（[[12月23日]]）は遥祀を行う。 == 交通 == [[ファイル:Tsukiyominomiyamae Bus Stop.jpg|thumb|最寄りの月夜見宮前バス停]] ;公共交通 * [[東海旅客鉄道|JR]][[参宮線]]・[[近畿日本鉄道|近鉄]][[近鉄山田線|山田線]][[伊勢市駅]]南口（JR側）から徒歩約10分（約550[[メートル|m]]）伊勢文化舎（2008）：33ページ。外宮北御門からは、神路通りで一直線に結ばれている。沿道には[[伊勢市立厚生小学校]]がある。 * [[三重交通]][[路線バス|バス]]新道[[バス停留所|バス停]]より徒歩約4分（約360m）。[[伊勢市コミュニティバス]]「おかげバス」月夜見宮前バス停よりすぐ。 ;自家用車 * [[伊勢自動車道]][[伊勢西インターチェンジ|伊勢西IC]]より[[三重県道32号伊勢磯部線]]（御木本道路）を北へ約5分（約2.5[[キロメートル|km]]）。境内入口前の道路に[[パーキングメーター]]付きの[[駐車場]]がある。 == 脚注 == {{Reflist}} == 参考文献 == * 宇治山田市役所 編『宇治山田市史 上巻』宇治山田市役所、昭和4年1月20日、862p. * [[学研パブリッシング]]『伊勢神宮に行こう』Gakken Mook神社紀行セレクションvol.1、[[薗田稔]]監修、学研マーケティング、2013年7月4日、82p.
