{{Shrine |name = Takagawara Shrine |religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Takagawara-jinja 02.jpg|270px]] |location = {{ill|Ise, Mie|ja|伊勢市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Miyago 1-chome 3-19, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|ja|三重県|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |latitude_deg = 34 | latitude_min = 29 | latitude_sec = 34.5 |longitude_deg = 136 | longitude_min = 42 | longitude_sec = 22.2 |map = Japan Mie |deity = {{ill|Tsukuyomi|ja|月夜見尊御魂|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |Rank = {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (small)
{{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮|1=Toyouke Daijingu|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}} Subordinate Shrine |founded = Before {{ill|Enryaku|ja|延暦|qq=draft|qq=draft}} 23 (804) |main_hall = {{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|ja|神明造|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |other_names = |pilgrimage_sites = |annual_festival = |rituals = {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} }} Takagawara Shrine (高河原神社, ''Takagawara Jinja''Shikinen Sengu Memorial Sengu-kan "[http://www.sengukan.jp/wp-content/themes/sengukan/shrine/area06.php Takagawara Shrine たかがわらじんじゃ>>]" (Accessed October 8, 2013).[[iTV]] "[http://www.yoitokose.jp/ise/encyclopedia/t0010.php Takagawara Shrine | Ise Grand Shrine Encyclopedia | Ise-Shima Travel Yoitokose]" (Accessed October 8, 2013)., also pronounced ''Takakawara Jinja''Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.39Gakken Publishing (2013): p.57) is a [[Shinto]] shrine located in Miyago, {{ill|Ise, Mie|ja|伊勢市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|ja|三重県|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|subordinate shrine (sessha/massha)|ja|摂末社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} of {{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮|1=Toyouke Daijingu|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (the Outer Shrine of {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) and classified as a {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. It Ranks 10th among the 16 subordinate shrines of the Outer ShrineUjiyamada City Hall (1929): pp.11–13.. The shrine is located within the precincts of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|ja|月夜見宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, which is a separate shrine of the Outer ShrineIse Bunka-sha (2008): p.38. == Overview (概要) == Located at {{ill|Mie Prefecture|ja|三重県|qq=draft|qq=draft}} {{ill|Ise, Mie|ja|伊勢市|qq=draft|qq=draft}} 1006 Miyago 1-chome式内社研究会 編（1990）：294ページ (modern address: 1-3-19 Miyago, Ise City). The shrine is situated behind and to the right (northeast) of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月夜見宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'s main hall. The shrine grounds are surrounded by a moat on three sides, which is believed to be a remnant of a tributary of the {{ill|Miyagawa River (Mie)|ja|宮川 (三重県)|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. The enshrined deity is {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto no Mitama|ja|月夜見尊御魂|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (つきよみのみことのみたま). The shrine is located in Takagawara (高河原), an area near the Miyagawa River, and serves as a {{ill|guardian deity|ja|守護神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (守護神) for the land development of the surrounding region. Many ancient texts describe the enshrined deity as the Mitama (spirit) of {{ill|Tsukiyomi|ja|月読|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. However, the ''{{ill|Shinmei-chō Kōshō Saikō|ja|神名帳考證再考|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'' (''神名帳考證再考'') claims that the deity is actually {{ill|Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto|ja|倉稲魂命|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (倉稲魂命), the deity of grain and prosperity. nother text, ''{{ill|Ninomiya Kansa Enkaku Kō|ja|二宮管社沿革考|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'' (''二宮管社沿革考''), asserts that the original name of the shrine in the ''{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'' (延喜式神名帳) was "{{ill|Kawahara-ni-Masu-Kuninamino-Kami Jinja|ja|川原坐国生神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}", proving that its deity is {{ill|Kuninamino-Kami|ja|国生神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (国生神), the god of land formation.Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): pp. 295–296 The main hall follows {{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|ja|神明造|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (神明造, the {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}} architectural style) and has a wooden board roof ({{ill|Itabuki|ja|板葺|qq=draft|qq=draft}}), enclosed by a {{ill|Tamagaki|ja|玉垣|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (玉垣, sacred fence). Unlike most {{ill|Sessha|ja|摂社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}・{{ill|Massha|ja|末社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}・{{ill|Shokan-sha|ja|所管社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (摂社・末社・所管社, auxiliary shrines) of {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, which do not have an offering box ({{ill|Saisenbako|ja|賽銭箱|qq=draft|qq=draft}})Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p. 26, Takagawara Shrine uniquely has one. == History (歴史) == Based on the definition of a {{ill|Sessha|ja|摂社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (auxiliary shrine) within {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, this shrine was established before the compilation of the ''{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'' in {{ill|Enchō (era)|ja|延長|qq=draft|qq=draft}} 5 ({{ill|927|ja|927th year|qq=draft|qq=draft}}).Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p. 22 * The shrine is listed in that text as "{{ill|Kawahara-ni-Masu-Kuninamino-Kami Jinja|ja|川原坐国生神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}". * Additionally, it is mentioned as "{{ill|Takagawara-sha|ja|高河原社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}" in the ''{{ill|Toyuke Daijingu Gishiki-chō|ja|止由気宮儀式帳|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''. * Since that text dates back to {{ill|Enryaku (era)|ja|延暦|qq=draft|qq=draft}} 23 ({{ill|804|ja|804th year|qq=draft|qq=draft}}), this confirms that the shrine existed before that time. According to the ''{{ill|Ruiju Jingi Hongen|ja|類聚神祇本源|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'', reconstructions were regularly conducted from {{ill|Tokuji (era)|ja|徳治|qq=draft|qq=draft}} 1 ({{ill|1306|ja|1306年|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) onwards, under the supervision of a special Zōsai-shi (造替使, shrine reconstruction official).Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p. 296 The ''{{ill|Ninomiya Kansa Enkaku Kō|ja|二宮管社沿革考|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'' records that: {{quote|"According to the '''Ōei Tōkō Nikki (応永頭工日記)''', on the '''fourth day of the first month in '''{{ill|Ōei (era)|ja|応永|qq=draft|qq=draft}} 26 ({{ill|1419|ja|1419th year|qq=draft|qq=draft}})''', a great fire burned down '''{{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月夜見宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''', its small shrine, '''Kawahara-sha (高河原社)''', and '''Imibiya-den (忌火屋殿, the sacred fire hall)'''."}} Thus, the shrine was confirmed to have existed until it burned down on {{ill|January 4 (old calendar)|ja|1月4日 (旧暦)|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, corresponding to {{ill|January 29|ja|1月29日|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, 1419 (Julian calendar). --- === Reconstruction in the Edo Period=== After this destruction, the shrine fell into neglect, and by the Early Modern Period (近世), its location was lost. However, thanks to the efforts of {{ill|Kawabe Kiyonaga|ja|河邊精長|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (also known as {{ill|Ōnakatomi Kiyonaga|ja|大中臣精長|qq=draft|qq=draft}}), the Grand Chief Priest ({{ill|Ōgūji|ja|大宮司|qq=draft|qq=draft}}), the shrine was reconstructed on its present site on {{ill|Kanbun (era)|ja|寛文|qq=draft|qq=draft}} 3, {{ill|July 7 (old calendar)|ja|7月7日 (旧暦)|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (corresponding to {{ill|August 9|ja|8月9日|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|1663|ja|1663rd year|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in the Gregorian calendar). * ''{{ill|Shinmei Hisho|ja|神名秘書|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'' states: "Located in Numaki-go, Yamada Village. East of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月読宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}." * ''{{ill|Ruiju Jingi Hongen|ja|類聚神祇本源|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'' states: "East of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月読宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, within the same {{ill|Tamagaki|ja|玉垣|qq=draft|qq=draft}} fence." * ''{{ill|Ninomiya Kansa Enkaku Kō|ja|二宮管社沿革考|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'' claims that the original shrine site was actually the present-day {{ill|Suhara Taisha|ja|須原大社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in Ichinoki, Ise City.Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p. 295 --- === Reconstruction in the Modern Period=== * In {{ill|1911|ja|1911th year|qq=draft|qq=draft}} ({{ill|Meiji|ja|明治|1=Meiji era|qq=draft|qq=draft}} 44), the shrine was rebuilt.Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): p. 12 * In {{ill|1938|ja|1938th year|qq=draft|qq=draft}} ({{ill|Shōwa|ja|昭和|qq=draft|qq=draft}} 13), it was rebuilt again. * In {{ill|1957|ja|1957th year|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Shōwa 32), a major renovation was completed, and a sacred transfer ritual ({{ill|Sengyo|ja|遷御|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) was performed 20 years later.Sakurai (1991): p. 298 --- == Rites and Festivals (祭事) == * February – {{ill|Kinen-sai (祈年祭)|ja|祈年祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Harvest Prayer Festival) * June & December – {{ill|Tsukinami-sai (月次祭)|ja|月次祭|1=Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Monthly Festival) * October – {{ill|Kannamesai (神嘗祭)|ja|神嘗祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Offering of First Fruits Festival) * November – {{ill|Niiname-sai (新嘗祭)|ja|新嘗祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Thanksgiving Harvest Festival) These four major rituals are conducted on-site by a Negi (禰宜, senior priest) in巡回祭典 (巡回祭,巡行 ceremony format). The following six rites are performed remotely (遥祀, Yōshi): * January – {{ill|Saitan-sai (歳旦祭)|ja|歳旦祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (New Year's Festival) * January – {{ill|Genshi-sai (元始祭)|ja|元始祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Imperial Foundation Festival) * February 11 – {{ill|Kenkoku-kinen-sai (建国記念祭)|ja|建国記念祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (National Foundation Day) * May & August – {{ill|Kaze-no-Hi-no-Matsuri (風日祈祭)|ja|風日祈祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Wind and Rain Prayers) * December 23 – {{ill|Tenchō-sai (天長祭)|ja|天長祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Emperor's Birthday Festival) --- == Access (交通) == [[File:Tsukiyominomiyamae Bus Stop.jpg|thumb|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya-mae Bus Stop]] Public Transport: * 10-minute walk (550m) from {{ill|Ise City Station|ja|伊勢市駅|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (JR & Kintetsu).Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p. 33 * 4-minute walk (360m) from Shindō Bus Stop (三重交通). {{Shrine |name = Takagawara Shrine |religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Takagawara-jinja 02.jpg|270px]] |location = {{ill|Ise, Mie|ja|伊勢市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Miyago 1-chome 3-19, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|ja|三重県|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |latitude_deg = 34 | latitude_min = 29 | latitude_sec = 34.5 |longitude_deg = 136 | longitude_min = 42 | longitude_sec = 22.2 |map = Japan Mie |deity = {{ill|Tsukuyomi|ja|月夜見尊御魂|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |Rank = {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (small)
{{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮|1=Toyouke Daijingu|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}} Subordinate Shrine |founded = Before {{ill|Enryaku|ja|延暦|qq=draft|qq=draft}} 23 (804) |main_hall = {{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|ja|神明造|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |other_names = |pilgrimage_sites = |annual_festival = |rituals = {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} }} Takagawara Shrine (高河原神社, ''Takagawara Jinja''Shikinen Sengu Memorial Sengu-kan "[http://www.sengukan.jp/wp-content/themes/sengukan/shrine/area06.php Takagawara Shrine たかがわらじんじゃ>>]" (Accessed October 8, 2013).[[iTV]] "[http://www.yoitokose.jp/ise/encyclopedia/t0010.php Takagawara Shrine | Ise Grand Shrine Encyclopedia | Ise-Shima Travel Yoitokose]" (Accessed October 8, 2013)., also pronounced ''Takakawara Jinja''Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.39Gakken Publishing (2013): p.57) is a [[Shinto]] shrine located in Miyago, {{ill|Ise, Mie|ja|伊勢市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|ja|三重県|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|subordinate shrine (sessha/massha)|ja|摂末社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} of {{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮|1=Toyouke Daijingu|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (the Outer Shrine of {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) and classified as a {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. It Ranks 10th among the 16 subordinate shrines of the Outer ShrineUjiyamada City Hall (1929): pp.11–13.. The shrine is located within the precincts of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|ja|月夜見宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, which is a separate shrine of the Outer ShrineIse Bunka-sha (2008): p.38. == Overview (概要) == Located at {{ill|Mie Prefecture|ja|三重県|qq=draft|qq=draft}} {{ill|Ise, Mie|ja|伊勢市|qq=draft|qq=draft}} 1006 Miyago 1-chome式内社研究会 編（1990）：294ページ (modern address: 1-3-19 Miyago, Ise City). The shrine is situated behind and to the right (northeast) of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月夜見宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'s main hall. The shrine grounds are surrounded by a moat on three sides, which is believed to be a remnant of a tributary of the {{ill|Miyagawa River (Mie)|ja|宮川 (三重県)|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. The enshrined deity is {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto no Mitama|ja|月夜見尊御魂|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (つきよみのみことのみたま). The shrine is located in Takagawara (高河原), an area near the Miyagawa River, and serves as a {{ill|guardian deity|ja|守護神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (守護神) for the land development of the surrounding region. Many ancient texts describe the enshrined deity as the Mitama (spirit) of {{ill|Tsukiyomi|ja|月読|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. However, the ''{{ill|Shinmei-chō Kōshō Saikō|ja|神名帳考證再考|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'' (''神名帳考證再考'') claims that the deity is actually {{ill|Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto|ja|倉稲魂命|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (倉稲魂命), the deity of grain and prosperity. nother text, ''{{ill|Ninomiya Kansa Enkaku Kō|ja|二宮管社沿革考|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'' (''二宮管社沿革考''), asserts that the original name of the shrine in the ''{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'' (延喜式神名帳) was "{{ill|Kawahara-ni-Masu-Kuninamino-Kami Jinja|ja|川原坐国生神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}", proving that its deity is {{ill|Kuninamino-Kami|ja|国生神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (国生神), the god of land formation.Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): pp. 295–296 The main hall follows {{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|ja|神明造|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (神明造, the {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}} architectural style) and has a wooden board roof ({{ill|Itabuki|ja|板葺|qq=draft|qq=draft}}), enclosed by a {{ill|Tamagaki|ja|玉垣|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (玉垣, sacred fence). Unlike most {{ill|Sessha|ja|摂社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}・{{ill|Massha|ja|末社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}・{{ill|Shokan-sha|ja|所管社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (摂社・末社・所管社, auxiliary shrines) of {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, which do not have an offering box ({{ill|Saisenbako|ja|賽銭箱|qq=draft|qq=draft}})Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p. 26, Takagawara Shrine uniquely has one. == History (歴史) == Based on the definition of a {{ill|Sessha|ja|摂社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (auxiliary shrine) within {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, this shrine was established before the compilation of the ''{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'' in {{ill|Enchō (era)|ja|延長|qq=draft|qq=draft}} 5 ({{ill|927|ja|927th year|qq=draft|qq=draft}}).Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p. 22 * The shrine is listed in that text as "{{ill|Kawahara-ni-Masu-Kuninamino-Kami Jinja|ja|川原坐国生神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}". * Additionally, it is mentioned as "{{ill|Takagawara-sha|ja|高河原社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}" in the ''{{ill|Toyuke Daijingu Gishiki-chō|ja|止由気宮儀式帳|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''. * Since that text dates back to {{ill|Enryaku (era)|ja|延暦|qq=draft|qq=draft}} 23 ({{ill|804|ja|804th year|qq=draft|qq=draft}}), this confirms that the shrine existed before that time. According to the ''{{ill|Ruiju Jingi Hongen|ja|類聚神祇本源|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'', reconstructions were regularly conducted from {{ill|Tokuji (era)|ja|徳治|qq=draft|qq=draft}} 1 ({{ill|1306|ja|1306年|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) onwards, under the supervision of a special Zōsai-shi (造替使, shrine reconstruction official).Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p. 296 The ''{{ill|Ninomiya Kansa Enkaku Kō|ja|二宮管社沿革考|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'' records that: {{quote|"According to the '''Ōei Tōkō Nikki (応永頭工日記)''', on the '''fourth day of the first month in '''{{ill|Ōei (era)|ja|応永|qq=draft|qq=draft}} 26 ({{ill|1419|ja|1419th year|qq=draft|qq=draft}})''', a great fire burned down '''{{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月夜見宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''', its small shrine, '''Kawahara-sha (高河原社)''', and '''Imibiya-den (忌火屋殿, the sacred fire hall)'''."}} Thus, the shrine was confirmed to have existed until it burned down on {{ill|January 4 (old calendar)|ja|1月4日 (旧暦)|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, corresponding to {{ill|January 29|ja|1月29日|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, 1419 (Julian calendar). --- === Reconstruction in the Edo Period=== After this destruction, the shrine fell into neglect, and by the Early Modern Period (近世), its location was lost. However, thanks to the efforts of {{ill|Kawabe Kiyonaga|ja|河邊精長|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (also known as {{ill|Ōnakatomi Kiyonaga|ja|大中臣精長|qq=draft|qq=draft}}), the Grand Chief Priest ({{ill|Ōgūji|ja|大宮司|qq=draft|qq=draft}}), the shrine was reconstructed on its present site on {{ill|Kanbun (era)|ja|寛文|qq=draft|qq=draft}} 3, {{ill|July 7 (old calendar)|ja|7月7日 (旧暦)|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (corresponding to {{ill|August 9|ja|8月9日|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|1663|ja|1663rd year|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in the Gregorian calendar). * ''{{ill|Shinmei Hisho|ja|神名秘書|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'' states: "Located in Numaki-go, Yamada Village. East of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月読宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}." * ''{{ill|Ruiju Jingi Hongen|ja|類聚神祇本源|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'' states: "East of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月読宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, within the same {{ill|Tamagaki|ja|玉垣|qq=draft|qq=draft}} fence." * ''{{ill|Ninomiya Kansa Enkaku Kō|ja|二宮管社沿革考|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'' claims that the original shrine site was actually the present-day {{ill|Suhara Taisha|ja|須原大社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in Ichinoki, Ise City.Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p. 295 --- === Reconstruction in the Modern Period=== * In {{ill|1911|ja|1911th year|qq=draft|qq=draft}} ({{ill|Meiji|ja|明治|1=Meiji era|qq=draft|qq=draft}} 44), the shrine was rebuilt.Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): p. 12 * In {{ill|1938|ja|1938th year|qq=draft|qq=draft}} ({{ill|Shōwa|ja|昭和|qq=draft|qq=draft}} 13), it was rebuilt again. * In {{ill|1957|ja|1957th year|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Shōwa 32), a major renovation was completed, and a sacred transfer ritual ({{ill|Sengyo|ja|遷御|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) was performed 20 years later.Sakurai (1991): p. 298 --- == Rites and Festivals (祭事) == * February – {{ill|Kinen-sai (祈年祭)|ja|祈年祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Harvest Prayer Festival) * June & December – {{ill|Tsukinami-sai (月次祭)|ja|月次祭|1=Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Monthly Festival) * October – {{ill|Kannamesai (神嘗祭)|ja|神嘗祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Offering of First Fruits Festival) * November – {{ill|Niiname-sai (新嘗祭)|ja|新嘗祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Thanksgiving Harvest Festival) These four major rituals are conducted on-site by a Negi (禰宜, senior priest) in巡回祭典 (巡回祭,巡行 ceremony format). The following six rites are performed remotely (遥祀, Yōshi): * January – {{ill|Saitan-sai (歳旦祭)|ja|歳旦祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (New Year's Festival) * January – {{ill|Genshi-sai (元始祭)|ja|元始祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Imperial Foundation Festival) * February 11 – {{ill|Kenkoku-kinen-sai (建国記念祭)|ja|建国記念祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (National Foundation Day) * May & August – {{ill|Kaze-no-Hi-no-Matsuri (風日祈祭)|ja|風日祈祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Wind and Rain Prayers) * December 23 – {{ill|Tenchō-sai (天長祭)|ja|天長祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Emperor's Birthday Festival) --- == Access (交通) == [[File:Tsukiyominomiyamae Bus Stop.jpg|thumb|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya-mae Bus Stop]] Public Transport: * 10-minute walk (550m) from {{ill|Ise City Station|ja|伊勢市駅|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (JR & Kintetsu).Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p. 33 * 4-minute walk (360m) from Shindō Bus Stop (三重交通). Unlike most {{ill|Sessha|ja|摂社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}・{{ill|Massha|ja|末社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}・{{ill|Shokan-sha|ja|所管社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (摂社・末社・所管社, auxiliary shrines) of {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, which do not have an offering box ({{ill|Saisenbako|ja|賽銭箱|qq=draft|qq=draft}})Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p. 26, Takagawara Shrine uniquely has one. == History (歴史) == Based on the definition of a {{ill|Sessha|ja|摂社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (auxiliary shrine) within {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, this shrine was established before the compilation of the ''{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'' in {{ill|Enchō (era)|ja|延長|qq=draft|qq=draft}} 5 ({{ill|927|ja|927th year|qq=draft|qq=draft}}).Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p. 22 * The shrine is listed in that text as "{{ill|Kawahara-ni-Masu-Kuninamino-Kami Jinja|ja|川原坐国生神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}". * Additionally, it is mentioned as "{{ill|Takagawara-sha|ja|高河原社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}" in the ''{{ill|Toyuke Daijingu Gishiki-chō|ja|止由気宮儀式帳|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''. * Since that text dates back to {{ill|Enryaku (era)|ja|延暦|qq=draft|qq=draft}} 23 ({{ill|804|ja|804th year|qq=draft|qq=draft}}), this confirms that the shrine existed before that time. According to the ''{{ill|Ruiju Jingi Hongen|ja|類聚神祇本源|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'', reconstructions were regularly conducted from {{ill|Tokuji (era)|ja|徳治|qq=draft|qq=draft}} 1 ({{ill|1306|ja|1306年|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) onwards, under the supervision of a special Zōsai-shi (造替使, shrine reconstruction official).Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p. 296 The ''{{ill|Ninomiya Kansa Enkaku Kō|ja|二宮管社沿革考|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'' records that: {{quote|"According to the '''Ōei Tōkō Nikki (応永頭工日記)''', on the '''fourth day of the first month in '''{{ill|Ōei (era)|ja|応永|qq=draft|qq=draft}} 26 ({{ill|1419|ja|1419th year|qq=draft|qq=draft}})''', a great fire burned down '''{{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月夜見宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''', its small shrine, '''Kawahara-sha (高河原社)''', and '''Imibiya-den (忌火屋殿, the sacred fire hall)'''."}} Thus, the shrine was confirmed to have existed until it burned down on {{ill|January 4 (old calendar)|ja|1月4日 (旧暦)|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, corresponding to {{ill|January 29|ja|1月29日|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, 1419 (Julian calendar). --- === Reconstruction in the Edo Period=== After this destruction, the shrine fell into neglect, and by the Early Modern Period (近世), its location was lost. However, thanks to the efforts of {{ill|Kawabe Kiyonaga|ja|河邊精長|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (also known as {{ill|Ōnakatomi Kiyonaga|ja|大中臣精長|qq=draft|qq=draft}}), the Grand Chief Priest ({{ill|Ōgūji|ja|大宮司|qq=draft|qq=draft}}), the shrine was reconstructed on its present site on {{ill|Kanbun (era)|ja|寛文|qq=draft|qq=draft}} 3, {{ill|July 7 (old calendar)|ja|7月7日 (旧暦)|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (corresponding to {{ill|August 9|ja|8月9日|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|1663|ja|1663rd year|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in the Gregorian calendar). * ''{{ill|Shinmei Hisho|ja|神名秘書|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'' states: "Located in Numaki-go, Yamada Village. East of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月読宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}." * ''{{ill|Ruiju Jingi Hongen|ja|類聚神祇本源|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'' states: "East of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月読宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, within the same {{ill|Tamagaki|ja|玉垣|qq=draft|qq=draft}} fence." * ''{{ill|Ninomiya Kansa Enkaku Kō|ja|二宮管社沿革考|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'' claims that the original shrine site was actually the present-day {{ill|Suhara Taisha|ja|須原大社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in Ichinoki, Ise City.Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p. 295 --- === Reconstruction in the Modern Period=== * In {{ill|1911|ja|1911th year|qq=draft|qq=draft}} ({{ill|Meiji|ja|明治|1=Meiji era|qq=draft|qq=draft}} 44), the shrine was rebuilt.Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): p. 12 * In {{ill|1938|ja|1938th year|qq=draft|qq=draft}} ({{ill|Shōwa|ja|昭和|qq=draft|qq=draft}} 13), it was rebuilt again. * In {{ill|1957|ja|1957th year|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Shōwa 32), a major renovation was completed, and a sacred transfer ritual ({{ill|Sengyo|ja|遷御|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) was performed 20 years later.Sakurai (1991): p. 298 --- == Rites and Festivals (祭事) == * February – {{ill|Kinen-sai (祈年祭)|ja|祈年祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Harvest Prayer Festival) * June & December – {{ill|Tsukinami-sai (月次祭)|ja|月次祭|1=Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Monthly Festival) * October – {{ill|Kannamesai (神嘗祭)|ja|神嘗祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Offering of First Fruits Festival) * November – {{ill|Niiname-sai (新嘗祭)|ja|新嘗祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Thanksgiving Harvest Festival) These four major rituals are conducted on-site by a Negi (禰宜, senior priest) in巡回祭典 (巡回祭,巡行 ceremony format). The following six rites are performed remotely (遥祀, Yōshi): * January – {{ill|Saitan-sai (歳旦祭)|ja|歳旦祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (New Year's Festival) * January – {{ill|Genshi-sai (元始祭)|ja|元始祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Imperial Foundation Festival) * February 11 – {{ill|Kenkoku-kinen-sai (建国記念祭)|ja|建国記念祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (National Foundation Day) * May & August – {{ill|Kaze-no-Hi-no-Matsuri (風日祈祭)|ja|風日祈祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Wind and Rain Prayers) * December 23 – {{ill|Tenchō-sai (天長祭)|ja|天長祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Emperor's Birthday Festival) --- == Access (交通) == [[File:Tsukiyominomiyamae Bus Stop.jpg|thumb|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya-mae Bus Stop]] Public Transport: * 10-minute walk (550m) from {{ill|Ise City Station|ja|伊勢市駅|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (JR & Kintetsu).Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p. 33 * 4-minute walk (360m) from Shindō Bus Stop (三重交通). By Car: * Approx. 5 minutes (2.5km) from Ise Nishi IC (伊勢西IC, Ise Expressway). * Metered parking available near the entrance. --- == References == {{Reflist}} == 参考文献 == * 宇治山田市役所 編『宇治山田市史 上巻』宇治山田市役所、昭和4th year 1月20日、862p. * [[学研パブリッシング]]『伊勢神宮に行こう』Gakken Mook神社紀行セレクションvol.1、[[薗田稔]]監修、学研マーケティング、2013rd year 7月4日、82p. ISBN 978-4-05-610047-1 * [[櫻井勝之進]]『伊勢神宮の祖型と展開』[[国書刊行会]]、平成3rd year 11月30日、318p. ISBN 4-336-03296-3 * 式内社研究会 編『式内社調査報告 第六巻 東海道1』[[Kogakkan University]]出版部、平成2nd year 2月28日、690p. {{Shrine |name = Takagawara Shrine |religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Takagawara-jinja 02.jpg|270px]] |location = {{ill|Ise, Mie|ja|伊勢市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Miyago 1-chome 3-19, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|ja|三重県|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |latitude_deg = 34 | latitude_min = 29 | latitude_sec = 34.5 |longitude_deg = 136 | longitude_min = 42 | longitude_sec = 22.2 |map = Japan Mie |deity = {{ill|Tsukuyomi|ja|月夜見尊御魂|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |Rank = {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (small)
{{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮|1=Toyouke Daijingu|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}} Subordinate Shrine |founded = Before {{ill|Enryaku|ja|延暦|qq=draft|qq=draft}} 23 (804) |main_hall = {{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|ja|神明造|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |other_names = |pilgrimage_sites = |annual_festival = |rituals = {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} }} Takagawara Shrine (高河原神社, ''Takagawara Jinja''Shikinen Sengu Memorial Sengu-kan "[http://www.sengukan.jp/wp-content/themes/sengukan/shrine/area06.php Takagawara Shrine たかがわらじんじゃ>>]" (Accessed October 8, 2013).[[iTV]] "[http://www.yoitokose.jp/ise/encyclopedia/t0010.php Takagawara Shrine | Ise Grand Shrine Encyclopedia | Ise-Shima Travel Yoitokose]" (Accessed October 8, 2013)., also pronounced ''Takakawara Jinja''Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.39Gakken Publishing (2013): p.57) is a [[Shinto]] shrine located in Miyago, {{ill|Ise, Mie|ja|伊勢市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|ja|三重県|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|subordinate shrine (sessha/massha)|ja|摂末社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} of {{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮|1=Toyouke Daijingu|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (the Outer Shrine of {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) and classified as a {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. It Ranks 10th among the 16 subordinate shrines of the Outer ShrineUjiyamada City Hall (1929): pp.11–13.. The shrine is located within the precincts of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|ja|月夜見宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, which is a separate shrine of the Outer ShrineIse Bunka-sha (2008): p.38. == Overview (概要) == Located at {{ill|Mie Prefecture|ja|三重県|qq=draft|qq=draft}} {{ill|Ise, Mie|ja|伊勢市|qq=draft|qq=draft}} 1006 Miyago 1-chome式内社研究会 編（1990）：294ページ (modern address: 1-3-19 Miyago, Ise City). The shrine is situated behind and to the right (northeast) of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月夜見宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'s main hall. The shrine grounds are surrounded by a moat on three sides, which is believed to be a remnant of a tributary of the {{ill|Miyagawa River (Mie)|ja|宮川 (三重県)|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. The enshrined deity is {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto no Mitama|ja|月夜見尊御魂|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (つきよみのみことのみたま). The shrine is located in Takagawara (高河原), an area near the Miyagawa River, and serves as a {{ill|guardian deity|ja|守護神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (守護神) for the land development of the surrounding region. Many ancient texts describe the enshrined deity as the Mitama (spirit) of {{ill|Tsukiyomi|ja|月読|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. According to the ''{{ill|Ruiju Jingi Hongen|ja|類聚神祇本源|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'', reconstructions were regularly conducted from {{ill|Tokuji (era)|ja|徳治|qq=draft|qq=draft}} 1 ({{ill|1306|ja|1306年|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) onwards, under the supervision of a special Zōsai-shi (造替使, shrine reconstruction official).Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p. 296 The ''{{ill|Ninomiya Kansa Enkaku Kō|ja|二宮管社沿革考|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'' records that: {{quote|"According to the '''Ōei Tōkō Nikki (応永頭工日記)''', on the '''fourth day of the first month in '''{{ill|Ōei (era)|ja|応永|qq=draft|qq=draft}} 26 ({{ill|1419|ja|1419th year|qq=draft|qq=draft}})''', a great fire burned down '''{{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月夜見宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''', its small shrine, '''Kawahara-sha (高河原社)''', and '''Imibiya-den (忌火屋殿, the sacred fire hall)'''."}} Thus, the shrine was confirmed to have existed until it burned down on {{ill|January 4 (old calendar)|ja|1月4日 (旧暦)|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, corresponding to {{ill|January 29|ja|1月29日|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, 1419 (Julian calendar). --- === Reconstruction in the Edo Period=== After this destruction, the shrine fell into neglect, and by the Early Modern Period (近世), its location was lost. However, thanks to the efforts of {{ill|Kawabe Kiyonaga|ja|河邊精長|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (also known as {{ill|Ōnakatomi Kiyonaga|ja|大中臣精長|qq=draft|qq=draft}}), the Grand Chief Priest ({{ill|Ōgūji|ja|大宮司|qq=draft|qq=draft}}), the shrine was reconstructed on its present site on {{ill|Kanbun (era)|ja|寛文|qq=draft|qq=draft}} 3, {{ill|July 7 (old calendar)|ja|7月7日 (旧暦)|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (corresponding to {{ill|August 9|ja|8月9日|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|1663|ja|1663rd year|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in the Gregorian calendar). * ''{{ill|Shinmei Hisho|ja|神名秘書|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'' states: "Located in Numaki-go, Yamada Village. East of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月読宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}." * ''{{ill|Ruiju Jingi Hongen|ja|類聚神祇本源|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'' states: "East of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月読宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, within the same {{ill|Tamagaki|ja|玉垣|qq=draft|qq=draft}} fence." * ''{{ill|Ninomiya Kansa Enkaku Kō|ja|二宮管社沿革考|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'' claims that the original shrine site was actually the present-day {{ill|Suhara Taisha|ja|須原大社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in Ichinoki, Ise City.Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p. 295 --- === Reconstruction in the Modern Period=== * In {{ill|1911|ja|1911th year|qq=draft|qq=draft}} ({{ill|Meiji|ja|明治|1=Meiji era|qq=draft|qq=draft}} 44), the shrine was rebuilt.Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): p. 12 * In {{ill|1938|ja|1938th year|qq=draft|qq=draft}} ({{ill|Shōwa|ja|昭和|qq=draft|qq=draft}} 13), it was rebuilt again. * In {{ill|1957|ja|1957th year|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Shōwa 32), a major renovation was completed, and a sacred transfer ritual ({{ill|Sengyo|ja|遷御|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) was performed 20 years later.Sakurai (1991): p. 298 --- == Rites and Festivals (祭事) == * February – {{ill|Kinen-sai (祈年祭)|ja|祈年祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Harvest Prayer Festival) * June & December – {{ill|Tsukinami-sai (月次祭)|ja|月次祭|1=Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Monthly Festival) * October – {{ill|Kannamesai (神嘗祭)|ja|神嘗祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Offering of First Fruits Festival) * November – {{ill|Niiname-sai (新嘗祭)|ja|新嘗祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Thanksgiving Harvest Festival) These four major rituals are conducted on-site by a Negi (禰宜, senior priest) in巡回祭典 (巡回祭,巡行 ceremony format). The following six rites are performed remotely (遥祀, Yōshi): * January – {{ill|Saitan-sai (歳旦祭)|ja|歳旦祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (New Year's Festival) * January – {{ill|Genshi-sai (元始祭)|ja|元始祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Imperial Foundation Festival) * February 11 – {{ill|Kenkoku-kinen-sai (建国記念祭)|ja|建国記念祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (National Foundation Day) * May & August – {{ill|Kaze-no-Hi-no-Matsuri (風日祈祭)|ja|風日祈祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Wind and Rain Prayers) * December 23 – {{ill|Tenchō-sai (天長祭)|ja|天長祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Emperor's Birthday Festival) --- == Access (交通) == [[File:Tsukiyominomiyamae Bus Stop.jpg|thumb|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya-mae Bus Stop]] Public Transport: * 10-minute walk (550m) from {{ill|Ise City Station|ja|伊勢市駅|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (JR & Kintetsu).Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p. 33 * 4-minute walk (360m) from Shindō Bus Stop (三重交通). By Car: * Approx. 5 minutes (2.5km) from Ise Nishi IC (伊勢西IC, Ise Expressway). * Metered parking available near the entrance. --- == References == {{Reflist}} == 参考文献 == * 宇治山田市役所 編『宇治山田市史 上巻』宇治山田市役所、昭和4th year 1月20日、862p. * [[学研パブリッシング]]『伊勢神宮に行こう』Gakken Mook神社紀行セレクションvol.1、[[薗田稔]]監修、学研マーケティング、2013rd year 7月4日、82p. {{Shrine |name = Takagawara Shrine |religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Takagawara-jinja 02.jpg|270px]] |location = {{ill|Ise, Mie|ja|伊勢市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Miyago 1-chome 3-19, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|ja|三重県|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |latitude_deg = 34 | latitude_min = 29 | latitude_sec = 34.5 |longitude_deg = 136 | longitude_min = 42 | longitude_sec = 22.2 |map = Japan Mie |deity = {{ill|Tsukuyomi|ja|月夜見尊御魂|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |Rank = {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (small)
{{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮|1=Toyouke Daijingu|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}} Subordinate Shrine |founded = Before {{ill|Enryaku|ja|延暦|qq=draft|qq=draft}} 23 (804) |main_hall = {{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|ja|神明造|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |other_names = |pilgrimage_sites = |annual_festival = |rituals = {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} }} Takagawara Shrine (高河原神社, ''Takagawara Jinja''Shikinen Sengu Memorial Sengu-kan "[http://www.sengukan.jp/wp-content/themes/sengukan/shrine/area06.php Takagawara Shrine たかがわらじんじゃ>>]" (Accessed October 8, 2013).[[iTV]] "[http://www.yoitokose.jp/ise/encyclopedia/t0010.php Takagawara Shrine | Ise Grand Shrine Encyclopedia | Ise-Shima Travel Yoitokose]" (Accessed October 8, 2013)., also pronounced ''Takakawara Jinja''Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.39Gakken Publishing (2013): p.57) is a [[Shinto]] shrine located in Miyago, {{ill|Ise, Mie|ja|伊勢市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|ja|三重県|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|subordinate shrine (sessha/massha)|ja|摂末社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} of {{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮|1=Toyouke Daijingu|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (the Outer Shrine of {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) and classified as a {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. It Ranks 10th among the 16 subordinate shrines of the Outer ShrineUjiyamada City Hall (1929): pp.11–13.. The shrine is located within the precincts of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|ja|月夜見宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, which is a separate shrine of the Outer ShrineIse Bunka-sha (2008): p.38. == Overview (概要) == Located at {{ill|Mie Prefecture|ja|三重県|qq=draft|qq=draft}} {{ill|Ise, Mie|ja|伊勢市|qq=draft|qq=draft}} 1006 Miyago 1-chome式内社研究会 編（1990）：294ページ (modern address: 1-3-19 Miyago, Ise City). The shrine is situated behind and to the right (northeast) of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月夜見宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'s main hall. The shrine grounds are surrounded by a moat on three sides, which is believed to be a remnant of a tributary of the {{ill|Miyagawa River (Mie)|ja|宮川 (三重県)|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. The enshrined deity is {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto no Mitama|ja|月夜見尊御魂|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (つきよみのみことのみたま). The shrine is located in Takagawara (高河原), an area near the Miyagawa River, and serves as a {{ill|guardian deity|ja|守護神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (守護神) for the land development of the surrounding region. Many ancient texts describe the enshrined deity as the Mitama (spirit) of {{ill|Tsukiyomi|ja|月読|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. However, the ''{{ill|Shinmei-chō Kōshō Saikō|ja|神名帳考證再考|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'' (''神名帳考證再考'') claims that the deity is actually {{ill|Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto|ja|倉稲魂命|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (倉稲魂命), the deity of grain and prosperity. nother text, ''{{ill|Ninomiya Kansa Enkaku Kō|ja|二宮管社沿革考|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'' (''二宮管社沿革考''), asserts that the original name of the shrine in the ''{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'' (延喜式神名帳) was "{{ill|Kawahara-ni-Masu-Kuninamino-Kami Jinja|ja|川原坐国生神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}", proving that its deity is {{ill|Kuninamino-Kami|ja|国生神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (国生神), the god of land formation.Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): pp. 295–296 The main hall follows {{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|ja|神明造|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (神明造, the {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}} architectural style) and has a wooden board roof ({{ill|Itabuki|ja|板葺|qq=draft|qq=draft}}), enclosed by a {{ill|Tamagaki|ja|玉垣|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (玉垣, sacred fence). Unlike most {{ill|Sessha|ja|摂社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}・{{ill|Massha|ja|末社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}・{{ill|Shokan-sha|ja|所管社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (摂社・末社・所管社, auxiliary shrines) of {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, which do not have an offering box ({{ill|Saisenbako|ja|賽銭箱|qq=draft|qq=draft}})Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p. 26, Takagawara Shrine uniquely has one. == History (歴史) == Based on the definition of a {{ill|Sessha|ja|摂社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (auxiliary shrine) within {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, this shrine was established before the compilation of the ''{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'' in {{ill|Enchō (era)|ja|延長|qq=draft|qq=draft}} 5 ({{ill|927|ja|927th year|qq=draft|qq=draft}}).Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p. 22 * The shrine is listed in that text as "{{ill|Kawahara-ni-Masu-Kuninamino-Kami Jinja|ja|川原坐国生神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}". * Additionally, it is mentioned as "{{ill|Takagawara-sha|ja|高河原社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}" in the ''{{ill|Toyuke Daijingu Gishiki-chō|ja|止由気宮儀式帳|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''. * Since that text dates back to {{ill|Enryaku (era)|ja|延暦|qq=draft|qq=draft}} 23 ({{ill|804|ja|804th year|qq=draft|qq=draft}}), this confirms that the shrine existed before that time. According to the ''{{ill|Ruiju Jingi Hongen|ja|類聚神祇本源|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'', reconstructions were regularly conducted from {{ill|Tokuji (era)|ja|徳治|qq=draft|qq=draft}} 1 ({{ill|1306|ja|1306年|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) onwards, under the supervision of a special Zōsai-shi (造替使, shrine reconstruction official).Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p. 296 The ''{{ill|Ninomiya Kansa Enkaku Kō|ja|二宮管社沿革考|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'' records that: {{quote|"According to the '''Ōei Tōkō Nikki (応永頭工日記)''', on the '''fourth day of the first month in '''{{ill|Ōei (era)|ja|応永|qq=draft|qq=draft}} 26 ({{ill|1419|ja|1419th year|qq=draft|qq=draft}})''', a great fire burned down '''{{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月夜見宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''', its small shrine, '''Kawahara-sha (高河原社)''', and '''Imibiya-den (忌火屋殿, the sacred fire hall)'''."}} Thus, the shrine was confirmed to have existed until it burned down on {{ill|January 4 (old calendar)|ja|1月4日 (旧暦)|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, corresponding to {{ill|January 29|ja|1月29日|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, 1419 (Julian calendar). --- === Reconstruction in the Edo Period=== After this destruction, the shrine fell into neglect, and by the Early Modern Period (近世), its location was lost. However, thanks to the efforts of {{ill|Kawabe Kiyonaga|ja|河邊精長|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (also known as {{ill|Ōnakatomi Kiyonaga|ja|大中臣精長|qq=draft|qq=draft}}), the Grand Chief Priest ({{ill|Ōgūji|ja|大宮司|qq=draft|qq=draft}}), the shrine was reconstructed on its present site on {{ill|Kanbun (era)|ja|寛文|qq=draft|qq=draft}} 3, {{ill|July 7 (old calendar)|ja|7月7日 (旧暦)|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (corresponding to {{ill|August 9|ja|8月9日|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|1663|ja|1663rd year|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in the Gregorian calendar). * ''{{ill|Shinmei Hisho|ja|神名秘書|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'' states: "Located in Numaki-go, Yamada Village. East of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月読宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}." * ''{{ill|Ruiju Jingi Hongen|ja|類聚神祇本源|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'' states: "East of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月読宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, within the same {{ill|Tamagaki|ja|玉垣|qq=draft|qq=draft}} fence." * ''{{ill|Ninomiya Kansa Enkaku Kō|ja|二宮管社沿革考|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'' claims that the original shrine site was actually the present-day {{ill|Suhara Taisha|ja|須原大社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in Ichinoki, Ise City.Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p. 295 --- === Reconstruction in the Modern Period=== * In {{ill|1911|ja|1911th year|qq=draft|qq=draft}} ({{ill|Meiji|ja|明治|1=Meiji era|qq=draft|qq=draft}} 44), the shrine was rebuilt.Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): p. 12 * In {{ill|1938|ja|1938th year|qq=draft|qq=draft}} ({{ill|Shōwa|ja|昭和|qq=draft|qq=draft}} 13), it was rebuilt again. * In {{ill|1957|ja|1957th year|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Shōwa 32), a major renovation was completed, and a sacred transfer ritual ({{ill|Sengyo|ja|遷御|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) was performed 20 years later.Sakurai (1991): p. 298 --- == Rites and Festivals (祭事) == * February – {{ill|Kinen-sai (祈年祭)|ja|祈年祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Harvest Prayer Festival) * June & December – {{ill|Tsukinami-sai (月次祭)|ja|月次祭|1=Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Monthly Festival) * October – {{ill|Kannamesai (神嘗祭)|ja|神嘗祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Offering of First Fruits Festival) * November – {{ill|Niiname-sai (新嘗祭)|ja|新嘗祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Thanksgiving Harvest Festival) These four major rituals are conducted on-site by a Negi (禰宜, senior priest) in巡回祭典 (巡回祭,巡行 ceremony format). The following six rites are performed remotely (遥祀, Yōshi): * January – {{ill|Saitan-sai (歳旦祭)|ja|歳旦祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (New Year's Festival) * January – {{ill|Genshi-sai (元始祭)|ja|元始祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Imperial Foundation Festival) * February 11 – {{ill|Kenkoku-kinen-sai (建国記念祭)|ja|建国記念祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (National Foundation Day) * May & August – {{ill|Kaze-no-Hi-no-Matsuri (風日祈祭)|ja|風日祈祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Wind and Rain Prayers) * December 23 – {{ill|Tenchō-sai (天長祭)|ja|天長祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Emperor's Birthday Festival) --- == Access (交通) == [[File:Tsukiyominomiyamae Bus Stop.jpg|thumb|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya-mae Bus Stop]] Public Transport: * 10-minute walk (550m) from {{ill|Ise City Station|ja|伊勢市駅|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (JR & Kintetsu).Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p. 33 * 4-minute walk (360m) from Shindō Bus Stop (三重交通). {{Shrine |name = Takagawara Shrine |religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Takagawara-jinja 02.jpg|270px]] |location = {{ill|Ise, Mie|ja|伊勢市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Miyago 1-chome 3-19, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|ja|三重県|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |latitude_deg = 34 | latitude_min = 29 | latitude_sec = 34.5 |longitude_deg = 136 | longitude_min = 42 | longitude_sec = 22.2 |map = Japan Mie |deity = {{ill|Tsukuyomi|ja|月夜見尊御魂|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |Rank = {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (small)
{{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮|1=Toyouke Daijingu|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}} Subordinate Shrine |founded = Before {{ill|Enryaku|ja|延暦|qq=draft|qq=draft}} 23 (804) |main_hall = {{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|ja|神明造|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |other_names = |pilgrimage_sites = |annual_festival = |rituals = {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} }} Takagawara Shrine (高河原神社, ''Takagawara Jinja''Shikinen Sengu Memorial Sengu-kan "[http://www.sengukan.jp/wp-content/themes/sengukan/shrine/area06.php Takagawara Shrine たかがわらじんじゃ>>]" (Accessed October 8, 2013).[[iTV]] "[http://www.yoitokose.jp/ise/encyclopedia/t0010.php Takagawara Shrine | Ise Grand Shrine Encyclopedia | Ise-Shima Travel Yoitokose]" (Accessed October 8, 2013)., also pronounced ''Takakawara Jinja''Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.39Gakken Publishing (2013): p.57) is a [[Shinto]] shrine located in Miyago, {{ill|Ise, Mie|ja|伊勢市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|ja|三重県|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|subordinate shrine (sessha/massha)|ja|摂末社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} of {{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮|1=Toyouke Daijingu|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (the Outer Shrine of {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) and classified as a {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. It Ranks 10th among the 16 subordinate shrines of the Outer ShrineUjiyamada City Hall (1929): pp.11–13.. The shrine is located within the precincts of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|ja|月夜見宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, which is a separate shrine of the Outer ShrineIse Bunka-sha (2008): p.38. == Overview (概要) == Located at {{ill|Mie Prefecture|ja|三重県|qq=draft|qq=draft}} {{ill|Ise, Mie|ja|伊勢市|qq=draft|qq=draft}} 1006 Miyago 1-chome式内社研究会 編（1990）：294ページ (modern address: 1-3-19 Miyago, Ise City). The shrine is situated behind and to the right (northeast) of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月夜見宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'s main hall. The shrine grounds are surrounded by a moat on three sides, which is believed to be a remnant of a tributary of the {{ill|Miyagawa River (Mie)|ja|宮川 (三重県)|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. The enshrined deity is {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto no Mitama|ja|月夜見尊御魂|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (つきよみのみことのみたま). The shrine is located in Takagawara (高河原), an area near the Miyagawa River, and serves as a {{ill|guardian deity|ja|守護神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (守護神) for the land development of the surrounding region. Many ancient texts describe the enshrined deity as the Mitama (spirit) of {{ill|Tsukiyomi|ja|月読|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. However, the ''{{ill|Shinmei-chō Kōshō Saikō|ja|神名帳考證再考|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'' (''神名帳考證再考'') claims that the deity is actually {{ill|Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto|ja|倉稲魂命|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (倉稲魂命), the deity of grain and prosperity. nother text, ''{{ill|Ninomiya Kansa Enkaku Kō|ja|二宮管社沿革考|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'' (''二宮管社沿革考''), asserts that the original name of the shrine in the ''{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'' (延喜式神名帳) was "{{ill|Kawahara-ni-Masu-Kuninamino-Kami Jinja|ja|川原坐国生神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}", proving that its deity is {{ill|Kuninamino-Kami|ja|国生神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (国生神), the god of land formation.Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): pp. 295–296 The main hall follows {{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|ja|神明造|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (神明造, the {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}} architectural style) and has a wooden board roof ({{ill|Itabuki|ja|板葺|qq=draft|qq=draft}}), enclosed by a {{ill|Tamagaki|ja|玉垣|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (玉垣, sacred fence). Unlike most {{ill|Sessha|ja|摂社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}・{{ill|Massha|ja|末社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}・{{ill|Shokan-sha|ja|所管社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (摂社・末社・所管社, auxiliary shrines) of {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, which do not have an offering box ({{ill|Saisenbako|ja|賽銭箱|qq=draft|qq=draft}})Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p. 26, Takagawara Shrine uniquely has one. == History (歴史) == Based on the definition of a {{ill|Sessha|ja|摂社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (auxiliary shrine) within {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, this shrine was established before the compilation of the ''{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'' in {{ill|Enchō (era)|ja|延長|qq=draft|qq=draft}} 5 ({{ill|927|ja|927th year|qq=draft|qq=draft}}).Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p. 22 * The shrine is listed in that text as "{{ill|Kawahara-ni-Masu-Kuninamino-Kami Jinja|ja|川原坐国生神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}". * Additionally, it is mentioned as "{{ill|Takagawara-sha|ja|高河原社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}" in the ''{{ill|Toyuke Daijingu Gishiki-chō|ja|止由気宮儀式帳|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''. * Since that text dates back to {{ill|Enryaku (era)|ja|延暦|qq=draft|qq=draft}} 23 ({{ill|804|ja|804th year|qq=draft|qq=draft}}), this confirms that the shrine existed before that time. According to the ''{{ill|Ruiju Jingi Hongen|ja|類聚神祇本源|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'', reconstructions were regularly conducted from {{ill|Tokuji (era)|ja|徳治|qq=draft|qq=draft}} 1 ({{ill|1306|ja|1306年|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) onwards, under the supervision of a special Zōsai-shi (造替使, shrine reconstruction official).Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p. 296 The ''{{ill|Ninomiya Kansa Enkaku Kō|ja|二宮管社沿革考|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'' records that: {{quote|"According to the '''Ōei Tōkō Nikki (応永頭工日記)''', on the '''fourth day of the first month in '''{{ill|Ōei (era)|ja|応永|qq=draft|qq=draft}} 26 ({{ill|1419|ja|1419th year|qq=draft|qq=draft}})''', a great fire burned down '''{{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月夜見宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''', its small shrine, '''Kawahara-sha (高河原社)''', and '''Imibiya-den (忌火屋殿, the sacred fire hall)'''."}} Thus, the shrine was confirmed to have existed until it burned down on {{ill|January 4 (old calendar)|ja|1月4日 (旧暦)|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, corresponding to {{ill|January 29|ja|1月29日|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, 1419 (Julian calendar). --- === Reconstruction in the Edo Period=== After this destruction, the shrine fell into neglect, and by the Early Modern Period (近世), its location was lost. However, thanks to the efforts of {{ill|Kawabe Kiyonaga|ja|河邊精長|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (also known as {{ill|Ōnakatomi Kiyonaga|ja|大中臣精長|qq=draft|qq=draft}}), the Grand Chief Priest ({{ill|Ōgūji|ja|大宮司|qq=draft|qq=draft}}), the shrine was reconstructed on its present site on {{ill|Kanbun (era)|ja|寛文|qq=draft|qq=draft}} 3, {{ill|July 7 (old calendar)|ja|7月7日 (旧暦)|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (corresponding to {{ill|August 9|ja|8月9日|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|1663|ja|1663rd year|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in the Gregorian calendar). * ''{{ill|Shinmei Hisho|ja|神名秘書|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'' states: "Located in Numaki-go, Yamada Village. East of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月読宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}." * ''{{ill|Ruiju Jingi Hongen|ja|類聚神祇本源|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'' states: "East of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月読宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, within the same {{ill|Tamagaki|ja|玉垣|qq=draft|qq=draft}} fence." * ''{{ill|Ninomiya Kansa Enkaku Kō|ja|二宮管社沿革考|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'' claims that the original shrine site was actually the present-day {{ill|Suhara Taisha|ja|須原大社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in Ichinoki, Ise City.Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p. 295 --- === Reconstruction in the Modern Period=== * In {{ill|1911|ja|1911th year|qq=draft|qq=draft}} ({{ill|Meiji|ja|明治|1=Meiji era|qq=draft|qq=draft}} 44), the shrine was rebuilt.Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): p. 12 * In {{ill|1938|ja|1938th year|qq=draft|qq=draft}} ({{ill|Shōwa|ja|昭和|qq=draft|qq=draft}} 13), it was rebuilt again. * In {{ill|1957|ja|1957th year|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Shōwa 32), a major renovation was completed, and a sacred transfer ritual ({{ill|Sengyo|ja|遷御|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) was performed 20 years later.Sakurai (1991): p. 298 --- == Rites and Festivals (祭事) == * February – {{ill|Kinen-sai (祈年祭)|ja|祈年祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Harvest Prayer Festival) * June & December – {{ill|Tsukinami-sai (月次祭)|ja|月次祭|1=Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Monthly Festival) * October – {{ill|Kannamesai (神嘗祭)|ja|神嘗祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Offering of First Fruits Festival) * November – {{ill|Niiname-sai (新嘗祭)|ja|新嘗祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Thanksgiving Harvest Festival) These four major rituals are conducted on-site by a Negi (禰宜, senior priest) in巡回祭典 (巡回祭,巡行 ceremony format). The following six rites are performed remotely (遥祀, Yōshi): * January – {{ill|Saitan-sai (歳旦祭)|ja|歳旦祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (New Year's Festival) * January – {{ill|Genshi-sai (元始祭)|ja|元始祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Imperial Foundation Festival) * February 11 – {{ill|Kenkoku-kinen-sai (建国記念祭)|ja|建国記念祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (National Foundation Day) * May & August – {{ill|Kaze-no-Hi-no-Matsuri (風日祈祭)|ja|風日祈祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Wind and Rain Prayers) * December 23 – {{ill|Tenchō-sai (天長祭)|ja|天長祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Emperor's Birthday Festival) --- == Access (交通) == [[File:Tsukiyominomiyamae Bus Stop.jpg|thumb|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya-mae Bus Stop]] Public Transport: * 10-minute walk (550m) from {{ill|Ise City Station|ja|伊勢市駅|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (JR & Kintetsu).Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p. 33 * 4-minute walk (360m) from Shindō Bus Stop (三重交通). Unlike most {{ill|Sessha|ja|摂社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}・{{ill|Massha|ja|末社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}・{{ill|Shokan-sha|ja|所管社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (摂社・末社・所管社, auxiliary shrines) of {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, which do not have an offering box ({{ill|Saisenbako|ja|賽銭箱|qq=draft|qq=draft}})Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p. 26, Takagawara Shrine uniquely has one. == History (歴史) == Based on the definition of a {{ill|Sessha|ja|摂社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (auxiliary shrine) within {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, this shrine was established before the compilation of the ''{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'' in {{ill|Enchō (era)|ja|延長|qq=draft|qq=draft}} 5 ({{ill|927|ja|927th year|qq=draft|qq=draft}}).Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p. 22 * The shrine is listed in that text as "{{ill|Kawahara-ni-Masu-Kuninamino-Kami Jinja|ja|川原坐国生神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}". * Additionally, it is mentioned as "{{ill|Takagawara-sha|ja|高河原社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}" in the ''{{ill|Toyuke Daijingu Gishiki-chō|ja|止由気宮儀式帳|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''. * Since that text dates back to {{ill|Enryaku (era)|ja|延暦|qq=draft|qq=draft}} 23 ({{ill|804|ja|804th year|qq=draft|qq=draft}}), this confirms that the shrine existed before that time. According to the ''{{ill|Ruiju Jingi Hongen|ja|類聚神祇本源|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'', reconstructions were regularly conducted from {{ill|Tokuji (era)|ja|徳治|qq=draft|qq=draft}} 1 ({{ill|1306|ja|1306年|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) onwards, under the supervision of a special Zōsai-shi (造替使, shrine reconstruction official).Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p. 296 The ''{{ill|Ninomiya Kansa Enkaku Kō|ja|二宮管社沿革考|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'' records that: {{quote|"According to the '''Ōei Tōkō Nikki (応永頭工日記)''', on the '''fourth day of the first month in '''{{ill|Ōei (era)|ja|応永|qq=draft|qq=draft}} 26 ({{ill|1419|ja|1419th year|qq=draft|qq=draft}})''', a great fire burned down '''{{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月夜見宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''', its small shrine, '''Kawahara-sha (高河原社)''', and '''Imibiya-den (忌火屋殿, the sacred fire hall)'''."}} Thus, the shrine was confirmed to have existed until it burned down on {{ill|January 4 (old calendar)|ja|1月4日 (旧暦)|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, corresponding to {{ill|January 29|ja|1月29日|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, 1419 (Julian calendar). --- === Reconstruction in the Edo Period=== After this destruction, the shrine fell into neglect, and by the Early Modern Period (近世), its location was lost. However, thanks to the efforts of {{ill|Kawabe Kiyonaga|ja|河邊精長|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (also known as {{ill|Ōnakatomi Kiyonaga|ja|大中臣精長|qq=draft|qq=draft}}), the Grand Chief Priest ({{ill|Ōgūji|ja|大宮司|qq=draft|qq=draft}}), the shrine was reconstructed on its present site on {{ill|Kanbun (era)|ja|寛文|qq=draft|qq=draft}} 3, {{ill|July 7 (old calendar)|ja|7月7日 (旧暦)|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (corresponding to {{ill|August 9|ja|8月9日|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|1663|ja|1663rd year|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in the Gregorian calendar). * ''{{ill|Shinmei Hisho|ja|神名秘書|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'' states: "Located in Numaki-go, Yamada Village. East of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月読宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}." * ''{{ill|Ruiju Jingi Hongen|ja|類聚神祇本源|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'' states: "East of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月読宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, within the same {{ill|Tamagaki|ja|玉垣|qq=draft|qq=draft}} fence." * ''{{ill|Ninomiya Kansa Enkaku Kō|ja|二宮管社沿革考|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'' claims that the original shrine site was actually the present-day {{ill|Suhara Taisha|ja|須原大社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in Ichinoki, Ise City.Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p. 295 --- === Reconstruction in the Modern Period=== * In {{ill|1911|ja|1911th year|qq=draft|qq=draft}} ({{ill|Meiji|ja|明治|1=Meiji era|qq=draft|qq=draft}} 44), the shrine was rebuilt.Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): p. 12 * In {{ill|1938|ja|1938th year|qq=draft|qq=draft}} ({{ill|Shōwa|ja|昭和|qq=draft|qq=draft}} 13), it was rebuilt again. * In {{ill|1957|ja|1957th year|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Shōwa 32), a major renovation was completed, and a sacred transfer ritual ({{ill|Sengyo|ja|遷御|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) was performed 20 years later.Sakurai (1991): p. 298 --- == Rites and Festivals (祭事) == * February – {{ill|Kinen-sai (祈年祭)|ja|祈年祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Harvest Prayer Festival) * June & December – {{ill|Tsukinami-sai (月次祭)|ja|月次祭|1=Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Monthly Festival) * October – {{ill|Kannamesai (神嘗祭)|ja|神嘗祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Offering of First Fruits Festival) * November – {{ill|Niiname-sai (新嘗祭)|ja|新嘗祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Thanksgiving Harvest Festival) These four major rituals are conducted on-site by a Negi (禰宜, senior priest) in巡回祭典 (巡回祭,巡行 ceremony format). The following six rites are performed remotely (遥祀, Yōshi): * January – {{ill|Saitan-sai (歳旦祭)|ja|歳旦祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (New Year's Festival) * January – {{ill|Genshi-sai (元始祭)|ja|元始祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Imperial Foundation Festival) * February 11 – {{ill|Kenkoku-kinen-sai (建国記念祭)|ja|建国記念祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (National Foundation Day) * May & August – {{ill|Kaze-no-Hi-no-Matsuri (風日祈祭)|ja|風日祈祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Wind and Rain Prayers) * December 23 – {{ill|Tenchō-sai (天長祭)|ja|天長祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Emperor's Birthday Festival) --- == Access (交通) == [[File:Tsukiyominomiyamae Bus Stop.jpg|thumb|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya-mae Bus Stop]] Public Transport: * 10-minute walk (550m) from {{ill|Ise City Station|ja|伊勢市駅|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (JR & Kintetsu).Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p. 33 * 4-minute walk (360m) from Shindō Bus Stop (三重交通). By Car: * Approx. 5 minutes (2.5km) from Ise Nishi IC (伊勢西IC, Ise Expressway). * Metered parking available near the entrance. --- == References == {{Reflist}} == 参考文献 == * 宇治山田市役所 編『宇治山田市史 上巻』宇治山田市役所、昭和4th year 1月20日、862p. * [[学研パブリッシング]]『伊勢神宮に行こう』Gakken Mook神社紀行セレクションvol.1、[[薗田稔]]監修、学研マーケティング、2013rd year 7月4日、82p. ISBN 978-4-05-610047-1 * [[櫻井勝之進]]『伊勢神宮の祖型と展開』[[国書刊行会]]、平成3rd year 11月30日、318p. ISBN 4-336-03296-3 * 式内社研究会 編『式内社調査報告 第六巻 東海道1』[[Kogakkan University]]出版部、平成2nd year 2月28日、690p. ISBN 4-87644-080-8 * 『お伊勢さん125社めぐり』別冊『伊勢人』、[[伊勢文化舎]]、平成20th year 12月23日、151p. ISBN 978-4-900759-37-4 == See Also == * {{ill|List of Shikinaisha in Ise Province|ja|伊勢国の式内社一覧|1=List of Shikinaisha in Ise Province|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|List of 125 Shrines of Ise|ja|神宮125社の一覧|lt=List of 125 Shrines of Ise|1=List of Shikinaisha in Ise Province|3=伊勢国の式内社一覧|1=List of Shikinaisha in Ise Province|qq=draft|qq=draft}} == External Links == * [http://www.jingukaikan.jp/125mairi/m02/0203.html 高河原神社（たかがわらじんじゃ）] - 財団法人伊勢神宮崇敬会 {{125 Shrines of Ise}} {{translated page|ja|高河原神社|version=90499812|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Shrines in Mie Prefecture]] [[Category:Subordinate shrines of Toyouke Daijingu]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Japan]] [[Category:Ise Grand Shrine]] [[Category:Completion tier 5]] [[Category:125 Shrines of Ise]] [[Category:11]] [[Category:高河原神社]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Ise Province]] [[Category:Setsumatsusha]] [[Category:Shrines in Ise City]] }} [[ja:高河原神社]] [[sn:Takagawara Shrine]] [[sn:akagawara Shrine]]

{{Shrine |name = Takagawara Shrine |religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Takagawara-jinja 02.jpg|270px]] |location = {{ill|Ise, Mie|ja|伊勢市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Miyago 1-chome 3-19, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|ja|三重県|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |latitude_deg = 34 | latitude_min = 29 | latitude_sec = 34.5 |longitude_deg = 136 | longitude_min = 42 | longitude_sec = 22.2 |map = Japan Mie |deity = {{ill|Tsukuyomi|ja|月夜見尊御魂|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |Rank = {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (small)
{{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮|1=Toyouke Daijingu|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}} Subordinate Shrine |founded = Before {{ill|Enryaku|ja|延暦|qq=draft|qq=draft}} 23 (804) |main_hall = {{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|ja|神明造|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |other_names = |pilgrimage_sites = |annual_festival = |rituals = {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} }} Takagawara Shrine (高河原神社, ''Takagawara Jinja''Shikinen Sengu Memorial Sengu-kan "[http://www.sengukan.jp/wp-content/themes/sengukan/shrine/area06.php Takagawara Shrine たかがわらじんじゃ>>]" (Accessed October 8, 2013).[[iTV]] "[http://www.yoitokose.jp/ise/encyclopedia/t0010.php Takagawara Shrine | Ise Grand Shrine Encyclopedia | Ise-Shima Travel Yoitokose]" (Accessed October 8, 2013)., also pronounced ''Takakawara Jinja''Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.39Gakken Publishing (2013): p.57) is a [[Shinto]] shrine located in Miyago, {{ill|Ise, Mie|ja|伊勢市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|ja|三重県|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|subordinate shrine (sessha/massha)|ja|摂末社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} of {{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮|1=Toyouke Daijingu|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (the Outer Shrine of {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) and classified as a {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. It Ranks 10th among the 16 subordinate shrines of the Outer ShrineUjiyamada City Hall (1929): pp.11–13.. The shrine is located within the precincts of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|ja|月夜見宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, which is a separate shrine of the Outer ShrineIse Bunka-sha (2008): p.38. == Overview (概要) == Located at {{ill|Mie Prefecture|ja|三重県|qq=draft|qq=draft}} {{ill|Ise, Mie|ja|伊勢市|qq=draft|qq=draft}} 1006 Miyago 1-chome式内社研究会 編（1990）：294ページ (modern address: 1-3-19 Miyago, Ise City). The shrine is situated behind and to the right (northeast) of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月夜見宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'s main hall. The shrine grounds are surrounded by a moat on three sides, which is believed to be a remnant of a tributary of the {{ill|Miyagawa River (Mie)|ja|宮川 (三重県)|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. The enshrined deity is {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto no Mitama|ja|月夜見尊御魂|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (つきよみのみことのみたま). The shrine is located in Takagawara (高河原), an area near the Miyagawa River, and serves as a {{ill|guardian deity|ja|守護神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (守護神) for the land development of the surrounding region. Many ancient texts describe the enshrined deity as the Mitama (spirit) of {{ill|Tsukiyomi|ja|月読|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. However, thanks to the efforts of {{ill|Kawabe Kiyonaga|ja|河邊精長|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (also known as {{ill|Ōnakatomi Kiyonaga|ja|大中臣精長|qq=draft|qq=draft}}), the Grand Chief Priest ({{ill|Ōgūji|ja|大宮司|qq=draft|qq=draft}}), the shrine was reconstructed on its present site on {{ill|Kanbun (era)|ja|寛文|qq=draft|qq=draft}} 3, {{ill|July 7 (old calendar)|ja|7月7日 (旧暦)|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (corresponding to {{ill|August 9|ja|8月9日|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|1663|ja|1663rd year|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in the Gregorian calendar). * ''{{ill|Shinmei Hisho|ja|神名秘書|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'' states: "Located in Numaki-go, Yamada Village. East of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月読宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}." * ''{{ill|Ruiju Jingi Hongen|ja|類聚神祇本源|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'' states: "East of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月読宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, within the same {{ill|Tamagaki|ja|玉垣|qq=draft|qq=draft}} fence." * ''{{ill|Ninomiya Kansa Enkaku Kō|ja|二宮管社沿革考|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'' claims that the original shrine site was actually the present-day {{ill|Suhara Taisha|ja|須原大社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in Ichinoki, Ise City.Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p. 295 --- === Reconstruction in the Modern Period=== * In {{ill|1911|ja|1911th year|qq=draft|qq=draft}} ({{ill|Meiji|ja|明治|1=Meiji era|qq=draft|qq=draft}} 44), the shrine was rebuilt.Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): p. 12 * In {{ill|1938|ja|1938th year|qq=draft|qq=draft}} ({{ill|Shōwa|ja|昭和|qq=draft|qq=draft}} 13), it was rebuilt again. * In {{ill|1957|ja|1957th year|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Shōwa 32), a major renovation was completed, and a sacred transfer ritual ({{ill|Sengyo|ja|遷御|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) was performed 20 years later.Sakurai (1991): p. 298 --- == Rites and Festivals (祭事) == * February – {{ill|Kinen-sai (祈年祭)|ja|祈年祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Harvest Prayer Festival) * June & December – {{ill|Tsukinami-sai (月次祭)|ja|月次祭|1=Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Monthly Festival) * October – {{ill|Kannamesai (神嘗祭)|ja|神嘗祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Offering of First Fruits Festival) * November – {{ill|Niiname-sai (新嘗祭)|ja|新嘗祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Thanksgiving Harvest Festival) These four major rituals are conducted on-site by a Negi (禰宜, senior priest) in巡回祭典 (巡回祭,巡行 ceremony format). The following six rites are performed remotely (遥祀, Yōshi): * January – {{ill|Saitan-sai (歳旦祭)|ja|歳旦祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (New Year's Festival) * January – {{ill|Genshi-sai (元始祭)|ja|元始祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Imperial Foundation Festival) * February 11 – {{ill|Kenkoku-kinen-sai (建国記念祭)|ja|建国記念祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (National Foundation Day) * May & August – {{ill|Kaze-no-Hi-no-Matsuri (風日祈祭)|ja|風日祈祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Wind and Rain Prayers) * December 23 – {{ill|Tenchō-sai (天長祭)|ja|天長祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Emperor's Birthday Festival) --- == Access (交通) == [[File:Tsukiyominomiyamae Bus Stop.jpg|thumb|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya-mae Bus Stop]] Public Transport: * 10-minute walk (550m) from {{ill|Ise City Station|ja|伊勢市駅|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (JR & Kintetsu).Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p. 33 * 4-minute walk (360m) from Shindō Bus Stop (三重交通). {{Shrine |name = Takagawara Shrine |religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Takagawara-jinja 02.jpg|270px]] |location = {{ill|Ise, Mie|ja|伊勢市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Miyago 1-chome 3-19, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|ja|三重県|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |latitude_deg = 34 | latitude_min = 29 | latitude_sec = 34.5 |longitude_deg = 136 | longitude_min = 42 | longitude_sec = 22.2 |map = Japan Mie |deity = {{ill|Tsukuyomi|ja|月夜見尊御魂|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |Rank = {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (small)
{{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮|1=Toyouke Daijingu|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}} Subordinate Shrine |founded = Before {{ill|Enryaku|ja|延暦|qq=draft|qq=draft}} 23 (804) |main_hall = {{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|ja|神明造|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |other_names = |pilgrimage_sites = |annual_festival = |rituals = {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} }} Takagawara Shrine (高河原神社, ''Takagawara Jinja''Shikinen Sengu Memorial Sengu-kan "[http://www.sengukan.jp/wp-content/themes/sengukan/shrine/area06.php Takagawara Shrine たかがわらじんじゃ>>]" (Accessed October 8, 2013).[[iTV]] "[http://www.yoitokose.jp/ise/encyclopedia/t0010.php Takagawara Shrine | Ise Grand Shrine Encyclopedia | Ise-Shima Travel Yoitokose]" (Accessed October 8, 2013)., also pronounced ''Takakawara Jinja''Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.39Gakken Publishing (2013): p.57) is a [[Shinto]] shrine located in Miyago, {{ill|Ise, Mie|ja|伊勢市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|ja|三重県|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|subordinate shrine (sessha/massha)|ja|摂末社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} of {{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮|1=Toyouke Daijingu|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (the Outer Shrine of {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) and classified as a {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. It Ranks 10th among the 16 subordinate shrines of the Outer ShrineUjiyamada City Hall (1929): pp.11–13.. The shrine is located within the precincts of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|ja|月夜見宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, which is a separate shrine of the Outer ShrineIse Bunka-sha (2008): p.38. == Overview (概要) == Located at {{ill|Mie Prefecture|ja|三重県|qq=draft|qq=draft}} {{ill|Ise, Mie|ja|伊勢市|qq=draft|qq=draft}} 1006 Miyago 1-chome式内社研究会 編（1990）：294ページ (modern address: 1-3-19 Miyago, Ise City). The shrine is situated behind and to the right (northeast) of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月夜見宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'s main hall. The shrine grounds are surrounded by a moat on three sides, which is believed to be a remnant of a tributary of the {{ill|Miyagawa River (Mie)|ja|宮川 (三重県)|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. The enshrined deity is {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto no Mitama|ja|月夜見尊御魂|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (つきよみのみことのみたま). The shrine is located in Takagawara (高河原), an area near the Miyagawa River, and serves as a {{ill|guardian deity|ja|守護神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (守護神) for the land development of the surrounding region. Many ancient texts describe the enshrined deity as the Mitama (spirit) of {{ill|Tsukiyomi|ja|月読|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. However, the ''{{ill|Shinmei-chō Kōshō Saikō|ja|神名帳考證再考|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'' (''神名帳考證再考'') claims that the deity is actually {{ill|Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto|ja|倉稲魂命|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (倉稲魂命), the deity of grain and prosperity. nother text, ''{{ill|Ninomiya Kansa Enkaku Kō|ja|二宮管社沿革考|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'' (''二宮管社沿革考''), asserts that the original name of the shrine in the ''{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'' (延喜式神名帳) was "{{ill|Kawahara-ni-Masu-Kuninamino-Kami Jinja|ja|川原坐国生神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}", proving that its deity is {{ill|Kuninamino-Kami|ja|国生神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (国生神), the god of land formation.Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): pp. 295–296 The main hall follows {{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|ja|神明造|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (神明造, the {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}} architectural style) and has a wooden board roof ({{ill|Itabuki|ja|板葺|qq=draft|qq=draft}}), enclosed by a {{ill|Tamagaki|ja|玉垣|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (玉垣, sacred fence). Unlike most {{ill|Sessha|ja|摂社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}・{{ill|Massha|ja|末社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}・{{ill|Shokan-sha|ja|所管社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (摂社・末社・所管社, auxiliary shrines) of {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, which do not have an offering box ({{ill|Saisenbako|ja|賽銭箱|qq=draft|qq=draft}})Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p. 26, Takagawara Shrine uniquely has one. == History (歴史) == Based on the definition of a {{ill|Sessha|ja|摂社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (auxiliary shrine) within {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, this shrine was established before the compilation of the ''{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'' in {{ill|Enchō (era)|ja|延長|qq=draft|qq=draft}} 5 ({{ill|927|ja|927th year|qq=draft|qq=draft}}).Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p. 22 * The shrine is listed in that text as "{{ill|Kawahara-ni-Masu-Kuninamino-Kami Jinja|ja|川原坐国生神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}". * Additionally, it is mentioned as "{{ill|Takagawara-sha|ja|高河原社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}" in the ''{{ill|Toyuke Daijingu Gishiki-chō|ja|止由気宮儀式帳|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''. * Since that text dates back to {{ill|Enryaku (era)|ja|延暦|qq=draft|qq=draft}} 23 ({{ill|804|ja|804th year|qq=draft|qq=draft}}), this confirms that the shrine existed before that time.
